Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/ability-tracker.md

# Ability Tracker

Ability Tracker watches the cooldowns of a short list of your abilities and shares them with all your characters. Its main use is the OgreMCP window: a button that casts a tracked ability turns red and counts down its cooldown, based on whichever of your characters has the longest wait for it. It only runs while 'Enable Ability Tracker' is ticked on the Settings tab. To add an ability, click it in the Full Ability list and press Add, or double-click it. On the right, double-click a row to switch it off, or use the X to remove it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Click one to select it for the Add button below, or double-click it to add it to the Ability Tracker List straight away. | your abilities |
| **Ability Tracker List** | The abilities whose cooldowns are tracked, shown A to Z. Twice a second the bot reads how long each has left and shares it with your other characters, and the OgreMCP window shows it on matching buttons. Double-click a row to switch it off, X to remove.<br>*Needs 'Enable Ability Tracker' on the Settings tab.* | empty |

## Full Ability list (left)

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Search ... abilities** | Type to filter the ability list. Display only. |
| **Add** | Adds the ability you clicked in the list above to the Ability Tracker List. It is greyed out until you click one, and the name you picked is shown beside it. |

## Good to know

- Nothing happens until 'Enable Ability Tracker' is ticked on the Settings tab.
- An MCP button only lights up if its cast command names the ability without its rank, for example 'Kick' and not 'Kick VII'. The tracker matches on the plain name.
- Keep the list short. Every ability on it is checked twice a second and sent to your other characters.
- An ability this character does not have (not in its ability export) is skipped without a message.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/aliases.md

# Aliases

An alias is a nickname for one character, so your setup can say `*MainTank` instead of a real name. Type the alias and who it is for, then Add. The bot puts a star in front, so 'MainTank' becomes `*MainTank`, and you use that in a Cast Stack target or in a command's 'for who'. 'For' can be a character name or a class word (a class, subclass or archetype such as Fury or Priest). The bot checks you first, then your group, then your raid, and picks the first character that fits. Aliases only work while 'Enable Aliases' on the Settings tab is ticked.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Aliases** | Your aliases, in the order they are tried. Drag to reorder, double-click to switch one off, x to delete. The colour shows whether the alias is used on the Cast Stack and whether this row is the one that wins right now. | empty |

## Add an alias

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Alias (e.g. RaidMT)** | The nickname. The bot adds a star in front, so you use it as `*RaidMT`. | empty |
| **For (player / class / role)** | Who the alias means: a character name, or a class word such as a class, subclass or archetype. The first match wins: you, then your group, then your raid.<br>*An alias with an empty For never points at anyone.* | empty |
| **No-Raid** | Only look in your own group for this alias, never the rest of the raid. | off |
| **Add Alias** | Adds the alias to the end of the list. The same alias name can be added again with a different For, as a backup.<br>*An exact repeat (same alias, same For) is refused with a console message. Press Save to keep it.* |  |
| **Display Aliases** | Prints every alias, and the character each one points to right now, in the console. |  |
| **Team Groups…** | Opens the Team Groups window. A team group is one word (`*Team:Name`) that selects many characters and is shared by every session. |  |

## Good to know

- The alias list is drawn by its own code. Each row shows the alias, an arrow, and who it is for; NR means 'no raid'. Drag a row to reorder, double-click a row to switch it off, and the x deletes it (after a confirm).
- Several rows can share one alias name. The first row, from the top, that finds a character in your group or raid wins, so later rows are backups. Drag rows to choose which one is tried first.
- The name colour tells you two things. Green: used on the Cast Stack, and this row is the one the alias points to now. Yellow: used on the Cast Stack, but a different row (or nobody) wins right now. Orange: not used on the Cast Stack, but this row wins. Red: not used on the Cast Stack, and this row does not win.
- With 'Enable Aliases' (Settings tab) off, no alias resolves: every row shows yellow or red and a line above the list says so.
- Adding, removing or switching an alias off takes effect at once, but it is only kept if you press Save at the top.
- An alias picks ONE character. To aim at several characters with one word, use Team Groups (the button under the list) instead.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/announce.md

# Announce

Announce says something, or runs a command, whenever one of your abilities goes off. Each row is an ability, where to send it (Group, Raid, a tell to the target, an in-game command or a console command) and the text. In the text, *Target* becomes the name of whoever the ability was cast on and *Ability* becomes the ability's name. Nothing is announced unless 'Enable Announce Tab' on the Settings tab is ticked.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Click one to choose it for the next announce; its name appears next to the Add button. |  |
| **Announces** | Your announce rows, shown as ability, destination and text. Every switched-on row whose ability matches goes out, at any rank.<br>*Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off.* | empty |

## Announce

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Announce To** | Where the text goes. Group: group chat. Raid: raid chat. Tell To Target: a tell to whoever the ability was cast on. In-Game Command: runs the text as a game command, so it must start with /. Execute In Console: runs the text as a console command. | Group |
| **Text to announce** | What to say or run. *Target* becomes the target's name and *Ability* the ability's name.<br>*Case matters: *target* is not replaced, and the row is then skipped.* | empty |
| **Add** | Adds a row for the ability you clicked, with this destination and text. When you are editing a row it says Update and saves your changes to that row instead. |  |

## Good to know

- To add a row: click an ability in the Full Ability list (its name shows next to Add), pick 'Announce To', type the text, then press Add or Enter.
- Click a saved row to load it back into the form; the button then says Update, and Cancel leaves it unchanged. Double-click a row to switch it off, and the x removes it. The list is shown A to Z.
- Instant abilities announce when the bot casts them. Abilities with a cast time announce when they appear on your cast bar, which includes casts you make by hand.
- For a cast you made by hand the bot does not know the target, so a row that uses *Target* or 'Tell To Target' is skipped for it.
- *Target* and *Ability* must be typed exactly like that, with the capitals. A text that still contains them, or contains NULL or ${, is not sent.
- 'In-Game Command' text must start with / (for example `/shout *Ability* is up!`). 'Execute In Console' text must NOT start with /; it runs as a console command, for example an `oc` line.
- Group rows only go out while you are grouped, Raid rows only while you are in a raid.
- Only abilities are listed, not items.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/ascension.md

# Ascension

The Ascension tab has one option. Etherflash normally teleports you to your target when it lands. With 'Etherflash - Prevent Port' ticked, the bot targets you yourself just before the cast finishes, so the damage still lands but you do not move. About a second after the cast ends it lets go, and your normal target comes back.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Etherflash - Prevent Port** | When the bot casts Etherflash, it switches your target to yourself once the cast is over 90% done, so the teleport takes you nowhere. About a second after the cast ends, your normal target returns.<br>*Only for Etherflash casts made by the bot, any rank.* | off |

## Good to know

- It only works when the bot casts Etherflash (for example from the Cast Stack). If you press Etherflash yourself, nothing changes.
- If nothing else is choosing your target (no assist, no auto-target), the bot puts back the target you had before the cast.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/assist.md

# Assist

Assist tells the bot whose fight to join. Pick people (or aliases such as @Tank) from the dropdown and they go into the Assist order list. While the bot is running, it uses the FIRST person on the list who is in your group or raid and in your zone: it targets that player, so your attacks go at whatever they are fighting. With 'Direct Assist Targeting' on Settings ticked, it targets that player's target directly instead. Drag names to change the priority, double-click a name to switch it off, and click x to remove it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Choose whom to assist** | Pick a group or raid member, or an alias such as @Tank, to add them to the bottom of the Assist order list. The dropdown then resets; a name already on the list is not added twice.<br>*The choices are refreshed every time you open the dropdown.* | n/a (it adds a name, it stores nothing itself) |
| **Assist order — drag to set priority, double-click to disable** | The people to assist, in priority order. The bot uses the first one who is in your group or raid and in this zone, and ignores the rest until that person is gone.<br>*Disabled names stay in place (struck through) and are skipped.* | empty |

## Assist

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Drag a row** | Drag a row up or down to change who is assisted first. |
| **Double-click a row** | Switches that name off or back on. A switched-off name is struck through and skipped, but keeps its place. |
| **x (remove)** | Removes that name from the list. |

## Good to know

- The list is used whenever the bot is running and Auto Target is off, even if 'Auto Assist' on Settings is unticked. To stop assisting, disable or remove the names here.
- When 'Enable Auto Target' is ticked on the Auto Target tab, this list is ignored completely.
- An assist set by the `-assist` command takes priority over this list until it is turned off.
- Someone in your group but in another zone is skipped, and the next name down is used.
- Aliases are looked up each time, so @Tank follows whoever is your tank right now. An alias that points at nobody is skipped.
- Changes take effect straight away. Press Save at the top to keep them after a reload.
- Type `ogre assist` to see who the bot is assisting right now and why.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/auto-hunt.md

# Auto-Hunt (not finished)

> **:warning: Not finished**
>
> OgreBot marks this tab as not finished (its name is struck through). Some options below work and some do not yet - each one says which.

Auto-Hunt is a simple grinding mode. The bot looks for a mob near you, targets it and opens the fight with the first ready ability from your Pull Abilities list; your Cast Stack then fights as usual. This tab is marked not finished: the mob choice and safety settings work, but the walking part does not. The Auto Hunt and Movement Only boxes and the nav path list do nothing yet, so the bot never walks a route; it pulls what comes within the scan radius. To switch it on, use the OgreConsole command `-autohunt` with hunt, movement or off. It only runs while OgreBot is open with a profile loaded and the bot is not paused.

## Auto-Hunt

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto Hunt** | **Not active yet.** It will be the on/off switch for Auto-Hunt. For now, start and stop it with the OgreConsole command `-autohunt` (hunt, movement or off). | off |
| **Movement Only** | **Not active yet.** It will make Auto-Hunt walk without pulling. The command `-autohunt movement` exists, but for now it does not walk anywhere; it only holds you still while a safety check is tripped. | off |

## Auto Hunt Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Scan radius (box)** | How far around you the bot looks for a mob to pull, and for mobs attacking your group. Leave it blank to use 35. | empty (35 is used) |
| **Check Aggro** | While anyone in your group (or raid) is in combat, the bot stops pulling and holds still. Your normal combat settings handle the fight. | off |
| **Check HP @** | While anyone in your group (or raid) has less health than the % in the box beside it, the bot stops pulling and holds still.<br>*A group member who is not in the zone counts as low health. A blank box never stops the hunt.* | off |
| **Check HP @ (box)** | The health % used by Check HP @. Only used while Check HP @ is ticked. | empty (never stops the hunt) |
| **Check Mana @** | While anyone in your group (or raid) has less power than the % in the box beside it, the bot stops pulling and holds still. | off |
| **Check Mana @ (box)** | The power % used by Check Mana @. Only used while Check Mana @ is ticked. | empty (never stops the hunt) |
| **Check if any group members dead** | While anyone in your group (or raid) is dead, the bot stops pulling and holds still.<br>*A group member who is not in the zone also counts as dead, so the hunt waits for them to arrive.* | off |

## Ignore mobs by con

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Gray** | The bot never pulls gray-con mobs.<br>*A gray mob already attacking your group is still fought.* | off |
| **Green** | The bot never pulls green-con mobs. | off |
| **Blue** | The bot never pulls blue-con mobs. | off |
| **White (even)** | The bot never pulls white-con (even) mobs. | off |
| **Yellow** | The bot never pulls yellow-con mobs. | off |
| **Orange** | The bot never pulls orange-con mobs. | off |
| **Red** | The bot never pulls red-con mobs. | off |
| **Non-Aggro** | The bot only pulls mobs that would attack you on sight. Mobs that leave you alone are skipped. | off |
| **Named** | The bot never pulls named mobs.<br>*Even when unticked, normal mobs in range are pulled before named ones.* | off |

## Pull Abilities

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **First ready one is used; drag order = priority** | Your pull list. When the bot has a mob targeted and you are out of combat, it uses the first entry from the top that is ready. Type in the box above to find one of your abilities or items; picking it adds it. Drag rows to change the order, double-click a row to switch it off or on.<br>*With an empty list the bot targets mobs but never pulls them.* | empty |

## Behaviour

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Campspot** | When the bot finds a mob to pull, it sets a camp spot where you stand and holds you there for the fight. When no mob is left, it clears that camp spot again.<br>*It only sets and clears this character's own camp spot, not the group's.* | off |
| **CS-JO-JI** | Right now this does exactly the same as Campspot. | off |
| **Prebuff** | Before each pull, the bot targets you, turns auto-attack on and waits 3 seconds, so your normal buffs have time to go out. Then it targets the mob.<br>*It does not cast buffs itself; your Cast Stack does that.* | off |
| **Use IRC** | **Not active yet.**  | off |
| **Ignore Collision** | Normally the bot skips mobs it cannot see (a wall or hill in the way). Tick this to let it pull those too. | off |
| **Delay After Combat** | **Not active yet.**  | off |
| **Pause on Exquisite Chest drop** | While an Exquisite chest is lying within 50 of you, the bot stops pulling and holds still, so you can deal with it.<br>*It carries on by itself once the chest is gone.* | off |

## Nav Paths

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Add a nav point** | **Not active yet.** It will list named places in the zone to add to the route; for now the list is always empty.<br>*Opened, it says 'No named nav points yet - not built in the new bot'.* | empty |
| **Nav Path Order** | **Not active yet.** It will hold the route Auto-Hunt walks, in order. It is saved with your profile, but nothing uses it. | empty |
| **Clear** | Empties the Nav Path Order list. Press Save at the top to keep the change. |  |
| **Loop path** | **Not active yet.** It will make the route start over when it reaches the end. | off |

## Good to know

- Ticking Auto Hunt does not start anything. Use `-autohunt` in OgreConsole (hunt / movement / off). That choice is not saved with your profile, so Auto-Hunt starts off every time the bot is loaded fresh.
- A mob that is already attacking your group is targeted before any new pull, whatever its con. The con, Non-Aggro and Named filters only decide which NEW mob to pull. With 'Check Aggro' ticked the bot instead holds still and leaves that fight to your normal combat settings.
- 'Check if any group members dead' and 'Check HP @' also count a group member who is not in the zone. The hunt waits until they arrive.
- Pulls only happen while you are out of combat, and only if at least one entry in the pull list is ready to use. With an empty list the bot targets a mob and just waits.
- If the Scan radius box is blank, the bot looks 35 around you.
- Movement mode (`-autohunt movement`) does not walk anywhere yet and never pulls. The safety checks still apply in it: while one of them is tripped (Check Aggro, HP, Mana, dead members, Exquisite chest), the bot holds you still.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/cancel-on-cast.md

# Cancel On Cast

Some casts spoil a buff you keep up, so that buff needs to be cancelled and cast again fresh. Each row here says: when you cast THIS, cancel THESE buffs. The Cast Stack then puts them back. To build a row, click what you cast in list 1 and one or more buffs in list 2 (click a buff again to unpick it), then press Add. The row appears in Cancels setup, for example 'Armored -> Battle Tactics, Call of Shielding'. It only runs inside instances unless you tick the overland box. It waits while you are in combat, and it waits while the bot is paused.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **1. When you cast this  (ability or item)** | Pick the cast that should trigger the cancel. Abilities and items are both listed; items start with 'Item:'. Click one to select it. It is highlighted until you press Add. | your abilities and items |
| **2. ...cancel these  (pick several)** | Pick the buffs to cancel when that cast happens. Click as many as you like, and click one again to unpick it. Only buffs that last until cancelled are listed. | your until-cancelled buffs |
| **Cancels setup** | Your rows: the cast, then the buffs it cancels. After that cast, each buff still up is cancelled one at a time, once a second, until it is gone. Drag to reorder, double-click to switch a row off, X to remove.<br>*A 'C' on a row means it may cancel during combat. Tick 'In combat' beside Add when you make the row.* | empty |

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Also run in overland zones (by default this only runs inside instances)** | Lets the cancels happen in overland zones too. When unticked they only happen inside instances. | off |

## Build a row

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add** | Adds a row with your picks from lists 1 and 2 to Cancels setup. Tick 'In combat' beside it first to let that row cancel during a fight. It is greyed out until both lists have a pick (hover it to see which is missing). When several buffs are picked it reads 'Add (3)'. |

## Good to know

- While you are in combat the cancel is held until combat ends, however long the fight lasts. The 30-second limit below only starts counting once it is out of combat.
- Every cast the bot makes counts. A cast you make by hand counts only if it shows a cast bar, so an instant cast by hand is missed. Ranks do not matter: a row for 'Armored' fires on 'Armored IV' too.
- List 2 only shows buffs that last until cancelled. Timed buffs run out on their own, so they are left out.
- A buff on several people is cancelled once per second until it is gone everywhere. The bot gives up after 30 seconds or 12 tries (time held in combat does not count).
- Scripts can fire a row without casting anything: -CancelOnCast <who> "Armored" acts as if you had just cast Armored.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/chat-events.md

# Chat Events

Chat Events watches the game's incoming text for words you choose. When a line contains your text, the bot can run a console command, post a line to OgreConsole, play a 'Ding' sound, or any mix of the three. Nothing happens until you tick "Enable Chat Events" on the Settings tab. You build the events with the boxes at the top, and they appear in the Configured Events list below. Click a row to edit it, double-click it to switch it off or on, drag it to reorder, and use the X to delete it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Configured Events** | Your chat events. Each row shows the text it watches for, its command, and OC or Ding if ticked. Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off or on, drag a row to reorder, and click X to delete it.<br>*A switched-off row is kept but never fires. The order does not change anything; every active row is checked.* | empty |

## Add an event

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Text to watch for** | The text to look for in incoming game text. An event fires whenever a line contains this text, in any case.<br>*Required. An event with no text cannot be added.* | empty |
| **Code to execute (leave blank for nothing)** | A console command to run when the text is seen. It runs exactly as if you typed it into the InnerSpace console. Leave it blank if you only want the OC line or the Ding. | empty |
| **OC - on success, send a message to OgreConsole** | When the text is seen, a line goes to OgreConsole saying which character saw it, the text it matched and the full line. | off |
| **Ding - on success, play a 'Ding'** | When the text is seen, a 'Ding' sound plays on this PC. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the event to the list below. Pressing Enter in either text box does the same. While you are editing a row this button reads Update and saves your changes to that row. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks OC and Ding. Ticks otherwise carry over to the next event you add. |  |
| **Cancel** | Only shown while editing a row. Stops editing without changing the row. |  |

## Good to know

- Nothing here works until "Enable Chat Events" is ticked on the Settings tab.
- The match ignores upper and lower case and can be anywhere in the line. Short text like "a" or "the" matches almost every line.
- An event with no command, no OC and no Ding is ignored, and the console prints a warning about it.
- The OC and Ding ticks stay ticked for the next event you add. Use Clear Options to untick them.
- Changes take effect within about a second. Press Save at the top to keep them for next time.
- Chat Events keep working while OgreBot is paused.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/codex-inspect.md

# Codex Inspect

Codex Inspect uploads the gear of the people in your group or raid to the EQ2Codex.com website, so you can see it there. You need an EQ2Codex API token first: press Setup API Token and paste the one from your eq2codex.com account. Opening the tab fills the left list (Roster) with your raid, or your group, or just you when solo. Each name shows how long until it can be inspected again, or 'ready'. Double-click names to move them into the right list (To Inspect), or press Queue All, then press Inspect Queued Now. The bot inspects each name in turn and uploads it. Names that upload leave the right list; names that fail stay there in red, marked FAIL.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Refresh from Group/Raid** | Reads your raid or group again and redraws the Roster. Opening the tab does this too. |  |
| **Roster (double-click to queue)** | Everyone in your raid, or your group, or just you when solo. Each name shows '(cd: ...)' with the time until it can be inspected again, or 'ready'. Double-click a name to add it to the To Inspect list.<br>*A name already in the To Inspect list is not added twice.* | empty until the tab is opened |
| **Queue All** | Adds every name in the Roster to the To Inspect list. |  |
| **To Inspect (double-click to remove)** | The names waiting to be inspected and uploaded. Double-click a name to take it out. Names leave on their own as they upload; failed ones stay in red, marked FAIL. | empty |
| **Clear Queue** | Empties the To Inspect list. It does not stop a run that has already started. |  |
| **Inspect Queued Now** | Starts a run: the bot inspects each name in the To Inspect list, one about every 3 seconds, and uploads their gear to eq2codex.com.<br>*Greyed out while a run is going. Names inspected in the last 5 minutes are skipped.* |  |
| **Reset Raid Force** | Clears your active group/raid on the eq2codex.com website, including the gear and adornments uploaded for it. Nothing on your PC changes.<br>*Greyed out while a run is going.* |  |

## Top of tab

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Visit EQ2Codex.com** | Opens eq2codex.com in your web browser. |
| **Wiki** | Opens the EQ2Codex help pages in your web browser. |
| **Setup API Token** | Opens the EQ2Codex API Token window, where you paste your token from eq2codex.com. The token is kept on this PC, outside your profile, and is never shown back to you.<br>*The same window opens from the Codex Toons tab. One token serves both.* |
| **View my Group/Raid** | Opens your active group/raid page on eq2codex.com in your web browser. |

## Good to know

- Nothing uploads until an API token is saved with Setup API Token. The line under the buttons says 'NOT configured' until then.
- A name inspected in the last 5 minutes is skipped. The Roster shows the time left for each name.
- The bot waits about 3 seconds between people, so a full raid takes a few minutes. Inspect Queued Now and Reset Raid Force are greyed out while a run is going.
- The inspect window pops open and closes for each person. That is normal.
- A FAIL row stays in the To Inspect list so you can see who failed. Press Inspect Queued Now again to retry them, or double-click to remove them.
- A '409' failure in the console means another uploader's account has already claimed that character.
- The To Inspect list is not saved in your profile. Closing OgreBot with its X stops a run in progress; the names not yet done stay in the list for next time you open it, until the bot is unloaded.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/codex-toons.md

# Codex Toons

Codex Toons uploads a snapshot of your own character (gear and stats) to the EQ2Codex.com website. Press Setup API Token once to paste your token from eq2codex.com, then press Upload My Toon Snapshot whenever you want your page updated. The result, good or bad, is posted in OgreConsole. You can also have it upload by itself every time the bot camps you out. For your group or raid members, use the Codex Inspect tab instead.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Visit EQ2Codex.com** | Opens eq2codex.com in your web browser. |  |
| **Wiki** | Opens the EQ2Codex help pages in your web browser. |  |
| **Setup API Token** | Opens the EQ2Codex API Token window, where you paste your token from eq2codex.com. The token is kept on this PC, outside your profile, and is never shown back to you.<br>*Same window and same token as on the Codex Inspect tab.* |  |
| **Upload My Toon Snapshot** | Inspects your own character and uploads your gear and stats to eq2codex.com. OgreConsole reports whether it worked. |  |
| **(idle)** | The upload status: whether a token is set, and whether an upload is running. | (idle) |
| **View My Characters** | Opens your characters page on eq2codex.com in your web browser. |  |
| **View My Group/Raids** | Opens your saved groups and raids on eq2codex.com in your web browser. |  |
| **Auto-upload my toon snapshot to Codex when I camp (-camp / logout)** | When the bot camps you out, it first starts an upload of your toon snapshot. The camp does not wait for the upload.<br>*Only camps done by the bot count, not a /camp you type yourself.* | off |

## Good to know

- Nothing uploads until an API token is saved with Setup API Token. The same token is used by Codex Inspect.
- You must be in the world. The inspect window pops open on yourself for a moment while the bot reads your gear.
- If another upload is already running (for example a Codex Inspect run), the snapshot is refused and OgreConsole says so. Try again when it is done.
- The auto-upload on camp only happens when the bot does the camping (for example the camp command, or the Instance Controller's end-of-list camp). Typing /camp yourself does not upload.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/consume-items.md

# Consume Items

Consume Items keeps you using items such as potions and temporary buffs. While the bot is running and 'Enable Consume Items' is ticked on the Settings tab, it checks the list about once a second. It uses the first item that is in your bags and ready, then waits before using that item again for as long as its effect lasts (10 minutes if the bot cannot read the duration). The list order is the priority. By default it only works inside instances; the two boxes at the top also allow guild halls and overland zones. To build the list, click an item in the Full Item List (your registered items from the Items tab), tick 'In-combat' if it should only be used in combat, and press Add. On the Consume Item List, drag rows to change the order, click a row to edit it, double-click a row to switch it off or on, and use the x to remove it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Item List** | Your registered items from the Items tab. Click one to pick it for the Add form, or double-click it to add it straight away with no options. | your registered items |
| **Consume Item List** | The items the bot uses, in priority order: each check it uses the first one that is in your bags, ready, and not waiting out its effect. 'IC' on a row means in combat only.<br>*Drag to reorder, click to edit, double-click to switch off or on, x to remove.* | empty |

## Where it works

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Allow in Guild Halls** | Lets the list be used automatically in a guild hall. Without it, nothing is used there. | off |
| **Allow in Overland zones** | Lets the list be used automatically outside instances, in overland and city zones. Without it, items are only used inside instances. | off |

## Item lists

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **In-combat** | The item being added is only used while you are in combat. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the item picked on the left to the end of the list, with the In-combat option as ticked. When you are editing a row, it reads Update and saves your change. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks In-combat. It otherwise stays ticked for the next Add. |  |

## Good to know

- Nothing happens unless 'Enable Consume Items' is ticked on the Settings tab. Pausing the bot also stops it.
- The Full Item List only shows items registered on the Items tab. If it is empty, register your consumables there first.
- Double-clicking an item on the left adds it straight away, without the In-combat option. To set it, click once, tick In-combat, then press Add.
- Nothing is used while you are moving or dead. In combat, the bot waits at least 5 seconds between uses.
- The wait for each item's effect is kept only while the session runs. After a reload the bot may use an item again straight away.
- The OgreConsole command `-ConsumeItems_ProcessList_AP` runs the list on demand (add `-all` to use every eligible item, not just the first). It ignores the zone boxes and the pause, but still needs 'Enable Consume Items'.
- To see what it picks and when, tick ConsumeItemsDebug on the Debug tab.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/crowd-control.md

# Crowd Control (not finished)

> **:warning: Not finished**
>
> OgreBot marks this tab as not finished (its name is struck through). Some options below work and some do not yet - each one says which.

Crowd Control is not active yet in the new bot. Its settings are saved with your profile, but nothing uses them, which is why the tab is struck through in the tab list. When it is built, the bot will mez (or root) extra mobs that are attacking your group, using the abilities in the Priority Order list, top first, and leaving the mob you are killing alone.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | Your abilities, with a search box. Click one and press Add (or double-click it) to put it in the Priority Order list. | filled from your ability export |
| **Priority Order** | **Not active yet.** It will be the mez abilities to use, top first.<br>*Drag to reorder, double-click to switch a row off, x to remove. Clicking a row loads it back into the form.* | empty |

## Crowd Control

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Allow Epics as Valid Targets** | **Not active yet.** It will let the bot mez epic mobs as well as ordinary ones. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the ability you clicked on the left to the bottom of the Priority Order list. Next to it you see the picked ability, or 'click an ability on the left' until you pick one. |  |

## Good to know

- Nothing on this tab does anything yet, and neither does 'Enable Crowd Control' on Settings.
- You can still set up the list now: it is saved with your profile and will be used once the feature is built.

# Despawn Event

Despawn Event is the opposite of Spawn Events: it fires when something whose name contains your text disappears. The bot can then run a console command, post a line to OgreConsole, play a 'Ding' sound, or any mix of the three. Nothing happens until you tick "Enable Despawn Event" on the Settings tab. Build events with the boxes at the top; they appear in the Configured Events list below.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Configured Events** | Your despawn events. Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off or on, drag a row to reorder, and click X to delete it.<br>*A switched-off row is kept but never fires.* | empty |

## Add an event

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Actor to watch for** | Part or all of the name to watch for. The event fires when something with a matching name disappears. Upper and lower case must match exactly.<br>*Required. An event with no name cannot be added.* | empty |
| **Code to execute (leave blank for nothing)** | A console command to run when a match disappears. It runs exactly as if you typed it into the InnerSpace console. Leave it blank if you only want the OC line or the Ding. | empty |
| **OC - on success, send a message to OgreConsole** | When a match disappears, a line goes to OgreConsole saying which character saw it, the text it matched and the full name. | off |
| **Ding - on success, play a 'Ding'** | When a match disappears, a 'Ding' sound plays on this PC. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the event to the list below. Pressing Enter in either text box does the same. While you are editing a row this button reads Update and saves your changes to that row. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks OC and Ding. Ticks otherwise carry over to the next event you add. |  |
| **Cancel** | Only shown while editing a row. Stops editing without changing the row. |  |

## Good to know

- Nothing here works until "Enable Despawn Event" is ticked on the Settings tab.
- The name match is case-sensitive: "vindicator" does not match "a Vindicator". Part of the name is enough.
- Something leaving your view can count as disappearing, not only a mob that dies or despawns.
- An event with no command, no OC and no Ding is ignored, and the console prints a warning about it.
- The OC and Ding ticks stay ticked for the next event you add. Use Clear Options to untick them.
- Despawn events keep working while OgreBot is paused.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/equipment-info.md

# Equipment Info

Equipment Info stores two charm choices so you can swap between them quickly. Pick an item in each drop-down (the choices are your registered items from the Items tab), then press Equip Charm 1 or Equip Charm 2. The bot looks for that item in your bags and asks the game to equip it. The buttons only affect this character. Scripts and OgreConsole can also run the same swap for other characters.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Charm Option 1:** | The item that 'Equip Charm 1' puts on. The list shows your registered items from the Items tab. | empty |
| **Charm Option 2:** | The item that 'Equip Charm 2' puts on. The list shows your registered items from the Items tab. | empty |
| **Equip Charm 1** | Finds the Charm Option 1 item in your bags and asks the game to equip it, on this character only.<br>*Does nothing but print a message if Charm Option 1 is empty or the item is not in your bags.* |  |
| **Equip Charm 2** | Finds the Charm Option 2 item in your bags and asks the game to equip it, on this character only.<br>*Does nothing but print a message if Charm Option 2 is empty or the item is not in your bags.* |  |

## Good to know

- The drop-downs are empty until you register items on the Items tab. They list every registered item, not only charms.
- The item must be in your bags (not the bank, and not already equipped). If it is not found, the console says so.
- The game can still refuse the swap, for example because of relic limits. The console line only says the bot asked.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/ho-excludes.md

# HO Excludes

HO Excludes lists abilities the bot must never use to work a Heroic Opportunity. When the bot picks an ability to match an HO icon, for the HO Starter or HO Wheel steps on the Settings tab or when a script asks for an HO icon ability, it skips anything on this list and uses another ability with that icon. Your normal Cast Stack rotation is not affected. Double-click an ability in the Full Ability list to add it. On the right, double-click a row to switch it off, or use the X to remove it. Changes apply straight away.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Double-click one to add it to the exclude list. An ability that is already listed is not added twice. | your abilities |
| **Abilities to Exclude in HOs** | The abilities the bot will not pick for HO Starter or HO Wheel icons, shown A to Z. Double-click a row to switch it off (it is then used again), X to remove. | empty |

## Full Ability list (left)

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Search ... abilities** | Type to filter the ability list. Display only. |

## Good to know

- The rank does not matter: excluding 'Assault' also excludes 'Assault XIII', and the other way round. The match is still the exact ability line, so 'Assault' does not exclude 'Taunting Assault'.
- It does not affect the ability that opens an HO (the HO Start step). It only affects the abilities that match starter and wheel icons.
- To keep an ability out of your normal rotation as well, use the Cast Stack or the 'Disable HO' boxes on the Settings tab.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/huds.md

# HUDs

HUDs puts live text straight onto your game screen: the nearest mob, the nearest other player, how far each group or raid member is, and timed messages from encounter scripts. The text sits on a see-through layer over the whole game window. It has no title bar, you cannot click or drag it, and your mouse clicks go through it to the game. Each block is placed by its X and Y boxes, counted in screen pixels from the top-left corner. Changes take effect as soon as you make them. The layer appears when you tick any of the Display boxes (or when an encounter puts up a Raid Options message) and closes when OgreBot closes. The last section sets up the OSA (On-Screen Assistant), which is a separate window of its own.

## Nearest NPC

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Display nearest NamedNPC/NPC** | Shows one line on your screen with the closest mob within 200 metres and its distance. A named mob always wins over a normal one, even if the normal one is closer. | off |
| **X** | How far from the left edge of the screen the Nearest NPC line starts, in pixels. | blank (300) |
| **Y** | How far down from the top of the screen the Nearest NPC line sits, in pixels. | blank (400) |

## Nearest PC

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Display nearest PC** | Shows one line with the closest player within 200 metres who is not in your group or raid. The line is red under 30 metres, yellow under 150 and white further out. | off |
| **X** | How far from the left edge of the screen the Nearest PC line starts, in pixels. | blank (300) |
| **Y** | How far down from the top of the screen the Nearest PC line sits, in pixels. | blank (380) |
| **Msg alerts to OgreConsole** | When a player comes within 150 metres, and again within 30, a line such as 'Kannkor --> Nearest PC: Serath: 24.1 < 30' is posted to OgreConsole. Each player is reported once per distance band, and alerts are at least 5 seconds apart.<br>*Needs 'Display nearest PC' ticked.* | off |
| **Ding alerts** | Plays a short ding when a player comes within 30 metres. If 'Msg alerts' is also ticked, it dings at 150 metres too. A ding under 30 metres also posts the OgreConsole line, even without 'Msg alerts'.<br>*Needs 'Display nearest PC' ticked.* | off |
| **Loud alarm when close** | When a player comes within 30 metres, plays a louder two-tone alarm instead of the short ding.<br>*Does nothing on its own. 'Msg alerts' or 'Ding alerts' must also be ticked.* | off |

## Group Distance

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Display group distance** | Shows a line for each other group member: their slot number, name, distance, their target and what they are casting. The colour shows distance: white close, then yellow, orange and red further out.<br>*In a raid with 'Display raid distance' ticked, the raid lines replace these.* | off |
| **X** | How far from the left edge of the screen the group lines start, in pixels. | blank (300) |
| **Y** | How far down from the top of the screen the first group line sits, in pixels. | blank (420) |
| **Line spacing** | How many pixels apart the group lines are. | blank (12) |

## Raid Distance

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Display raid distance** | In a raid, shows one line per raid slot (01 to 24) with the same details as the group lines. Empty slots stay blank so every line matches the raid window. Outside a raid it shows your group instead. | off |
| **X** | How far from the left edge of the screen the raid lines start, in pixels. Scan Raid Window fills this in. | blank (300) |
| **Y** | How far down the screen raid slot 1's line sits, in pixels. Scan Raid Window fills this in. | blank (420) |
| **Line spacing** | How many pixels apart the lines within one raid group are. Scan Raid Window fills this in from the raid window's own row height. | blank (12) |
| **Group gap** | Extra pixels added after slots 6, 12 and 18, so each raid group lines up with its block in the raid window. | blank (6) |
| **Scan Raid Window** | Reads where your raid window is on screen and fills in the four boxes above. The raid lines are placed right beside it (on the left if there is no room on the right). The HUD moves straight away.<br>*Open the raid window first. If it cannot read the window you get 'Scan failed - see console'. Press Save to keep the numbers.* |  |
| **Hide names** | Leaves the slot number and name off each line, so it shows only the distance, target and cast. Applies to the group lines too. | off |
| **Hide casting** | Leaves off the 'what they are casting' part of each line. Applies to the group lines too. | off |

## Raid Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show 5 demo lines** | Puts 5 test lines with a 10-second countdown on screen so you can see where Raid Options messages appear. They disappear after 15 seconds. |  |
| **X** | How far from the left edge of the screen the Raid Options messages start, in pixels. | blank (300) |
| **Y** | How far down from the top of the screen the first Raid Options message sits, in pixels. | blank (300) |
| **Line spacing** | How many pixels apart the Raid Options messages are. | blank (15) |

## OSA - NPC On-Screen-Assistant

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Scan Radius** | How far out, in metres, the OSA window looks for mobs. Anything over 200 counts as 200.<br>*Only used while the OSA is turned on. The box and the slider always show the same number.* | blank (50) |
| **Scan Radius (slider)** | The same scan radius as the box beside it, as a slider from 0 to 149. Moving one updates the other. | not set (the OSA uses 50) |
| **Display NPCs with Targets Only** | The OSA window only lists mobs that have a target, meaning mobs that are fighting someone. Idle mobs are hidden. | off |
| **Clip Y Axis (only show mobs on the same floor as you)** | The OSA window hides mobs that are 8 or more above or below you, so the floors over and under you drop out of the list.<br>*Only used while the OSA is turned on.* | off |

## What you see

- Nearest NPC - one white line: 'Named NPC: <name>: <distance>' for the closest named mob within 200 metres, or 'NPC: <name>: <distance>' when no named mob is in range.
- Nearest PC - one line: 'Nearest PC: <name>: <distance>' for the closest player within 200 metres who is not in your group or raid. It is red under 30 metres, yellow under 150 and white further out.
- Group distance - one line per group member (you are not listed): '(2) Brutus: 12.3 * <their target> * <what they are casting>'. Names are cut to their first 6 letters so the columns line up.
- Raid distance - one line per raid slot, '(01)' to '(24)', in the same layout as the group lines. An empty slot leaves a blank line and there is an extra gap after every 6 slots, so each line sits beside the matching row of the game's raid window.
- Group and raid line colours show distance: white under 20 metres, yellow under 30, orange under 75, red at 75 or more, grey when the game reports 0.
- The 'what they are casting' part shows the spell name for members running the new bot. For anyone else it just says 'casting'.
- Raid Options - up to 10 lines written by encounter files and scripts, usually a message with a countdown in seconds (for example 'Adds incoming: 12.4'). Each line disappears 5 seconds after its countdown ends.
- All HUD text is white-on-dark-outline monospace text so it stays readable on bright backgrounds. It refreshes about three times a second.

## Good to know

- The HUD layer has no title bar and ignores the mouse, so you cannot move it by dragging. Use the X and Y boxes to move each block.
- With 'Display raid distance' ticked and no raid, you see your group instead. So you do not need both boxes ticked. In a raid, the raid lines replace the group lines.
- The alert boxes only work while 'Display nearest PC' is ticked, and 'Loud alarm when close' does nothing unless 'Msg alerts' or 'Ding alerts' is also ticked.
- Scan Raid Window fills in the four Raid Distance boxes, but you still have to press Save to keep them.
- Emptying a position box does not move the block to 0,0. The block stays where it was, even after the profile is loaded again. It only goes back to its default position after the game client is restarted.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/invis-abilities.md

# Invis Abilities

Invis Abilities lists the stealth abilities the bot may use to open a Cast Stack ability that only works while you are hidden (for example a scout attack from stealth). When such an entry comes up in the Cast Stack and you are not hidden, the bot first casts the first ready ability from the Invis Cast List, then fires the stealth ability straight after it, holding the cast bar so nothing else slips in between. The left list shows only this character's abilities that grant stealth, with a search box; double-click one to add it to the right-hand list.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Invis Abilities for Combat Arts** | Your abilities that grant stealth. Type in the search box to narrow it, and double-click an ability to add it to the Invis Cast List.<br>*An ability already on the right-hand list is not added twice.* | filled from your ability export |
| **Invis Cast List** | The stealth openers to try, in order. Before a Cast Stack ability that needs stealth, the bot casts the first one here that is ready.<br>*Switched-off rows are skipped.* | empty |

## Invis Abilities

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Drag a row** | Drag a row up or down to change which opener is tried first. |
| **Double-click a row** | Switches that ability off or back on. A switched-off row is struck through and never used. |
| **x (remove)** | Removes that ability from the list. |

## Good to know

- If no ability on the Invis Cast List is ready, a Cast Stack entry that needs stealth is simply skipped until one is.
- Order matters: the first ready ability in the Invis Cast List is used. Drag to reorder.
- An ability here that itself needs stealth can never open anything. The bot skips it and prints a warning in the console once.
- Some class abilities let certain stealth attacks fire without being hidden; in that case no opener is cast.
- If the left list is empty for a class that has stealth, run the ability export again.
- Changes take effect straight away. Press Save at the top to keep them after a reload.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/item-embargo.md

# Item Embargo (not finished)

> **:warning: Not finished**
>
> OgreBot marks this tab as not finished (its name is struck through). Some options below work and some do not yet - each one says which.

Item Embargo is meant to stop your characters all using the same item at once: when one uses a listed item, the others hold off for the set time. In the new bot this tab is not active yet. You can build and save the list, but nothing reads it, so it has no effect. How the screen works: the Full Item list on the left shows your registered items (from the Items tab). Click one to pick it, set a Duration and the option flags under the right-hand list, then press Add. Double-clicking an item adds it straight away with no options. On the right-hand list, click a row to edit it (Add becomes Update, with a Cancel), double-click a row to switch it off or on, drag rows to reorder them, and use the x to remove one.

## Item Embargo

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Item list** | **Not active yet.** Your registered items (from the Items tab). Click one to pick it for the form on the right, or double-click it to add it straight away with no options.<br>*This tab is not active yet in the new bot.* | your registered items |

## Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Globally Mute messages** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to stop item embargo messages being shown. | off |
| **Item Embargo List** | **Not active yet.** The saved list of items that are meant to be embargoed, each with its duration and options.<br>*Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off or on, drag to reorder, x to remove.* | empty |

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Item name** | The item to add. Type part of a name to get suggestions from your registered items, or click an item in the Full Item list. | empty |
| **Duration** | How many seconds the other characters are meant to hold off after the item is used. | empty |
| **IRC** | Meant to announce the embargo over IRC. | off |
| **Group** | Meant to limit the embargo to group members. | off |
| **Me** | Meant to limit the embargo to this character. | off |
| **Incl. caster** | Meant to include the character who used the item, and the item's name, in the embargo. | off |
| **Hide from OgreConsole** | Meant to send the embargo without showing it in OgreConsole. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the picked item with its Duration and ticked options to the list. When you are editing a row, it reads Update and saves your changes. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks all the option boxes. They otherwise carry over to the next Add. |  |

## Good to know

- Nothing on this tab does anything yet in the new bot, and neither does 'Enable Item Embargo' on the Settings tab.
- The Full Item list only shows items you have registered on the Items tab. If it is empty, register some there first.
- The option flags stay ticked after an Add. Use Clear Options to untick them all before the next item.
- On the list each row shows its options as coloured letters: IRC, G (Group), Me, I (Incl. caster) and H (Hide from OgreConsole). The same colour is used on the matching tick box.

# Items

Items is where you register the items the rest of OgreBot can offer you. The left list, All Item List, shows everything you have equipped and everything in your bags. It is filled when your profile loads; press Refresh list after looting or changing gear. It also has a search box. Double-click an item to register it: it moves into the right list, 'Items to include in ability lists', and gets a green '✓ registered' mark on the left. Only registered items appear in the item pickers on other tabs: the Cast Stack, Consume Items, Item Embargo, Pre-Cast and Post-Cast, the Equipment Info charm choices and the Auto-Hunt pull list. Click the x on a right-hand row to unregister it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **All Item List** | Everything you have equipped, everything in your bags, 'whatever is in slot X' entries and your equipped adornments. Double-click an item to register it.<br>*Items already registered show a green '✓ registered' mark and cannot be added twice.* | filled when your profile loads |
| **Items to include in ability lists** | Your registered items. These are the items the item pickers on the Cast Stack, Consume Items, Item Embargo, Pre/Post-Cast, Equipment Info and Auto-Hunt tabs offer. | empty |

## Items

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Refresh list** | Reads your equipment and bags again and refreshes the All Item List. Use it after looting or changing gear. |  |
| **Search N items...** | Type part of a name to show only the matching items in the All Item List. It only filters what you see. | empty |
| **Double-click an item (left list)** | Registers that item, adding it to 'Items to include in ability lists'. The change is saved straight away. |  |
| **x (remove row)** | Unregisters that item. It stops appearing in the other tabs' pickers. |  |

## Good to know

- If the Item List on Consume Items or Item Embargo, or a charm drop-down on Equipment Info, is empty, you have not registered any items here yet.
- Registering does not make the bot use an item. It only makes the item appear in the other tabs' pickers.
- The left list has special entries. '_EQUIPPED_<slot>_<number>' means 'whatever is in that slot', so you can use a charm slot without naming a specific charm. '_ADORN_<name>' is an adornment you have equipped.
- Right after a profile loads, the adornment entries can take a few seconds to appear. The bot scans again by itself once they are ready.
- Unregistering an item does not remove it from Cast Stack or Consume Items entries you already made.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/load.md

# Load

Load holds things the bot does every time it loads your profile. The left side sets a few game options: the radar, the game's Player Combat Auto Face option, and your group loot rules. Ticking one of those boxes also applies it right away. The right side is a list of commands the bot runs, in order, each time it loads.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Radar on** | Opens the OgreBot radar window when the profile loads, and right away when you tick it.<br>*You can tick Radar on or Radar off, not both.* | off |
| **Radar off** | Closes the OgreBot radar window when the profile loads, and right away when you tick it. | off |
| **Player Combat Auto Face  (recommended for TANKS)** | Turns ON the game's 'Player Combat Auto Face' option when the profile loads, and right away when you tick it. Your character then turns to face what it is fighting.<br>*Tick this one or the DISABLED one below, not both.* | off |
| **Player Combat Auto Face DISABLED  (recommended for NON-TANKS)** | Turns OFF the game's 'Player Combat Auto Face' option when the profile loads, and right away when you tick it. | off |
| **Set loot options (applies the three below on load)** | Applies the three loot dropdowns below when the profile loads, and right away when you tick it. As group leader the bot opens the game's Group Options window, sets them and clicks Apply. If you are not the leader, only the auto-loot mode is set.<br>*A dropdown left on 'Select...' is not changed.* | off |
| **Loot method (group leader only)** | The group loot method to set: Leader Only, Free For All, Lotto, Need Before Greed or Round Robin. Only used by 'Set loot options', and only when you lead the group. | not set (left alone) |
| **Loot rarity (group leader only)** | The lowest item rarity the group loot rules apply to: All, Treasured+, Legendary+ or Fabled+. Only used by 'Set loot options', and only when you lead the group. | not set (left alone) |
| **Auto-loot mode (everyone)** | Your own auto-loot choice: None, Auto-Greed or Auto-Decline. Used by 'Set loot options', whether or not you lead the group. | not set (left alone) |
| **Executes** | Commands the bot runs, top to bottom, every time it loads your profile. Switched-off lines are skipped.<br>*Double-click a line to switch it off or on. Drag to reorder.* | empty |
| **Button test** | **Not active yet.**  | empty |

## Executes

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Command to run on load** | Type a console command here. Put `eq2execute` in front of an in-game slash command. Press Enter or Add to put it on the list.<br>*Commas and ] are removed when you add the line.* | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed command to the end of the list and runs it once straight away, so you can see it works. |  |

## Good to know

- The Executes list takes console commands. To run an in-game slash command, start the line with `eq2execute`, for example `eq2execute /join_channel MyChannel`.
- A command you add is run once straight away, so a typo shows up right then.
- Commas and ] are removed from a command when you add it. A line that needs them will not run as typed.
- Changing one of the three loot dropdowns does nothing by itself. It is used the next time the profile loads, or when you tick 'Set loot options' again.
- Double-click a command to switch it off without deleting it. Drag a row to change the order. The x removes it.
