Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/loot.md

# Loot

Loot decides what the bot does when a loot window opens. Nothing on the left half works unless 'Accept Loot' is ticked on the Settings tab. Each window type has its own block: Free For All (solo boxes and FFA groups), Lottery, Need Before Greed, and Leader Only (you are the loot master). Leader Only is where Smart Loot and Loot Distribution hand items to group members; anything they do not claim goes to the plain 'loot this kind of item' boxes. The right half holds options that apply on their own, plus the Auto-Loot list: type an exact item name in the box under it and press Add (or Enter), and the item is always taken from Free For All and Leader Only windows. Each row has an x to remove it.

## FFA Loot Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Accept any tradable** | The bot handles Free For All loot windows. It takes every tradable item, plus anything on the Auto-Loot list. No-Trade and Heirloom items are left behind unless 'Loot everything' is ticked.<br>*With this off, Free For All windows are ignored completely.* | off |
| **Loot everything** | In Free For All windows the bot takes every item, No-Trade and Heirloom included.<br>*Needs 'Accept any tradable' ticked too.* | off |

## Lotto Loot Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Accept All (including No-Trade)** | When a Lottery loot window opens, the bot enters the roll for everything in it.<br>*If both Lotto boxes are ticked, this one wins.* | off |
| **Decline all** | When a Lottery loot window opens, the bot declines the roll. | off |

## NBG Loot Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Need All (including No-Trade)** | When a Need Before Greed window opens, the bot picks Need.<br>*If several NBG boxes are ticked, Need wins, then Greed, then Decline.* | off |
| **Greed All (including No-Trade)** | When a Need Before Greed window opens, the bot picks Greed. | off |
| **Decline all** | When a Need Before Greed window opens, the bot declines it. | off |

## Leader Only Loot Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Enable options below** | The bot handles Leader Only loot windows using the boxes below. With it off, Leader Only windows are left for you. | off |
| **Loot Adepts** | The bot takes items with '(Adept)' in the name. | off |
| **Loot Masters** | The bot takes items with '(Master)' in the name. | off |
| **Loot Ancients** | The bot takes items with '(Ancient)' in the name. | off |
| **Loot Illegible Scrolls** | The bot takes items whose name contains 'Illegible Scroll:'. | off |
| **Loot Tradables** | The bot takes every item that is neither No-Trade nor Heirloom. A few names are always skipped: 'CD Armor:', 'CD Armor Voucher:' and 'Living Embodiment of Shadow'. | off |
| **Loot everything** | The bot takes every item in the window. Once it has finished with the window, it closes it, even if something was left behind.<br>*Smart Loot and Loot Distribution still get first pick of each item.* | off |
| **Smart Loot** | Before anything else, the bot gives each item to the first member of your group or raid (in slot order) whose Smart Loot quota still wants it, or wants an adornment on it. Quotas are set in the Smart Loot window (`ogre smartloot`). | off |
| **Loot Distribution (see the Loot Distribution tab)** | Items Smart Loot did not hand out go to a Resolve auction first: the group is asked who gains the most Resolve from the item, and the winner gets it. Items nobody wants, or that do not qualify, fall through to the boxes above.<br>*Group only. In a raid nothing is auctioned. Each auction waits up to about 3 seconds for answers.* | off |

## Misc Options

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **TTS [Text to Speak] when a loot window has been open for 30 seconds.** | If a loot window is still open 30 seconds after it appeared, every one of your sessions says '<your name> Loot Window' out loud.<br>*Only works while 'Accept Loot' (Settings tab) is ticked.* | off |
| **Auto Confirm No-Trade and Heirloom (this does not "Loot" them, only confirms after they have been looted/assigned.)** | When the game asks you to confirm taking a No-Trade or Heirloom item, the bot clicks yes for you.<br>*It never loots anything by itself. An Instance Controller run ticks this box.* | off |
| **Do NOT loot shinies ( ? or ! )** | The bot stops picking up shinies ('?' and '!' collectibles) near you. Corpses and chests are still looted as usual.<br>*Applies to the automatic looter ('Loot Corpses/Chests' on the Settings tab) and to Instance Controller shiny steps.* | off |
| **Testing: loot Free For All items by item ID (LootWindow:LootItem) instead of selecting and clicking them. Leader Only windows and assigns still click.** | A test option. In Free For All windows the bot takes each item directly instead of selecting it and clicking Loot, which is faster. Leader Only windows and handing items to others are not affected.<br>*Still being tried out. Untick it if Free For All items start being left behind.* | off |
| **Play noise when an Exquisite Chest or A Reliquary drops (alerts the whole fleet).** | When an Exquisite Chest or A Reliquary appears, all your sessions get a message with a sound.<br>*Every session with this ticked sends its own alert, so tick it on one character only.* | off |
| **Enable coin splitting with the group/raid after looting.** | Each time you loot coin, the bot splits that amount with your group or raid. | off |
| **Only split if the coin includes 1 platinum or more.** | Coin is only split when the looted amount has at least 1 platinum in it. Gold, silver and copper alone are kept.<br>*Does nothing unless the box above is ticked. 99 gold does not count as 1 platinum.* | off |

## Auto-Loot item names

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Always loot these exact item names (Free-For-All and Leader Only). Adds to the built-in list (Void Shard, Obol, ...).** | Items named here are always taken from Free For All and Leader Only windows, even No-Trade ones. Your names are added to the shipped list.<br>*The name must match exactly (case does not matter). The FFA or Leader Only master box must be ticked for its window type.* | empty |

## Auto-Loot item names

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Exact item name** | Type an item name here (or fill it with From examine), then press Add or Enter to put it on the list. | empty |
| **From examine** | Fills the name box with the item in the examine window you have open (examine the item in game first). Press Add to put it on the list.<br>*It only fills the box - nothing is added until you press Add. With no item examine window open, the box is left as it was and the window says 'Examine the item first, then press From examine'.* |  |
| **Add** | Adds the typed name to the Auto-Loot list. It takes effect on the next loot window. |  |
| **x (remove row)** | Removes that name from your list. |  |

## Good to know

- 'Accept Loot' on the Settings tab is the master switch. With it off, the bot ignores every loot window, whatever is ticked here.
- 'Loot everything' under FFA only works when 'Accept any tradable' is also ticked. That box is what makes the bot handle Free For All windows at all.
- The Leader Only boxes only work when 'Enable options below' is ticked. With it off, Leader Only windows (including Smart Loot and Loot Distribution) are left alone.
- A paused bot does not loot Free For All or Leader Only windows. A window that opened while paused is not handled when you resume. Close it and open it again.
- Starting an Instance Controller run ticks some of these for you: Leader Only 'Enable options below', 'Loot everything' and 'Smart Loot' on all your characters, and 'Auto Confirm No-Trade'. Solo, it also ticks both FFA boxes.
- Auto-Loot names must match the item name exactly (upper or lower case does not matter). Your list is added to a shipped list (Void Shard, Obol and others). To remove a shipped name, list it as false in your own list file, Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\Loot\custom\autoloot-names.json (the shipped file explains how). Just leaving a name out of that file does not remove it.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/loot-distribution.md

# Loot Distribution

Loot Distribution hands out gear from a Leader Only chest by Resolve. The looter asks the group about each piece of equipment. Every member's bot works out how much Resolve it would gain in the slot the item would replace, and the biggest gain wins. A plain upgrade always beats a 'maybe later' bid. The top half of this tab (Lootee and Weapon Choices) is what THIS character will accept when someone else's chest asks. The bottom half (Looter) only matters on the character opening the chest, and only when 'Loot Distribution' is ticked in the Leader Only block of the Loot tab.

## Lootee Options. Options receiving loot.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Match Type for secondary slot. Example: If you are using a tower shield, only accept a tower shield.** | For your secondary slot, this character only bids on the same kind of item it already holds there, for example tower shield for tower shield.<br>*If your secondary slot is empty, nothing matches, so you bid on nothing for that slot.* | off |
| **Weapons only for secondary slot. Example: Scouts/Brawlers - This means you will NOT accept a shield in your secondary.** | For your secondary slot, this character only bids on weapons (sword, dagger, mace, axe, rapier, hammer, fist, katana, great sword, great axe, great hammer, staff, spear). Shields and other off-hand items are refused.<br>*A weapon that also fits your primary slot can still be bid on for primary.* | off |
| **Match Type for ranged slot. Example: If you are using a crossbow, only accept a crossbow.** | For your ranged slot, this character only bids on the same kind of item it already holds there, for example crossbow for crossbow.<br>*If your ranged slot is empty, nothing matches.* | off |

## Weapon Choices

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Do not accept two-handed weapons** | This character never bids on two-handed weapons.<br>*Tick both Weapon Choice boxes to take no weapons at all from distribution.* | off |
| **Do not accept one-handed weapons** | This character never bids on one-handed weapons. Shields and other off-hand items that are not weapons are still accepted.<br>*Ranged items are not affected.* | off |

## Looter Options. Options for the person opening the chest.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Only distribute items at or above a minimum Resolve:** | Only items with at least the Resolve in the box below are auctioned. Lower items go to the normal Leader Only loot boxes instead. | off |
| **Minimum Resolve** | The lowest Resolve an item needs to be auctioned. Only used when the box above is ticked. | empty (0 - no minimum) |

## Good to know

- Group only. In a raid nothing is auctioned; items go straight to the normal Leader Only loot boxes.
- Only the looter needs 'Loot Distribution' ticked on the Loot tab. Everyone else answers with the Lootee and Weapon Choice boxes from their own tab, whatever their own Loot tab says.
- Not auctioned: items with no Resolve, items you cannot equip, mercenary and mount gear, and items no class in the group can use. Those go to the normal loot boxes instead, as do items nobody bids on.
- A character never bids on an item it already has equipped or in its bags.
- 'Match Type' boxes need something in that slot. With an empty secondary or ranged slot and the box ticked, that character bids on nothing for that slot.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/onzone.md

# OnZone

OnZone does two things each time you finish zoning. It runs the commands in the Executes list, top to bottom. Then it cancels any of your maintained spells that are on the 'Cancel after zoning' list. Both wait until the new zone has fully loaded (about three and a half seconds after it appears), so they act on a zone that is really there.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Executes** | Commands the bot runs, top to bottom, each time you finish zoning and the new zone has loaded. Switched-off lines are skipped.<br>*Runs even while OgreBot is paused. Double-click a line to switch it off; drag to reorder.* | empty |
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Click one and press Add below, or double-click it, to put it on the 'Cancel after zoning' list. |  |
| **Cancel after zoning** | After each zone has loaded, the bot cancels any of your maintained spells that match a name here, whatever its rank.<br>*Runs even while paused. Double-click a row to switch it off.* | empty |

## Executes

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Command to run on zone** | Type a console command here. Put `eq2execute` in front of an in-game slash command. Press Enter or Add to put it on the list.<br>*Commas and ] are removed when you add the line.* | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed command to the end of the Executes list. It is not run now, only after your next zone. |  |

## Cancel after zoning

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add** | Adds the ability you clicked in the Full Ability list to the cancel list. Greyed out until you click one. |

## Good to know

- Both lists work even while OgreBot is paused. They only need OgreBot to be loaded.
- The Executes list takes console commands. To run an in-game slash command, start the line with `eq2execute`. A command you add here is not run straight away.
- Commas and ] are removed from a command when you add it.
- The cancel list matches any rank: 'Assault' also cancels 'Assault XIII'. It only cancels spells you are maintaining (your own buffs and effects in the maintained window).
- To add a spell to the cancel list, click it in the Full Ability list and press Add, or double-click it. In the cancel list, double-click a spell to switch it off, and the x removes it. The cancel list is shown A to Z because order does not matter there.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/other.md

# Other

Other holds options that do not have a tab of their own yet. The left column asks a dirge for Confront Fear when you have revive sickness, stops a few automatic cast cancels, and lets you accept group invites from any player nearby. The right column is a list of abilities the bot uses when you are stunned, stifled or rooted and have a detrimental on you, because the normal Cast Stack cannot act then.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Request confront fear via uplink.** | When you get revive sickness, send a request to your other characters over the uplink. A dirge among them, with OgreBot running (not paused) and in your group or raid in the same zone, casts Confront Fear on you. Used only if the raid and group chat requests below did not go out.<br>*Needs no message and no dirge in view; the other sessions decide if they can help. Fighters are cured first, then priests, then everyone else.* | off |
| **Request confront fear via group chat:** | When you get revive sickness and another dirge is in your group, say the text in the box beside this in group chat.<br>*Nothing is said if the box is empty. If you are a dirge yourself, nothing is asked.* | off |
| **(group chat message)** | What to say in group chat to ask for Confront Fear.<br>*A message containing the word NULL is not sent.* | empty |
| **Request confront fear via raid chat:** | When you get revive sickness and another dirge is in your raid, say the text in the box beside this in raid chat. This is tried before group chat.<br>*Nothing is said if the box is empty.* | off |
| **(raid chat message)** | What to say in raid chat to ask for Confront Fear.<br>*A message containing the word NULL is not sent.* | empty |
| **[NOT RECOMMENDED] Do not cancel group cures when no one has a detrimental.** | Normally the bot stops a group cure mid-cast when nobody needs it any more. Tick this to let it finish anyway.<br>*Some raid scripts tick this during a fight.* | off |
| **[NOT RECOMMENDED] Do not cancel cure curse when no one has a curse.** | Normally the bot stops a Cure Curse mid-cast when the target no longer has a curse. Tick this to let it finish anyway. | off |
| **[NOT RECOMMENDED] Do not cancel res when the person has been res'd already.** | Normally the bot stops a res mid-cast when the target is no longer a corpse, for example because someone else res'd them first. Tick this to let it finish anyway. | off |
| **[NOT RECOMMENDED] Accept group/raid invites from ANYONE nearby.** | Accepts a group or raid invite from any player your client can see, not only from your own characters. It only works when 'Accept Invites' on the Settings tab is ticked too.<br>*Invites from your own characters are accepted by 'Accept Invites' alone.* | off |
| **Use these while stunned / stifled / rooted:** | While the bot is running and you are stunned, stifled or rooted with a detrimental on you, it casts the first ready ability from the list below. Useful because the normal Cast Stack cannot cast in that state.<br>*Does nothing while 'Disable CS_Cure' on the Settings tab is ticked. The Enable/Disable Cures commands flip this box.* | off |
| **Delay between casts (seconds)** | How long to wait after one of these abilities fires before the next one may. Decimals work. Blank or not a number means 3 seconds; 0 means no wait. | empty (3 seconds) |
| **Full Ability list** | All of this character's abilities. Double-click one to add it to the end of the 'Use while disabled' list. |  |
| **Use while disabled (in order)** | The abilities to use while stunned, stifled or rooted, best first. The bot casts the first one that is ready; one on cooldown just lets the next one try.<br>*Group or raid cures are skipped while 'Disable Group/Raid Cures in CS' is ticked on Settings, and single-target ones while 'Disable Single Target Cures in CS' is ticked.* | empty |

## Good to know

- Confront Fear requests go out only once per revive sickness, and only while the bot is running. If you are paused when the sickness lands, the request waits until you resume. A revive at a scout camp is ignored.
- Only one channel is ever used for a request. Raid chat is tried first, then group chat, then the uplink.
- The stunned list only fires when you have an Arcane, Noxious, Elemental or Trauma detrimental. It does not check that the ability cures that type, so abilities that give immunity work too.
- 'Disable CS_Cure' on the Settings tab switches the stunned list off. The Enable Cures and Disable Cures commands also tick and untick 'Use these while stunned / stifled / rooted'.
- To add to the stunned list, double-click an ability in the Full Ability list. In the saved list, drag rows to set priority, double-click to switch one off, and the x removes it.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/overseer.md

# Overseer

The left column controls the bot's daily Overseer run. The bot opens the Overseer window, turns in finished missions, adds any mission scrolls in your bags, starts new missions with the best agents it has, and afterwards uses any Research Material in your bags. The run starts on its own soon after OgreBot loads your profile, then at most once an hour. It will not start while the bot is paused, you are in combat or dead, or you are zoning. Start Overseer Now runs it straight away. The right column is a separate tool: stand at an Administrator Agent and it buys mission scrolls for you.

## Overseer

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Do not touch overseer at all no matter what** | The bot does not run Overseer: no daily run, and Start Overseer Now does nothing (it says why in the console). Overseer reward windows are still answered.<br>*Buying missions (the right column) is a separate tool and still works.* | off |
| **Only do overseer when in a guild hall** | The bot only starts the daily Overseer run on its own while you are in a guild hall.<br>*Start Overseer Now works anywhere.* | off |
| **ONLY do Heritage Hunt [Daily]** | The only new mission the bot starts is 'Heritage Hunt [Daily]', and it skips Mishap missions. It still turns in finished missions and adds scrolls from your bags. | off |
| **Do not consume research material when finished** | Normally, after a run in which it turned in at least one of your own missions, the bot uses any Research Material in your bags (Advancement, Companion, Mount, Tradeskill, Upgrade and General). Tick this to keep them. | off |
| **Do not automatically add overseer quests** | Normally the bot uses every Overseer mission scroll in your bags and Overseer bag to add it to your missions, then looks at the list again. Tick this to leave the scrolls alone.<br>*'Overseer Boost to Season 5' is never used.* | off |
| **Do not select overseer rewards when multiple are present** | When an Overseer reward window offers a choice, the bot normally takes the first reward. Tick this to leave the window for you. | off |
| **Skip Charged Quests (The ones with a number beside them)** | The bot never starts charged missions. Normally it starts them once there are no daily or plain missions left to start. | off |
| **Skip Non-Charged Quests (The ones that count against your daily limit)** | The bot never starts plain missions or 'Heritage Hunt [Daily]', so of the regular missions only charged ones are started. Mishap missions are not affected.<br>*When your daily limit is used up, the bot only tries charged missions anyway.* | off |
| **Skip Mishap Quests/Agents** | The bot skips Mishap missions entirely and goes straight to the normal missions. | off |
| **Skip Treasured Quests (Blue)** | The bot does not start plain Treasured (blue) missions.<br>*Charged missions of this colour are still started.* | off |
| **Skip Legendary Quests (Yellow)** | The bot does not start plain Legendary (yellow) missions.<br>*Charged missions of this colour are still started.* | off |
| **Skip Fabled Quests (Purple)** | The bot does not start plain Fabled (purple) missions.<br>*Charged missions of this colour are still started.* | off |
| **Skip Celestial Quests (Green)** | The bot does not start plain Celestial (green) missions.<br>*Charged missions of this colour are still started.* | off |
| **Use Agents with Traits that are not positive and not negative** | Normally the bot only sends agents whose traits help the mission, plus agents with no traits. Tick this to also send agents whose traits neither help nor hurt, when it needs more agents to start a mission.<br>*Never used for Mishap missions.* | off |
| **Use Agents with Traits that are NEGATIVE** | Also send agents that carry a trait the mission dislikes, when it needs more agents to start the mission. They are used last.<br>*Never used for Mishap missions.* | off |
| **Try EVERY quest each run (keep going until your charges hit 0 or no agents are left)** | Normally the bot tries at most 50 missions per run. Tick this to try every mission in the list once, stopping early only when no agent is free. | off |

## Overseer - Manual run

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Overseer: idle** | Shows what the Overseer run is doing: 'running' with the current step and how many missions it has started and turned in, or 'idle' with the totals from the last run. |
| **Start Overseer Now** | Starts the daily Overseer run now. It ignores the guild hall box, combat, and the one-hour wait between runs. It does nothing if a run is already going, or if 'Do not touch overseer at all no matter what' is ticked.<br>*OgreBot must have a profile loaded.* |
| **Stop** | Stops the daily Overseer run that is in progress, and a Buy Missions run too. |

## Overseer options - For BUYING missions.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Any** | Buy missions from any season. Ticking it unticks the season numbers; leaving every season box unticked means the same. | off |
| **1** | Only buy missions from Overseer season 1.<br>*Only one season can be ticked: ticking one unticks the others.* | off |
| **2** | Only buy missions from Overseer season 2. | off |
| **3** | Only buy missions from Overseer season 3. | off |
| **4** | Only buy missions from Overseer season 4. | off |
| **5** | Only buy missions from Overseer season 5. | off |
| **6** | Only buy missions from Overseer season 6. | off |
| **7** | Only buy missions from Overseer season 7. | off |
| **Any** | Buy missions of any colour. Ticking it unticks the colours; leaving every colour box unticked means the same. | off |
| **Blue** | Only buy blue missions.<br>*Only one colour can be ticked: ticking one unticks the others.* | off |
| **Yellow** | Only buy yellow missions. | off |
| **Purple** | Only buy purple missions. | off |
| **Green** | Only buy green missions. | off |
| **Different missions (default 10)** | How many different missions to buy. From the missions this merchant sells that match your season and colour, the bot picks this many at random. | empty (10 is used) |
| **Copies of each (default 10)** | How many copies of each chosen mission you want. The bot buys until you have this many in your bags, counting copies you already had. The most is 20. | empty (10 is used) |
| **No Scribe Missions** | Normally the bot uses each copy of a mission right after buying it, to add it to your Overseer missions. Tick this to leave the scrolls in your bags. | off |
| **Destroy Extra Missions Purchased** | After using the scrolls, the bot destroys any copies of that mission still in your bags.<br>*This includes copies you had before the run.* | off |
| **Get to GH when done** | When a buy run finishes, each character travels to its own guild hall, the same as the Get To GH button. It does not happen if the run is stopped or fails. | off |
| **Buy Missions** | Starts a buy run for this character with the options above. It uses the merchant window if it is open; otherwise it opens the nearest Administrator Agent, which must be within 10. Then it buys, uses and (if ticked) destroys the scrolls, one mission at a time.<br>*OgreBot must have a profile loaded. To stop it, type `buyoverseermissions stop`.* |  |
| **Buy Missions via OgreConsole** | Sends a buy run, with this screen's season, colour and amounts, to every character picked in the MCP For-Who window (everyone if it was never set). Each of them must be standing at its own Administrator Agent.<br>*No Scribe, Destroy and Get to GH are sent as they are set here, ticked or not, so every character uses this screen's choices, not its own tab.* |  |

## Good to know

- The Settings tab has its own 'Do not auto Overseer' box. Either that box or 'Do not touch overseer at all' stops the automatic run.
- Start Overseer Now runs even when 'Only do overseer when in a guild hall' is ticked, and ignores the one-hour wait. It does not run while 'Do not touch overseer at all no matter what' is ticked - it says so in the console instead.
- Ticking a 'do not' box during a run does not stop it. Press Stop. The mission and agent choices do change mid-run, from the next mission the bot picks.
- The Skip Treasured/Legendary/Fabled/Celestial boxes only skip plain missions. A charged mission of that colour is still started.
- The agent boxes never apply to Mishap missions. Those use a Mishap agent first if one is free, then only agents with helpful traits or no traits.
- Stop stops a Buy Missions run too. `buyoverseermissions stop` also works.
- Season and Colour are one choice each: ticking a box unticks the others in its column. 'Any', or nothing ticked, means no filter.
- 'Destroy Extra Missions Purchased' destroys every copy of that mission left in your bags, including copies you had before. With 'No Scribe Missions' also ticked, it buys the scrolls and then destroys them all.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/pack-pony.md

# Pack Pony

Pack Pony sends your Artisan's Pack Pony out to gather harvests by itself. With 'Enable Pack Pony' ticked and the bot running, the bot summons the pony, hails it and answers its questions using your choices below. If the pony offers to empty its packs, the bot accepts that first and then hails it again. The bot is paused while it does this and resumed afterwards. After a successful send-out it waits 2 hours 5 minutes before trying again, 10 minutes if the pony is still out or something failed, and 1 minute if you were busy. The three groups of boxes are the answers to the pony's three questions. Tick one box per group; ticking a box unticks the others in that group.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Enable Pack Pony** | While the bot is running, it sends your pack pony out whenever the wait from the last run is over. | off |
| **In Guild Hall only** | The pony is only sent out while you are in a guild hall. | off |
| **Do not dismiss when finished** | The pony stays summoned after the run. Normally the bot dismisses it when it is done.<br>*Runs started by TaskRunner still dismiss it.* | off (the pony is dismissed) |
| **Conversation 1 - Option 1 (1-59 harvests)** | When the pony asks its first question ('I need some level ... harvests'), the bot picks reply 1. | off |
| **Conversation 1 - Option 2 (60-99 harvests)** | When the pony asks its first question, the bot picks reply 2. | off |
| **Conversation 1 - Option 3 (100+ harvests)** | When the pony asks its first question, the bot picks reply 3. This is also used when no box in this group is ticked. | off (used anyway when none is ticked) |
| **Conversation 1 - Option 4 (Special Events?)** | When the pony asks its first question, the bot picks reply 4. | off |
| **Conversation 2 - Option 1 (1-9 / 60-69 / 100-109 harvests)** | When the pony asks its second question ('Gather level ... harvests'), the bot picks reply 1. | off |
| **Conversation 2 - Option 2 (10-19 / 70-79 / 110-120 harvests)** | When the pony asks its second question, the bot picks reply 2. | off |
| **Conversation 2 - Option 3 (20-29 / 80-89 / 120-130 harvests)** | When the pony asks its second question, the bot picks reply 3. This is also used when no box in this group is ticked. | off (used anyway when none is ticked) |
| **Conversation 2 - Option 4 (30-39 / 90-95 / 131-140 harvests)** | When the pony asks its second question, the bot picks reply 4. | off |
| **Conversation 3 - Option 1 (VoV 120-125 / PoM 110 / Thalumbra harvests / RoC 135)** | When the pony asks its third question ('Gather harvests from ...'), the bot picks reply 1. | off |
| **Conversation 3 - Option 2 (RoR 125 / EP 110 harvests)** | When the pony asks its third question, the bot picks reply 2. This is also used when no box in this group is ticked. | off (used anyway when none is ticked) |
| **Conversation 3 - Option 3 (BoZimara 125-130 / Luclin 110-120 harvests)** | When the pony asks its third question, the bot picks reply 3. | off |
| **Conversation 3 - Option 4 (SoD 130 harvests)** | When the pony asks its third question, the bot picks reply 4. | off |

## Good to know

- The character needs the 'Summon Artisan's Pack Pony' ability, or the run does not start.
- It never starts while you are in combat, while the bot is paused, or while another conversation window is open.
- If no box in a group is ticked, the bot uses option 3 for Conversations 1 and 2, and option 2 for Conversation 3.
- The boxes follow your earlier picks, the way the pony's questions do: Conversation 2 shows the replies the pony offers after your Conversation 1 pick (six under 1-59 harvests, five under 60-99, four under 100+), and Conversation 3 is only asked under 100+ harvests. Where a reply is not known (Special Events, Conversation 3 below 100) the boxes read 'placeholder' and can still be picked, in case the game adds one. A ticked box your path does not offer says 'not offered ..., pick another'. The options listed on this page are the ones shown for 100+ harvests, 120-130.
- The wait timers are kept only while the session runs. After a reload the bot tries again straight away.
- The harvest ranges in the box names describe what each reply meant in the old bot. The bot clicks the reply by its number (Option 1 = the first reply), so check them in game if the pony's replies change.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/post-cast.md

# Post-Cast

Post-Cast casts one thing right AFTER another has finished. Each row says 'after the bot casts B, cast A'. A can be an ability or an item; B is the ability that sets it off. For a spell with a cast time, A goes out once the cast bar is done; for an instant, straight after. Several rows can share the same B; they go one at a time, top to bottom.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Cast THIS  (ability or item)** | Pick what the bot should cast afterwards. Click an ability or item to select it for the next row. |  |
| **2. ...after this is cast** | Pick the ability that sets it off. After the bot casts this ability, the pick from list 1 follows. |  |
| **Post-casts setup** | Your post-cast rows, shown as 'what to cast   After: what it follows'. Rows for the same ability fire top to bottom, one at a time, once that ability's cast is over.<br>*Double-click a row to switch it off. Drag to reorder.* | empty |

## Post-Cast

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add** | Saves your two picks as a new row at the end of 'Post-casts setup'. It stays greyed out until you have picked one entry in each list. |

## Good to know

- To add a row, click the thing to cast in list 1, click the ability it follows in list 2, then press Add under 'Post-casts setup'. The text next to Add shows your two picks.
- Any cast the bot makes can set off a post-cast: the Cast Stack, scripts and commands. Abilities you click yourself do not.
- If your cast bar stays busy with something else for more than about 2 seconds after B, the post-cast is dropped, because it would no longer be 'after B'.
- Names match any rank: 'Assault' also matches 'Assault XIII'. An ability must be ready; items are just tried.
- A row that points at itself is ignored, and a post-cast never sets off another post-cast or a pre-cast.
- 'Disable Post-Cast tab' on the Settings tab switches this whole tab off. While a script has 'Dynamic Ignore Encounter CAs' or 'Dynamic Ignore PBAE CAs' ticked, post-casts of that kind are skipped too.
- In 'Post-casts setup', drag a row to change the order, double-click a row to switch it off, and the x removes it.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/pre-cast.md

# Pre-Cast

Pre-Cast casts one thing right BEFORE another. Each row says 'when the Cast Stack is about to cast B, cast A first'. A can be an ability or an item; B is the ability that sets it off. A pre-cast is optional: if A is not ready, B is cast anyway. Several rows can share the same B; they go one at a time, top to bottom, and then B goes out.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Cast THIS  (ability or item)** | Pick what the bot should cast first. Click an ability or item to select it for the next row. |  |
| **2. ...before this is cast** | Pick the ability that sets it off. When the Cast Stack is about to cast this ability, the pick from list 1 goes first. |  |
| **Pre-casts setup** | Your pre-cast rows, shown as 'what to cast   On: what it goes before'. Rows for the same ability fire top to bottom, one at a time, then that ability is cast.<br>*Double-click a row to switch it off. Drag to reorder.* | empty |

## Pre-Cast

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add** | Saves your two picks as a new row at the end of 'Pre-casts setup'. It stays greyed out until you have picked one entry in each list. |

## Good to know

- To add a row, click the thing to cast in list 1, click the ability it goes before in list 2, then press Add under 'Pre-casts setup'. The text next to Add shows your two picks.
- Only casts the Cast Stack chooses get pre-casts. Casts from scripts, commands or other bot features do not.
- Names match any rank: 'Assault' also matches 'Assault XIII'.
- An ability must be ready to be pre-cast. Items are not checked for readiness; the bot just tries them.
- A row that points at itself (the same ability in both lists) is ignored.
- 'Disable Pre-Cast tab' on the Settings tab switches this whole tab off. While a script has 'Dynamic Ignore Encounter CAs' or 'Dynamic Ignore PBAE CAs' ticked, pre-casts of that kind are skipped too.
- In 'Pre-casts setup', drag a row to change the order, double-click a row to switch it off, and the x removes it.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/pushover.md

# Pushover

Pushover is a separate phone and desktop notification service (pushover.net). With a Pushover account, the bot can send you a notification when certain things happen: a loot window left open, SmartLoot handing out an item, or a tell. Press 'Set up Pushover account' once to enter your Pushover details, then tick the notifications you want. The two Disable boxes at the top switch notifications off without losing your choices below.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Set up Pushover account** | Opens the Pushover Account window. Enter your application API token and your user key from pushover.net, then Save. Its 'Send test' button sends a test notification.<br>*The test obeys the Disable boxes below, so untick them to test.* |  |
| **Disable ALL Pushover Messages** | No Pushover notification is sent at all, whatever is ticked below. | off |
| **Disable Normal Pushover Messages. But allow priority messages. (Such as getting tells from people not on your eq2chars)** | Only high-priority notifications are sent. Of the options below, that is just the tell from someone not on your EQ2Chars list; the rest are normal priority and are blocked. | off |
| **[Normal Priority] When a loot window has been open for 60 seconds.** | If a loot window is still open 60 seconds after it appeared, you get a notification listing the items in it. | off |
| **[Normal Priority] When smartloot assigns an item.** | Each time SmartLoot gives an item to someone, you get a notification with the time, who got it and the item. | off |
| **[Normal Priority] When you get an in-game TELL from someone on your eq2chars list.** | When one of your own characters (anyone on the EQ2Chars tab) sends you a tell, you get a notification with who sent it and what they said. | off |
| **[HIGHEST Priority] When you get an in-game TELL from someone NOT on your eq2chars list.** | When anyone not on your EQ2Chars list sends you a tell, you get a high-priority notification with who sent it and what they said.<br>*This is the one notification that still gets through 'Disable Normal Pushover Messages'.* | off |

## Good to know

- Nothing is sent until your Pushover application token and user key are saved with 'Set up Pushover account'. They are kept on this PC, outside your profile.
- No tell notification is sent if you sent that person a tell in the last 60 seconds. You are clearly at the keyboard already.
- Notifications go out at most about one every 10 seconds. If many pile up, the oldest waiting ones are dropped.
- Scripts and commands can also send Pushover messages. The two Disable boxes block those too.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/spawn-events.md

# Spawn Events

Spawn Events works like Chat Events, but it watches for things appearing around you instead of chat. When something appears whose name contains your text, the bot can run a console command, post a line to OgreConsole, play a 'Ding' sound, or any mix of the three. Nothing happens until you tick "Enable Spawn Events" on the Settings tab. Build events with the boxes at the top; they appear in the Configured Events list below.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Configured Events** | Your spawn events. Click a row to edit it, double-click to switch it off or on, drag a row to reorder, and click X to delete it.<br>*A switched-off row is kept but never fires. Every active row is checked, so the order does not matter.* | empty |

## Add an event

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Actor to watch for** | Part or all of the name to watch for. The event fires when something with a matching name appears. Upper and lower case must match exactly.<br>*Required. An event with no name cannot be added.* | empty |
| **Code to execute (leave blank for nothing)** | A console command to run when a match appears. It runs exactly as if you typed it into the InnerSpace console. Leave it blank if you only want the OC line or the Ding. | empty |
| **OC - on success, send a message to OgreConsole** | When a match appears, a line goes to OgreConsole saying which character saw it, the text it matched and the full name of what appeared. | off |
| **Ding - on success, play a 'Ding'** | When a match appears, a 'Ding' sound plays on this PC. | off |
| **Add** | Adds the event to the list below. Pressing Enter in either text box does the same. While you are editing a row this button reads Update and saves your changes to that row. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks OC and Ding. Ticks otherwise carry over to the next event you add. |  |
| **Cancel** | Only shown while editing a row. Stops editing without changing the row. |  |

## Good to know

- Nothing here works until "Enable Spawn Events" is ticked on the Settings tab.
- The name match is case-sensitive: "vindicator" does not match "a Vindicator". Copy the name exactly as the game shows it. Part of the name is enough.
- It fires when something comes into your view, not only for a fresh spawn. Things that were already around when OgreBot was loaded do not fire.
- An event with no command, no OC and no Ding is ignored, and the console prints a warning about it.
- The OC and Ding ticks stay ticked for the next event you add. Use Clear Options to untick them.
- Spawn Events keep working while OgreBot is paused.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/tags.md

# Tags

Tags let one bot's cast switch other abilities off or on for a while, across all your bots. On the Cast Stack you give an ability an Embargo tag (it is blocked while the tag is on) or an Allow tag (it may only fire while the tag is on). When the bot casts an ability that carries a tag, the tag turns on, on this bot and on your other bots in the same relay group, for the time set here (a Cast Stack row set to 'Listen Only' never turns its tag on, and one set to 'Trigger Only' is not held back by it). This tab is where each tag is defined. The left list holds your tag names: type a name under it and press Add. Click a name to pick it, set its duration and options on the right, and press Add to put it in the Tags List. A tag that is not in the Tags List never turns on.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Full Tag List** | Your tag names, sorted A-Z. Click a name to pick it for the Tags List on the right. Double-click a name to rename it, and click X to delete it.<br>*A name here does nothing until it is also added to the Tags List. Renaming it here does not rename it in the Tags List.* | empty |
| **Tags List** | The tags that are actually defined, with their duration and options. Click a row to edit it and click X to delete it.<br>*Only tags in this list can turn on.* | empty |

## Top of tab

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Globally mute all tag messages** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot it hid the tag lines in OgreConsole. | off |

## Full Tag List (left)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Tag name** | Type a new tag name here. Use the same name you put in the Embargo tag or Allow tag box on the Cast Stack. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed name to the Full Tag List. While you are renaming a name this reads Update. |  |

## Tags List (right)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Duration** | How many seconds the tag stays on after the ability is cast. Leave it blank to use the ability's own duration.<br>*Items need a number here.* | blank (the ability's own duration) |
| **IRC** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot it also sent the tag over IRC. | off |
| **Group** | The tag only turns on for bots in the caster's own group, instead of every bot in your relay group. | off |
| **Me** | The tag only turns on for the character who cast the ability. Your other bots are not told. | off |
| **Incl. caster** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot it added the caster's name and the ability to the tag message. | off |
| **Hide from OgreConsole** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot it kept the tag message out of OgreConsole. | off |
| **Maintained** | The tag stays on while the caster still has the buff in their maintained list, and turns off for every bot as soon as it drops. The duration is then only a safety limit.<br>*Any rank of the ability counts. For an item it is the buff the item puts on you when you use it.* | off |
| **Add** | Adds the picked tag name, with the duration and ticks you set, to the Tags List. While you are editing a row this reads Update and saves your changes. |  |
| **Clear Options** | Unticks every option. Ticks otherwise carry over to the next tag you add. |  |

## Good to know

- A tag used on the Cast Stack but missing from the Tags List (or typed differently) never turns on. The match ignores upper and lower case.
- Leave Duration blank to use the ability's own duration. An item has no duration of its own, so an item that sets a tag must have a Duration here or the tag does not turn on.
- Two bots can hold the same tag at once; it stays on until the last one runs out.
- Only three options change anything: Group, Me and Maintained. IRC, Incl. caster and Hide from OgreConsole are shown for your information - the bot saves them but does not act on them (by design).
- The ticks stay ticked for the next tag you add. Use Clear Options to untick them.
- Press Save at the top to keep your changes for next time.
- Changes to the Tags List are used straight away. Press Save at the top to keep them for next time.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/unload.md

# Unload

Unload is a list of commands the bot runs, top to bottom, when OgreBot closes. That is the X on the OgreBot window or its mini toolbar, or `ogre end bot`. It also happens when you camp to another character in the same game window, because OgreBot closes and reopens for the new character.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Executes** | Commands the bot runs, top to bottom, when OgreBot closes. Switched-off lines are skipped.<br>*Also runs when you swap to another character in the same game window.* | empty |

## Executes

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Command to run on unload** | Type a console command here. Put `eq2execute` in front of an in-game slash command. Press Enter or Add to put it on the list.<br>*Commas and ] are removed when you add the line.* | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed command to the end of the list. It is not run now, only when OgreBot closes. |  |

## Good to know

- The list takes console commands. To run an in-game slash command, start the line with `eq2execute`.
- Unlike the Load tab, a command you add here is NOT run when you add it. It only runs when OgreBot closes.
- Commas and ] are removed from a command when you add it. A line that needs them will not run as typed.
- Double-click a line to switch it off without deleting it. Drag a row to change the order. The x removes it.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/admin.md

# Admin

Admin is for sharing profiles and for Profile Parts. The left side saves a shareable copy of your current profile, and imports profiles other people give you. The right side, Profile Parts, lets several characters share one tab's settings: you point a tab (for example the Cast Stack) at a shared file, and every character pointed at that file reads and saves that tab there. The Clear Item Effect Cache button makes the bot look at your usable items again.

## Administration

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Use file name** | The file name for the shareable copy, without .json. Leave blank to use 'SingleProfile' plus your class, for example SingleProfileBerserker.<br>*No slashes or '..' allowed.* | empty |
| **Use profile name** | The profile name stored inside the shareable copy. This is the name the other person sees after importing it. Leave blank to use your class name. | empty |
| **Save Custom Profile** | Writes a shareable copy of the profile you are running to Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\OgreBot\Profiles\Samples\<file name>.json. Your Aliases and Relay Groups are left out.<br>*Refuses if that file already exists.* |  |

## Importing Profiles

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Refresh List** | Reads the Profiles\Import folder again and shows the files you can import in the list below.<br>*The list does not update by itself; press this after dropping in a file.* |  |
| **Import Profile** | Imports the file selected in the list below: every profile in it is added next to yours (renamed with _1, _2 if the name is taken) and not loaded. With nothing selected it says so and does nothing. |  |
| **Profiles you can import** | The .json files in Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\OgreBot\Profiles\Import. Click a name to select it (it is highlighted), then press Import Profile. Click it again to clear the selection. | empty until you press Refresh List |
| **Clear Item Effect Cache** | Forgets everything the bot learned about what your usable items do, then examines the items on your Cast Stack again right away. Use it when an item's effect changed or was read wrong.<br>*The cache is shared by every character on this PC.* |  |

## Profile Parts

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Enable Profile Parts** | Master switch. On: each tab listed below loads from, and saves to, its shared file. Off: every tab uses your own profile, and the list is kept for later.<br>*Takes effect at once by reloading your profile. Save your other changes first.* | off |
| **New file name** | Name for a new, empty shared file, without .json. | empty |
| **Create** | Creates the empty shared file Profiles\Shared\<name>.json so it appears in the File list.<br>*Refuses if a file with that name already exists; pick it from the File list instead.* |  |
| **Tab:** | Which part of your profile to share: the list shows your profile's saved sections, one per tab. | empty |
| **File:** | Which shared file that tab should use: the files in Profiles\Shared. | empty |
| **Add AND load tab immediately** | Points the chosen tab at the chosen file and reloads your profile, so that tab now shows and saves the shared settings. Choosing a tab that is already listed moves it to the new file.<br>*Needs Enable Profile Parts ticked to have any effect.* |  |
| **Profile Parts in use** | Each shared tab and the file it uses ('from <file>.json'). A struck-through row ('would use') is switched off and uses your own profile. | empty |

## Profile Parts

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Double-click a row** | Switches that mapping off (the tab goes back to your own profile) or back on. The mapping is kept either way.<br>*Reloads your profile at once.* |
| **x (stop sharing this tab)** | Removes the mapping. The tab goes back to your own profile's settings, which were never changed while it was shared.<br>*Reloads your profile at once. The shared file itself is not deleted.* |

## Good to know

- Save Custom Profile never overwrites. If a file with that name already exists in Profiles\Samples, it refuses; pick another name.
- The shared copy leaves out your Aliases and Relay Groups, because those name your own characters and sessions. Everything else is included as it is right now, including tabs that come from Profile Parts.
- To import, drop the .json file into Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\OgreBot\Profiles\Import, press Refresh List, click the file's name in the list, then press Import Profile.
- Imported profiles are added next to yours and never replace one. If the name is taken, _1, _2 and so on is added. They are not loaded; pick one from the Profiles menu.
- Profile Parts files live in Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\OgreBot\Profiles\Shared. Any character pointed at the same file shares that tab: a change saved by one changes it for all of them.
- Every Profile Parts change (Enable, Add, the X, a double-click) takes effect immediately by reloading your profile from its saved files. Unsaved changes on other tabs are lost, so press Save first.
- In the Profile Parts list, double-click a row to switch that mapping off or back on (a struck-through row loads and saves your own profile instead). Hover a row to see this.
- Clear Item Effect Cache clears one file shared by every character on this PC (Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\OgreBot\ItemEffectDB.json).


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/debug.md

# Debug

Debug holds switches that make the bot explain itself. Each box turns on extra lines about one part of the bot: casting, the Cast Stack, HOs, assist, Overseer, and so on. The lines appear in this character's InnerSpace console and in its log file (ISXOgreEQ2.<session>.log in InnerSpace's extensions folder). None of these boxes changes what the bot does, except Visible Console Commands, which only changes how the bot's group commands show in OgreConsole. At the bottom, the Cast-Stack Dry-Run lists every Cast Stack entry and what it would do right now, without casting anything.

## Debugging specifics (these are wired up and working)

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **CastingDebug: logs one line each time the bot casts a spell - the spell name and its ID. (Light)** | Logs one line each time the bot casts something: the ability name and ID, or the item name, the cure target for cures, and what asked for the cast. | off |
| **CastingProgressDebug: logs each step a cast goes through - issued, cast bar started, fired/completed (or skipped as already maintained). Useful for diagnosing casts that stall, interrupt, or never start. (Moderate)** | Logs each step of every cast: sent, cast bar started, finished, already up, or given up. Use it for casts that stall, get interrupted or never start. | off |
| **CSDetailsDebug: logs the full saved settings of each spell as it casts (every option on that entry) plus who it actually resolved to and got cast on. Good for confirming a spell is set up and targeting the way you intended. (Moderate)** | Each time a Cast Stack entry casts, logs every saved option on that entry plus who it was actually cast on. Good for checking an entry is set up the way you meant. | off |
| **CSEvalDebug: logs the bot's entire decision every game tick - your status, then every spell and why it was or was not picked. Best for finding why a spell will not fire. (VERY noisy - turn off when done)** | Logs the Cast Stack's whole decision every time it runs: your health, power and target, then every entry and why it was or was not picked. The best way to find why a spell will not fire.<br>*Very noisy. Turn it off when you are done.* | off |
| **CSRecastDelayDebug: logs only the spells that were skipped because they are still on their recast-delay timer. (Light)** | Logs only the Cast Stack entries skipped because their own recast delay has not run out yet. | off |
| **ConsumeItemsDebug: logs the step-by-step of each automatic consume - which item, when it was issued, and when the flow completed. The Consume Items tab fires on its own whenever an item comes off cooldown, so this is off by default and the consume happens silently; turn it on to see what it picked. Failures are shown either way. (Light - a few lines per consume)** | Logs each automatic use from the Consume Items tab step by step: which item, when it was used and when it finished. | off |
| **CommsEventsDebug: logs the C3 comms receipt lines - '[Curse] <toon> -> igw:<x>: cure curse requested for <x>', '[GroupCure] ...' - one per session that receives the event. OFF by default: the -autocurse command that CAUSED them is already visible on the console, so these are duplicate narration in normal play and only earn their place while debugging the comms layer. (Light)** | Logs a line each time this character receives a cure-curse or group-cure request from another character.<br>*Every character that receives the request logs its own line.* | off |
| **ForWhoDebug: logs one line each time a command is skipped because its forwho did not match this character - the command, the forwho it was aimed with, and the name this session weighed it against (an empty name means this session has not resolved its identity yet). Commands that DO match stay silent, so group-wide broadcasts do not spam. (Light)** | Logs a line each time a command is ignored because it was aimed at someone else: the command, who it was aimed at, and this character's name. Commands that do apply stay silent. | off |
| **NPCCastDebug: logs one line each time a WATCHED named mob starts or stops casting - the actor, the ability ID and the base cast time. This is what tells you whether an encounter's interrupt rule is failing to DETECT the cast or failing to land the interrupt. (Moderate - one line per cast edge, only for mobs an active encounter is watching)** | Logs a line each time a mob that an encounter is watching starts or stops casting: the mob, the ability and its cast time. Tells you whether an interrupt rule failed to see the cast or failed to land the interrupt. | off |
| **CombatMoveDebug: logs in-combat movement (Move behind / in front / to melee) in detail - each time the maneuver changes, every input it decided on (the target, your position and heading, the mob's position, heading and HeadingTo, the angle, the behind/front point, who the mob is targeting, each check); while it moves, once a second, where the goal is and whether you got closer (flags MOVING AWAY FROM ITS GOAL). Turn it on when a toon walks the wrong way in combat. (Heavy while moving - one line a second, four per change)** | Logs Move behind / Move in front / Move to melee in detail: every time the maneuver changes, the target, where you and the mob are, which way the mob faces, the point it is walking to and every check it made; while moving, once a second, whether you are getting closer. Turn it on when a toon walks the wrong way in combat. |  |
| **WhatIsTheBotDoing: logs the bot's reasoning as it enters and leaves routines - for example why it turned auto-attack off. Useful when the bot looks idle and you want to know what it decided. (Moderate)** | Logs why the bot did some things on its own: moving into or out of combat position, turning auto-attack off, dropping invisibility after combat, and follow changes.<br>*Follow and Come2Me lines go to the log file only.* | off |
| **AnnounceDebug: logs each announce row weighed when a cast lands - which row matched (or that none did) and the text that went out. Use it when an announce fires on the wrong spell, or not at all. (Light - one line per announced cast)** | When a cast lands, logs each Announce tab row it checked, which one matched (or that none did), and the text sent. Use it when an announce fires on the wrong spell or not at all. | off |
| **OverseerDebug: logs an Overseer run step by step - which window it is on, what it read there and what it clicked. The first thing to turn on for a run that stalls partway. (Moderate, and only during a run)** | Logs an Overseer run step by step: each stage it moves to, each agent assigned, each quest started or completed, and quests skipped for lack of agents. | off |
| **OverseerAgentsDebug: logs the 'add agents to your collection' pass - each agent card, and whether it was added, a duplicate, converted or destroyed. It does not log which agent goes on which mission. (Light - only while agent cards are being used)** | Logs the 'add agents to your collection' pass step by step: each agent card, and whether it was added, a duplicate, converted or destroyed. | off |
| **Keyboard dump - Shift stuck, or symbols will not type? Click it WHILE it is happening and send the console lines (same as `ogre keys`)** | Prints everything about the keyboard right now: which keys the game thinks are held (Shift, Caps Lock and others), which window has keyboard focus, and the last keys pressed. Same as typing `ogre keys`.<br>*The last keys cover only this visit to the world. Check the lines before sharing them.* |  |
| **RewardWindowDebug: logs one line for each reward window that opens - its title and how many rewards it offers. (The line saying which reward was taken prints with or without this box.) (Light)** | Logs one line for each reward window that opens: its title and how many rewards it offers.<br>*The line saying which reward was taken prints whether this is on or off.* | off |
| **DoHODebug: logs the solo HO (DoHO) step by step - the setup and its target, whether it ran the full election or only turned the HO'er's own legs back on, every HO option it set and for whom (here, or sent to the group), the prime, each HO counted as completed or expired, and why it stood down (done, timed out, target gone). Use it when a fight's HO does not open or the group does not join it. (Moderate - about 40 lines per HO)** | Logs the solo HO (Do HO) step by step: the setup and its target, every HO option it set and for whom, each HO completed or expired, and why it stopped. Use it when a fight's HO does not open or the group does not join in. | off |
| **VisibleConsoleCommands: the bot's own group commands (DoHO options, encounter broadcasts, HO events, group travel) are sent as oc !c instead of the invisible oc !ci, so each one shows in OgreConsole. Delivery is the same either way - every session in the relay group gets them, this one included; only the display changes. (Noisy while on)** | The bot's own group commands (Do HO options, encounter messages, HO events, group travel) show up in OgreConsole so you can watch them. Normally they are sent hidden. Every character still receives them exactly the same way.<br>*Noisy while on.* | off |
| **HeroicOpportunityDebug: logs each HO the bot opens - the actor, the starter ability it chose, whether the starter icon was visible and whether the timer was skipped. The HO engine spans five files and had one log line in all of them, so an HO that never starts was previously silent. (Light - one line per HO)** | Logs each HO the bot starts: the mob, the starter ability it chose, whether the starter icon was showing, and whether the wait timer was skipped. | off |
| **AssistDebug: logs what assist decided, and names the three outcomes that look identical from outside - claiming a target, 'I am in control' and 'leave me alone'. Only speaks when the answer CHANGES, so it is safe to leave on. (Light)** | Logs who assist wants you to attack and why. It only logs when that answer changes, so it is safe to leave on. | off |
| **ReapplyValueDebug: for every ward carrying an RW< value, logs its remaining damage against the value you set and whether that counts as depleted. Use it when a ward is not re-cast, or is re-cast constantly - it tells you which of the two numbers is wrong. (Noisy - one line per ward every tick)** | For every ward with a 'Reapply-ward <=' value, logs how much damage it has left, your value, and whether that counts as used up. Use it when a ward is not re-cast, or is re-cast all the time.<br>*Noisy: one line per ward each time the Cast Stack runs.* | off |
| **AbilityViaDebug: logs each CastVia query exactly as the bot parsed it - every term, the options in effect, anything it was told to ignore, and which ability won (or that NOTHING matched, which otherwise looks the same as a deliberate hold). (Light - one line per query)** | When a script or command asks the bot to find an ability by description (CastVia), logs how the request was read, what was ruled out, and which ability won, or that nothing matched. | off |
| **AliasesDebug: each time the alias list is rebuilt, logs every record and who it currently resolves to, or 'nobody live'. Separates an alias that failed to parse from one that simply has nobody online - downstream both just fail to match. (Light - once per rebuild)** | Each time the Aliases list is rebuilt, logs every alias and who it points to right now, or 'nobody live'. Tells a mistyped alias apart from one whose characters are simply not online. | off |
| **ProfilePartsDebug: on profile load, logs whether Profile Parts is on and which tab is being read from which shared file, disabled mappings included. Use it when a tab shows settings you do not remember saving. (Light - once per load)** | When a profile loads, logs whether Profile Parts is on and which tab is being read from which shared file, including switched-off ones. Use it when a tab shows settings you do not remember saving. | off |
| **LoadingProcessDebug: times each step of opening the bot - the ability export, the roster, the cast stack, every tab seed - so a slow or apparently hung load names the step responsible instead of one silent gap. (Light - once per load)** | Times each step of opening the bot (abilities, roster, Cast Stack, each tab), so a slow or stuck load shows which step is to blame. | off |

## Deliberately not wired (the information is already there)

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Failed casts: already covered - CastingProgressDebug above reports every cast that was issued and did not complete, with the reason. A second flag for the same lines would only split one story across two switches.** | **Not active yet.** Does nothing. Casts that fail are already reported by CastingProgressDebug. | off |
| **Queued commands: the command queue already logs unconditionally, so there is nothing here to turn ON. What this wants is the opposite - a MUTE - which is a different control and a different decision.** | **Not active yet.** Does nothing. The command queue already logs all the time. | off |
| **Dispels: there is no dispel module in the new bot yet. A dispel is an ordinary cast-stack entry, and the walk trace already says why one was or was not picked. Wire this if dispels ever get their own handling.** | **Not active yet.** Does nothing. Dispels are ordinary Cast Stack entries, and CSEvalDebug already shows why one was or was not picked. | off |

## Cast-Stack Dry-Run

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Evaluate every cast-order entry vs the live game state - what each would do right now (dry-run, never casts)** | One row per Cast Stack entry, in order: its number, its name, then 'WOULD CAST' in green (with the target), or the reason it would be skipped, such as 'recast delay still active' or 'no valid target'. Switched-off entries are greyed. The last column sums up the entry's settings. | empty until you press Evaluate |

## Cast-Stack Dry-Run

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Evaluate every entry now** | Checks every Cast Stack entry against your current target, group and state, and fills the list below with what each one would do right now. Nothing is cast.<br>*It also prints every entry and its saved settings to the console, so expect a burst of lines.* |

## Good to know

- Debug boxes are saved in your profile like any other setting. A noisy box you forget to untick stays on after a reload.
- The log file starts fresh every time the extension loads. Copy it before you restart if you want to send it to someone.
- A few WhatIsTheBotDoing lines (following, and the Come2Me command) go only to the log file, not the console.
- The three boxes under 'Deliberately not wired' do nothing. They are there so you know why no switch exists for those topics.
- The Keyboard dump includes the last keys you pressed since entering the world. If you just typed something private in game, do not paste the dump anywhere public.
- Cast-Stack Dry-Run: the list only fills after you press 'Evaluate every entry now'. It is a snapshot of that moment; press it again to refresh. It also prints every entry, with all its saved settings, to the console.
