Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/eq2chars.md

# EQ2Chars

EQ2Chars is your list of characters. It does two jobs. Every character on it is trusted: the bot obeys chat commands from them and, when 'Accept Invites' is ticked, accepts their group and raid invites. A character that also has an account and password can be logged in by the bot, for example with `ogre <name>` (add `-p` to load the bot paused, or `-ph` paused with its main window hidden). The list is one list for the whole PC, not part of any profile. Fill in the form on the left and press Add / Save; the list on the right shows everything stored.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Character:** | The character's name. Required. | empty |
| **Account:** | The game account the character is on, used to log it in. Leave blank to only recognise the character (trusted for commands and invites, but no login). | empty |
| **Password:** | The account's password. It is hidden as you type and goes straight to the private file on this PC, never into your profile. Blank keeps the stored password; a single - clears it.<br>*One password per account, shared by all its characters.* | empty |
| **Server:** | The server the character plays on. The bot picks this server when logging the character in. Blank keeps the server already stored. | empty |
| **Add / Save** | Saves the character with the account, password and server typed above. If the character is already listed, its entry is replaced (moved to the new account if you changed it). The password box is emptied afterwards. |  |
| **Clear Fields** | Empties the four boxes on the form. The stored list is not touched. |  |
| **Clear Character Name after Add** | After Add / Save, the Character box is emptied, ready for the next one. | off |
| **Clear Account Name after Add** | After Add / Save, the Account box is emptied. Leave it off to add several characters on the same account without retyping it. | off |
| **Add current Group/Raid** | Adds every player in your group or raid who is not already listed, as 'recognised only' (no login details). Mercenaries and pets are skipped. The first click only tells you how many it would add; click again within 15 seconds to confirm.<br>*Everyone added becomes someone whose commands and invites this character accepts.* |  |
| **Your characters - click one to edit it, X to forget it** | Every stored character with its account and server. 'Recognised only' in the Account column means no login details are stored. | empty |

## Your characters

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Search character or account** | Narrows the list to rows whose character or account contains what you type. The small x clears it. | empty |
| **Character / Account / Server (column headers)** | Click a heading to sort by it; click it again to reverse the order. | sorted by Character |
| **Click a row** | Loads that character into the form so you can change it. The password box stays empty; leaving it empty keeps the stored password. |  |
| **x (forget this character)** | Removes the character from the list straight away. The bot stops trusting it and can no longer log it in.<br>*No confirmation.* |  |

## Good to know

- Passwords are kept in a file on this PC, Scripts\OgreSavePrivate\EQ2\Accounts.json. They are stored as plain text (not encrypted), so keep that folder to yourself and never send it to anyone. They are never put in a profile, so sharing a profile does not share them.
- A password belongs to an account, not a character. Every character on the same account uses the one password.
- The password box never shows a stored password. Leave it blank to keep the stored one; type a single - (minus) to clear it.
- A character added with no account is 'recognised only': trusted for commands and invites, but the bot cannot log it in.
- The x on a row forgets that character at once, with no confirmation.
- Only the first 200 matching rows are drawn. Type in the search box to find the rest.
- The Character, Account and Server boxes are ordinary settings: whatever is left in them is saved in your profile, and in a Save Custom Profile copy. Press Clear Fields before sharing a profile.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/key-binds.md

# Key Binds

Key Binds tells the bot which keys your game uses for moving, jumping, flying and so on. Whenever the bot has to press one of these keys for you, it presses the key set here, so if your Forward is not W the bot still walks. The tab shows eleven actions in two columns. Each has a box with its key, a Set button and a Clear button. To change one, click the key box or Set, then press the key you want. The change is saved straight away, for every EverQuest 2 character on this PC. The keys are kept in Scripts\OgreSave\EQ2\KeyBinds.json, not in your profile.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **(the key list)** | One row per action: its name, the key it uses, Set and Clear. Click the key or Set, then press a key to change it. | the standard keys |

## Key Binds

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **(key box)** | Shows the key the bot presses for this action. Click it to choose a new key, the same as Set. Grey means it is still the standard key. |  |
| **Set** | Starts waiting for a key. The list is replaced by 'Press the key you want to use.' The next key you press becomes this action's key and is saved at once.<br>*Mouse buttons still work while it waits, so you can click Cancel.* |  |
| **Clear** | Puts this action back to its standard key.<br>*Hidden while the action already uses its standard key.* |  |
| **Cancel** | Only shown while waiting for a key. Stops waiting and keeps the old key. |  |
| **Forward** | The key the bot holds to walk you forward when it moves you somewhere. | w |
| **Backward** | The key the bot holds to back you up when it moves you. | s |
| **Autorun** | The key the bot presses for its Autorun command. | Num Lock |
| **Fly/Swim up** | The key the bot holds to rise while flying or swimming, both when it moves you and for its Fly Up command. | Home |
| **Fly/Swim down** | The key the bot holds to sink while flying or swimming, both when it moves you and for its Fly Down command. It is also used to land a flying mount. | End |
| **Jump** | The key the bot presses for its Jump command and for jumps along a travel path. | Space |
| **Crouch** | The key the bot presses for its Crouch command. | Z |
| **Look up** | **Not active yet.** Stored for later. Nothing in the bot presses this key yet. | Page Up |
| **Look down** | **Not active yet.** Stored for later. Nothing in the bot presses this key yet. | Page Down |
| **Zoom in** | **Not active yet.** Stored for later. Nothing in the bot presses this key yet. | Num + |
| **Zoom out** | **Not active yet.** Stored for later. Nothing in the bot presses this key yet. | Num - |

## Good to know

- While the tab waits for your key press, every key is caught, so the game does not see it. Press the key, click Cancel, or wait 15 seconds.
- If Set shows 'Reading the key list - press Set again in a moment', wait a moment and press Set again.
- A grey key is the standard one. Clear only shows once you have changed a key, and puts it back to the standard one.
- If two actions use the same key, an 'also used by ...' warning appears under it. The bot still allows it.
- Changing a key updates all your EverQuest 2 sessions on this PC right away. No Save is needed.
- Look up, Look down, Zoom in and Zoom out are stored, but nothing in the bot presses them yet.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/ogreconsole.md

# OgreConsole

OgreConsole is the window where Ogre shows messages from all your characters. The left column decides whether that window opens or closes when this character's profile loads, and whether Ogre may pop it open by itself. The right column sets up OgreIRC, which links your bot fleet to an IRC channel so you can send commands to it from IRC. The IRC settings are one set for the whole PC, not per character.

## OgreConsole

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show console on load (and right now)** | Opens OgreConsole each time this profile loads. Ticking it also opens it right now and unticks 'Hide console on load'.<br>*Unticking it does not close the console; it only stops the open on the next load.* | off |
| **Hide console on load (and right now)** | Closes OgreConsole each time this profile loads. Ticking it also closes it right now and unticks 'Show console on load'.<br>*If both boxes end up ticked, hide wins.* | off |
| **Never auto open OgreConsole** | Ogre never pops OgreConsole open by itself for an event, such as a tell passed on from another of your sessions. Your own commands and buttons still open it. | off |

## OgreIRC

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Connect to IRC** | Connects to IRC each time this profile loads, and when you press 'Save OgreIRC information'. This box is saved per character profile, unlike the IRC details below.<br>*Unticking it never disconnects. By hand: `ogre irc` connects, `ogre end irc` disconnects.* | off |
| **Uplink name:** | **Not active yet.** It is saved, but the IRC link always runs on this PC's own uplink. | empty |
| **Server:** | The IRC server address to connect to. Required. | empty |
| **Server port:** | The server's port. 6667 unless your server says otherwise. | 6667 (used when blank or invalid) |
| **Server password:** | The server's password, if it has one. Leave blank if not.<br>*Shown as plain text on screen.* | empty |
| **Nick:** | The name the bot uses in the IRC channel. This nick is always allowed to send commands. Required. | empty |
| **Channel:** | The IRC channel the bot joins. Required. | empty |
| **Channel password:** | The channel's key (password). Strongly recommended, because anyone in the channel who is on the Auth list can command your fleet.<br>*Shown as plain text on screen.* | empty |
| **Auth list:** | IRC nicks allowed to send commands to your fleet, separated by commas. Your own nick above is always allowed. Commands from anyone else are ignored.<br>*Anyone in the channel can add a nick from IRC with -auth, so this list is not real protection - the channel password is. Nicks added that way are not written back here.* | empty |
| **Save OgreIRC information** | Saves the IRC details above for this whole PC. If 'Connect to IRC' is ticked, it also applies them and connects. |  |

## Good to know

- The IRC settings are only stored when you press 'Save OgreIRC information'. They go to Scripts\OgreSavePrivate\Common\OgreConsoleIRC.json, shared by every character on this PC.
- Ticking 'Connect to IRC' does not connect right away. It connects the next time this profile loads, or when you press 'Save OgreIRC information'. Unticking it never disconnects.
- Anyone who can talk in the channel can give themselves command rights with -auth, and a command can do anything, including closing every session. Use a private channel with a password; that is the only real protection.
- Currently the only thing that pops the console open by itself is an incoming tell passed on from another of your sessions. 'Never auto open' stops that too.
- Whatever is in the IRC boxes, the two passwords included, is also saved in this character's profile on Save, and so in a Save Custom Profile copy. The log never shows the passwords.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/relay-groups.md

# Relay Groups

A relay group is a named channel that InnerSpace sessions use to talk to each other. Every EQ2 session joins 'ogre_everquest2' by itself, and the bot sends its fleet messages there: cast requests, cure requests, event messages, the MCP and key-bind syncs, and OgreConsole lines such as oc !c that name no -rg. You only need this tab to use a different or extra group, for example to keep two separate fleets apart on one PC. The left side moves this character's fleet messages to another group; the right side joins extra groups each time the profile loads.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Send this bot's fleet commands to another group:** | Sends this character's fleet messages (casts, cures, events, MCP and key-bind syncs, and OgreConsole lines such as oc !c that name no -rg) to the group named below instead of 'ogre_everquest2'. Takes effect as soon as you tick or untick it, and again at every profile load.<br>*Unticked always means 'ogre_everquest2', whatever the box below says.* | off |
| **Group:** | The group to send to while the box above is ticked. Setting it does not join it: for this character to hear what is sent there too, add it to 'Also join these groups'. Blank means 'ogre_everquest2'.<br>*Letters, numbers and _ only.* | empty |
| **Put it back when OgreBot closes:** | When OgreBot closes, this character goes back to sending to the group in 'Back to' (or 'ogre_everquest2' if that is blank). Unticked, it keeps sending to whatever group was in use.<br>*Matters because parts of Ogre, such as MCP, still send messages after OgreBot closes.* | off |
| **Back to:** | The group to go back to when OgreBot closes. Blank means 'ogre_everquest2'. | empty |
| **Also join these groups (joined on every profile load)** | Relay groups this character joins, on top of 'ogre_everquest2'. List the group it sends to here too if this character should hear it. Each is joined when you add it and again every time the profile loads. | empty |
| **Leave the groups above when OgreBot closes** | When OgreBot closes, this character leaves every group on the list above. It never leaves 'ogre_everquest2', even if that is on the list. | off |

## Extra groups

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Relay group to auto-join** | Type a group name here, then press Add. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed group to the list and joins it straight away.<br>*Press Save to keep the list for next time.* |  |
| **x (remove a row)** | Takes the group off the list. This character stays in it until OgreBot closes (and leaves only if the box below is ticked). |  |

## Good to know

- Changing the group only changes where THIS character sends. Characters - this one included - only hear it if they are in that group, and setting it here does not join it. So set the same group on every character of that fleet, and add it to each one's 'Also join' list.
- This character never leaves 'ogre_everquest2', so it still hears everything sent there.
- Group names can only use letters, numbers and _. Anything else is removed when you add a row, so the name you see is the one that is joined now and on every profile load.
- Removing a row from the 'Also join' list does not leave that group now. It is left only when OgreBot closes, and only if 'Leave the groups above' is ticked.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/uplink-info.md

# Uplink Info

Uplink Info is the list of your other PCs. InnerSpace can link PCs together (each PC's InnerSpace is an 'uplink'), so your characters on different PCs can talk to each other. 'Connect to all' links this PC to every PC on the list; 'Disconnect from all' drops those links. MCP's Connect and Disconnect buttons use this same list. The list belongs to the PC, not to a character, and is saved as soon as you change it.

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Uplinks** | The PCs this PC can link to. The row for this PC is marked 'this PC - skipped'. | empty |
| **Connect to all** | Links this PC to every other PC on the list, one after another. Same as MCP's Connect button.<br>*Does nothing if the list is empty or holds only this PC.* |  |
| **Disconnect from all** | Drops the link from this PC to every other PC on the list. Same as MCP's Disconnect button. |  |

## Uplinks

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Uplink name of another PC** | Type another PC's uplink name, then press Add or Enter. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed name to the list and saves it at once. A name already on the list is refused. |  |
| **Add this PC** | Adds this PC's own uplink name to the list. The button shows the name once it is known. |  |
| **x (remove this PC from the list)** | Takes that PC off the list and saves at once. It does not disconnect it. |  |

## Good to know

- Names must be each PC's InnerSpace uplink name, exactly. 'Add this PC' fills in this PC's name for you, so running it once on each PC and copying the names is the easy way.
- This PC is always skipped when connecting, so it is fine to keep the same list on every PC.
- The list is saved in Scripts\OgreSave\Common\Uplinks.json, shared by every game on this PC.
- If several of your characters on this PC press Connect at almost the same moment (for example from an MCP button sent to all), only the first one does it; the rest are ignored for 3 seconds.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/ogrebot/class-tab.md

# Class tab

The class tab is named after your class (Coercer, Dirge, Channeler, and so on) and sits in the top group of tabs next to Settings and Setup. It only holds options for your own class, so every character sees a different tab. Thirteen classes have options here. Berserker, Wizard, Illusionist and Templar show only a heading with nothing below it, and every other class shows '(no class-specific options for ...)'. Most of these options came over from the old bot and are not active yet in the new bot. The ones that work today are the Channeler's Construct's Sacrifice pet health % and conduits, the Coercer's Possess Essence options, the Dirge's Confront Fear options, and the Conjuror and Necromancer Dimensional Storage box.

## Assassin

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Exploit Weakness** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to control how the bot uses the Exploit Weakness ability. | off |

## Brigand

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **While Crimson Swath (Epic 2.0 buff) is up, cast Barrooms in cast stack ignoring # of NPCs.** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to let your Barroom abilities on the Cast Stack fire while Crimson Swath is up, even when too few mobs are in range for the area-attack rules. | off |

## Channeler

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Use this conduit with Efficiency:** | Whenever your Efficiency buff is up, the bot casts the conduit picked in the drop-down beside it as soon as it is ready.<br>*Only while the bot is running. It does not need a target.* | off |
| **(drop-down beside the box)** | The conduit to cast while Efficiency is up. The list shows your abilities that fit conduit slots 1 to 3, from your ability export.<br>*The saved value is the ability's name, so a choice carried over from an old profile works.* | empty |
| **Use this conduit with Snap Channel:** | Whenever your Snap Channel buff is up, the bot casts the conduit picked in the drop-down beside it as soon as it is ready.<br>*Only while the bot is running. It does not need a target.* | off |
| **(drop-down beside the box)** | The conduit to cast while Snap Channel is up. The list shows your abilities that fit conduit slots 4 to 8, from your ability export.<br>*The saved value is the ability's name, so a choice carried over from an old profile works.* | empty |
| **When CastStack for Construct's Sacrifice says "UseChannelerTab" - only cast if pet health is at or above this %** | For a Construct's Sacrifice entry on your Cast Stack set to 'UseChannelerTab': the bot only casts it in combat, on your own pet, when the pet's health is at or above this %, and not while the buff is already on you.<br>*The ability export tags Construct's Sacrifice as 'UseChannelerTab' for you. Other types ignore this box.* | empty (counts as 0: any pet health) |

## Coercer

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Intellectual Remedy rotation text to listen for: (Use Announce for calling out IR)** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, several coercers took turns casting Intellectual Remedy (IR) by listening for this chat line.<br>*The hint in brackets means: the call-out itself is set up on the Announce tab.* | empty |
| **Archetype Preference:** | The archetype (fighter, priest, mage or scout) Possess Essence is cast on: the first of you and your group of that archetype who is alive and in the zone - you first. If your pet came from a different essence and someone of this archetype is here, the bot dismisses the pet so the next Possess Essence goes to them.<br>*Empty means Possess Essence is never cast, as in the old bot. Only your group is searched, not the rest of a raid. The list offers fighter, priest, mage and scout.* | empty |
| **Do not cast in combat.** | Possess Essence is not cast while you are in combat. | off |
| **Cast outside of instances - such as overland zones and guild halls.** | Allows Possess Essence outside instances. Unticked, it is only cast inside instances. | off |

## Conjuror

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Cancel Dimensional Storage in combat when you have no pet** | While the bot is running, if you are in combat with no pet out and Dimensional Storage is on you, the bot cancels Dimensional Storage so your stored pet can come back. It never casts Dimensional Storage itself. | off |
| **Crystal Blast when Crystalline Destruction procs** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to cast Crystal Blast when Crystalline Destruction procs. | off |
| **Do NOT automatically cast "Shockwave" while casting other abilities.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Shockwave was slipped in automatically alongside your other casts unless this was ticked. The new bot does not do that automatic cast at all. | off |
| **Do NOT automatically cast "Shadowstep" while casting other abilities.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Shadowstep was slipped in automatically alongside your other casts unless this was ticked. The new bot does not do that automatic cast at all. | off |
| **Do NOT automatically cast "Magic Leash" while casting other abilities.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Magic Leash was slipped in automatically alongside your other casts unless this was ticked. The new bot does not do that automatic cast at all. | off |

## Defiler

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Do not use leg bite.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Leg Bite was cast automatically alongside your other abilities unless this was ticked.<br>*One encounter file (the Unseen) ticks it for 20 seconds, but nothing reads it yet.* | off |

## Dirge

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **COB rotation text to listen for: (Use Announce for calling out COB)** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, several dirges took turns on their COB ability by listening for this chat line.<br>*The hint in brackets means: the call-out itself is set up on the Announce tab. For taking turns today, use the Ability Embargo tab.* | empty |
| **Cast Confront Fear** | Your dirge casts Confront Fear on whoever is waiting for it: fighters first, then priests, then everyone else, oldest request first. Requests come from your other characters, the request text below, and your own revive sickness.<br>*Nothing is cast while it is unticked: requests still queue and are dropped after 2 minutes. Requests are sent by the 'Request confront fear' boxes on the Other tab of the character who died.* | off |
| **Confront Fear text to listen for:Example: Need a confront fear** | When someone says a line containing this text in group, raid or a tell, your dirge adds them to its Confront Fear list. Capital letters do not matter.<br>*Empty means chat is not listened to. The cure itself still needs 'Cast Confront Fear' ticked.* | empty |
| **Confront Fear text to listen for from other dirges: Example: Casting confront fear on** | When another player says a line containing this text in group, raid or a tell, your dirge takes the LAST word of that line as a name and removes that player from its Confront Fear list, so two dirges do not cure the same player.<br>*Put the name at the end of the line, for example 'Casting confront fear on Bob'. Your own lines are ignored. The bot does not say this line itself.* | empty |

## Inquisitor

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Verdict On Epics @** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to use Verdict on epic mobs when they reach the health % typed in the box below. | off |
| **(% box beside it)** | **Not active yet.** The mob health % for 'Verdict On Epics @'. | empty |
| **Verdict On Epic Named @** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to use Verdict on named epic mobs when they reach the health % typed in the box below. | off |
| **(% box beside it)** | **Not active yet.** The mob health % for 'Verdict On Epic Named @'. | empty |
| **Verdict On Heroics @** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to use Verdict on heroic mobs when they reach the health % typed in the box below. | off |
| **(% box beside it)** | **Not active yet.** The mob health % for 'Verdict On Heroics @'. | empty |
| **Verdict On Heroic Named @** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to use Verdict on named heroic mobs when they reach the health % typed in the box below. | off |
| **(% box beside it)** | **Not active yet.** The mob health % for 'Verdict On Heroic Named @'. | empty |

## Mystic

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Do not use leg bite.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Leg Bite was cast automatically alongside your other abilities unless this was ticked.<br>*One encounter file (the Unseen) ticks it for 20 seconds, but nothing reads it yet.* | off |

## Necromancer

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Cancel Dimensional Storage in combat when you have no pet** | While the bot is running, if you are in combat with no pet out and Dimensional Storage is on you, the bot cancels Dimensional Storage so your stored pet can come back. It never casts Dimensional Storage itself. | off |
| **Do NOT automatically cast "Shockwave" while casting other abilities.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Shockwave was slipped in automatically alongside your other casts unless this was ticked. The new bot does not do that automatic cast at all. | off |
| **Do NOT automatically cast "Shadowstep" while casting other abilities.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Shadowstep was slipped in automatically alongside your other casts unless this was ticked. The new bot does not do that automatic cast at all. | off |
| **Do NOT automatically cast "Magic Leash" while casting other abilities.** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, Magic Leash was slipped in automatically alongside your other casts unless this was ticked. The new bot does not do that automatic cast at all. | off |

## Ranger

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Exploit Weakness** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to control how the bot uses the Exploit Weakness ability. | off |
| **Cancel Focus Aim** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to let the bot cancel your Focus Aim. | off |
| **Cancel Wreak Havoc** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to let the bot cancel your Wreak Havoc.<br>*The bot does notice Wreak Havoc on its own (it lets you cast while moving), but this box plays no part in that.* | off |
| **Cancel Tracing Shot** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to let the bot cancel your Tracing Shot. | off |

## Troubador

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **POTM rotation text to listen for: (Use Announce for calling out POTM)** | **Not active yet.** In the old bot, several troubadors took turns casting Perfection of the Maestro (POTM) by listening for this chat line.<br>*The hint in brackets means: the call-out itself is set up on the Announce tab. For taking turns today, use the Ability Embargo tab.* | empty |

## Warlock

| Option | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Toggle Myth Click Automatically** | **Not active yet.** It is meant to let the bot switch your Mythical weapon's click on and off for you. | off |
| **Do NOT Force Myth OFF for Dark Siphoning** | **Not active yet.** It belongs to 'Toggle Myth Click Automatically' above: it would stop the bot turning the Myth click off for Dark Siphoning. | off |
| **Debugging for Myth** | **Not active yet.** It would print extra messages about the automatic Myth toggle. | off |

## Good to know

- Only your own class's options are shown. To see another class's tab, open the bot on a character of that class.
- Most boxes here are saved with your profile but do nothing yet in the new bot. Each one below says so.
- The three 'rotation text to listen for' boxes (Troubador POTM, Dirge COB, Coercer Intellectual Remedy) belong to an old way of taking turns that the new bot does not use. The Ability Embargo tab is the current way to share an ability between several players.
- Channeler: the conduit drop-downs hold an ability NAME. A choice carried over from an old profile works; the bot finds that ability in your ability export.
- Coercer: for the Possess Essence options to count, the Possess Essence entry in your Cast Stack must have the type 'UseCoercerTab' (the ability export sets this for you). With no Archetype Preference chosen, Possess Essence is never cast.
- Dirge: 'Cast Confront Fear' must be ticked for your dirge to cure anyone - requests from the uplink, from chat, and your own revive sickness. Requests still queue while it is off and are dropped after 2 minutes.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/windows/ogremini.md

# OgreBot

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> The small OgreBot window: a quick remote for pausing the bot and showing or hiding the main OgreBot window.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Pause / Resume** - Pause stops the bot acting on its own (casting, following, camp spot, looting, Auto-Hunt). The button turns yellow and reads Resume.
> - **Hide Main / Show Main** - hides or shows the main OgreBot window. The bot keeps running.
> - **The top line** shows your class. The **cog** in the title bar lets you choose what this window shows: your class, your character's name, and a line saying what the bot is doing. Tick what you want and press Done.
> - **What the bot is doing** (the bottom line) - Paused, the ability it is casting (Cast: ...) or item it is using (Item: ...), who it is following, Campspot active, or Idle.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - The X on this window stops OgreBot completely, the same as the X on the main window. Unsaved changes are lost.
> - A yellow star (*) in the title bar means the profile has unsaved changes. Hover over it to see that.
> - Your choices from the cog are kept for next time.
> - Pause only affects this character. Commands you send still work while paused.

**Open it:** It opens by itself whenever OgreBot loads (type `ogre`), next to the main OgreBot window. `ogre end bot` closes both. Opening it again while it is open does nothing (typing `ogre` reloads the whole bot instead).

## What it is for

The small OgreBot window is a remote for the bot and a quick look at what it is doing. The top line shows your class. Pause stops the bot from acting on its own and Resume starts it again. Hide Main hides the big OgreBot window and Show Main brings it back. The bottom line says what the bot is doing right now. The cog in the title bar picks which of the two lines you see. OgreBot normally loads with the big window hidden, so this small window is what you see.

## The top line and the status line

Both lines update by themselves while the bot runs. Here the character name is turned on in the cog, and the bot is following someone.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Top line** | Shows your class, for example Templar. If you tick Character name in the cog, your name comes first: Kannkor · Templar. If neither is ticked, the line goes away and the buttons get the room. | your class |
| **Status line (bottom)** | What the bot is doing right now. Only the first of these that is true shows: Paused, then Cast: and the ability the bot is casting, then Item: and the item it is using, then Following and who it follows, then Campspot active, and otherwise Idle.<br>*Cast: and Item: show only what the bot itself casts or uses, not what you click.* | shown |

## Pause and Resume

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Pause / Resume** | Pause stops this character's bot from acting on its own, for example: no new casts from the cast stack, no following, no pulling back to the camp spot, no looting, no auto-targeting, no Auto-Hunt. Commands you send still work. The button turns yellow and reads Resume. Click it to start the bot again.<br>*Only this character pauses, not the group. If something else pauses or resumes the bot, the button updates by itself.* | running (Pause shown) after `ogre`; paused after `ogre -p` or `ogre -ph` |

## Show / Hide the main window

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Hide Main / Show Main** | Hides the big OgreBot window, or shows it again. The bot keeps running either way. Only the window is hidden. | Show Main (the big window starts hidden after `ogre`) |

## Title bar

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **\* (yellow star)** | The profile has changes that are not saved yet. Hover over it to see that. Save them on the big OgreBot window. | hidden |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Shuts OgreBot down completely, the same as the X on the big window. Both windows close, movement and HUDs stop, the profile is unloaded, and unsaved changes are thrown away.<br>*To just get the big window out of the way, use Hide Main.* |  |

## Choosing what the window shows

The cog in the title bar opens a short list in place of the buttons. Tick what you want to see and press Done.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Title bar cog** | Opens the list. Click the cog again to close it without saving. |  |
| **Class** | Shows your class on the top line. | on |
| **Character name** | Shows your character's name on the top line, in front of the class. | off |
| **What the bot is doing** | Shows the status line under the buttons. | on |
| **Done** | Saves your ticks, closes the list and brings the buttons back. The choice is kept for next time. |  |

## What the window shows

- Top line: your class, with your name in front when it is picked in the cog.
- Pause (green) = the bot is running. Resume (yellow) = the bot is paused.
- Show Main = the big window is hidden. Hide Main = it is on screen.
- Bottom line: Paused, Cast: ..., Item: ..., Following ..., Campspot active, or Idle.

## Good to know

- The X on this small window stops OgreBot. It is not a minimize.
- Pause only stops what the bot decides by itself. Commands from you or your group still run.
- The cog's choice is saved for the whole computer, not for each character.

## Paused, with the main window hidden

![Paused](../assets/ogremini/paused.png)

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/windows/commands.md

# Commands

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Every `ogre` command you can use, in one list. Open it with `ogre ?`, `ogre help` or `ogre commands`.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - The first rows are `ogre` itself: loading OgreBot (`ogre`, `ogre -p`, `ogre -ph`) and `ogre ui reload` / `ogre ui windows` / `ogre ui report` (copies a report of the windows to paste when someone asks for one).
> - **Search** finds a command by its name, its other names, or any word in its description.
> - **Run** is `ogre <command>`; **End** is `ogre end <command>`, shown when the command has one.
> - A command that takes arguments has a box after its name: type them as you would after `ogre <command>`, then **Run** (or press Enter). The grey text in the box shows what it accepts.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - The list shows only the commands your access level allows. If you lower your level, the list follows at once.
> - Greyed rows are commands that have not been ported to the new bot yet.
> - The line under the search box says what was sent. Each command's own messages still go to the InnerSpace console.
> - For the exact arguments a command takes, see its documentation.
> - The bottom line names the OgreBot release you are on (the name the What's new page uses) and when the core was built. `ogre version` prints the same.

**Open it:** Type `ogre ?` (or `ogre help`, or `ogre commands`). `ogre end commands` closes it.

## What it is for

Every `ogre` command you can use, in one searchable list. Each row is one command: its name, any other names it answers to, what it does and, when it takes them, what you can type after it. Run does exactly what typing `ogre <command>` does, and End does what `ogre end <command>` does. Each command's own messages still go to the InnerSpace console; this window only tells you what it sent.

## Search and the result line

The count on the right is how many commands you can use. The line under the search box says what the last Run or End sent, or why it was not sent.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Search commands...** | Narrows the list as you type. It matches a command's name, its other names, its title, what it takes and its description. While you search, the count shows how many match out of the total. |
| **Result line** | Shows what was sent - for example `ran: ogre perf 10` in green - or, in red, why nothing was sent.<br>*It does not show the command's own output. Look in the InnerSpace console for that.* |

## A command row

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Run** | Runs the command, exactly as typing `ogre <command>` would - with whatever is in its box after it. |
| **End** | Stops or closes the command, exactly as typing `ogre end <command>` would. Only shown for commands that have something to end. |
| **Argument box (ogre <command> [ ... ])** | For a command that takes something after its name. Type it as you would after `ogre <command>`, then press Run or Enter. The grey text in the empty box shows what the command accepts.<br>*What you type is sent as typed - text with `${` in it is refused rather than worked out. For the exact meaning of each option, see that command's own page.* |

## Not ported yet

Greyed rows marked NOT PORTED are commands the old bot had that the new bot does not have yet. They are listed so you can see what is still to come; they have no buttons.

## What the window shows

- The first rows are `ogre` itself - loading OgreBot (`ogre`, `ogre -p`, `ogre -ph`) and `ogre ui reload` / `ogre ui windows` / `ogre ui report` (copies a report of the windows to paste when someone asks for one). They have Run only.
- Bold name = the command (`ogre <name>`). Next to it, its title.
- also: = other names that work the same way, for example `ogre fps` for `ogre perf`.
- The grey line under a row is what the command takes after its name, when it takes something.
- The count = how many commands you can use; while searching, how many match out of that.

## Good to know

- The list only shows the commands your access level allows. If you lower your access level (for testing), the list changes straight away.
- Run is the same as typing the command, so a command that opens a window opens it, and one that prints something prints it in the InnerSpace console - not here.


---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/windows/console.md

# OgreConsole

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Where your sessions talk to each other, and where the bot tells you things. Ctrl + ~ shows or hides it.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Type and press Enter** to send to every OgreBot session on this PC. Plain text is chat.
> - **Start a line with** `!c` to make every session run it as a command, e.g. `!c -pause igw:${Me.Name}`.
> - **Click a tab** (Chat, Commands, Events...) to see only those lines. A glowing dot means new lines.
> - **The gear** opens settings: time stamps, hide on load, line colours, and Clear text.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - `ogre` commands go in the InnerSpace console, not here. `oc <text>` there is the same as typing here.
> - Red = command, green = chat, white = bot message, bold yellow on a red band = error, purple = fleet event. Change any of them in the gear's Colours.
> - An orange name at the start of a line is who said it on IRC.
> - **Send typed text to IRC** (gear): what you type here goes to IRC instead, like `irc <text>`, and comes back to your sessions with your IRC name.

**Open it:** Press **Ctrl + ~** (the key left of 1) to show or hide it, or type `ogre console` in the InnerSpace console (if it is already open, that does nothing). It opens by itself when the bot loads unless **Hide on load** is ticked.

## What it is for

OgreConsole is where your sessions talk to each other. Anything typed in the box at the bottom goes to every OgreBot session on this PC: plain text is chat, and a line starting with `!c` is a command that every session runs. It also shows what the bot has to tell you - alerts, unknown commands, and the commands other sessions sent. Lines are sorted into tabs so you can look at just one kind.

## Title bar

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **⚙ (gear)** | Opens and closes the settings drawer at the top of the window.<br>*While the drawer is open it takes the place of the lines; if it does not fit, scroll it (or drag the window's bottom edge to make it taller). Click the gear again to close it.* |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes the window. The console keeps collecting lines in the background, and they are all there when you open it again. |

## Tabs

Click a tab to see only its lines. A tab appears the first time a line for it arrives.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **All** | Every line, in the order it arrived. | selected |
| **Chat** | Plain text typed by you or another session (and lines relayed from IRC). |  |
| **Commands** | `!c` commands sent by any session, plus the bot's replies about them (for example an unknown command). |  |
| **Events** | Fleet requests such as a cure-curse call, one line each, showing who asked, who it was for and what for.<br>*Only appears when the OgreBot Debug option CommsEventsDebug is on.* |  |
| **Any other tab (e.g. Raid)** | A line sent with `-tab <name>` at the front also shows in a tab of that name. |  |
| **Glowing dot on a tab** | New lines arrived in that tab while you were looking at another one. Clicking the tab clears it. |  |

## The lines

Each line's colour tells you what kind of line it is (the colours below are the defaults).

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Line list** | The last 2000 lines. It stays at the bottom as new lines arrive, unless you have scrolled up to read, then it stays where you are.<br>*Right-click to Copy or Select All.* |

## Typing and sending

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Input line (message, or !c <cmd> ... (Enter to send))** | Press Enter to send the line to every OgreBot session on this PC, including this one. Plain text is chat. A line starting with `!c` is a command that every session runs. `!ci` runs it too but the line is not shown. Anything like `${Me.Name}` is filled in with this character's value before it is sent.<br>*Put `-tab <name>` right after `!c` to also show the line in that tab, or `-cfw <who>` to have only that character (or group of characters) run it.* |

## Settings drawer

Open it with the gear. Settings are saved straight away and are shared by every character on this PC.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Send typed text to IRC** | When ticked, what you type in the input line goes to IRC instead of only this PC - exactly like typing `irc <text>` in the InnerSpace console. It comes back to your sessions with your IRC name in front. `oc <text>` is not affected.<br>*Needs IRC connected (`ogre irc`). A `!c` line sent this way runs on every session that reads the IRC channel.* | off |
| **Show time stamps** | Shows the time each line arrived at the start of the line.<br>*Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.* | on |
| **Hide on load** | When ticked, the console does not pop up when the bot loads. It still collects every line, so opening it later with Ctrl + ~ shows what you missed. | off |
| **Debug: trace verbs to log** | For troubleshooting. Writes one line per command this session receives to the bot's log file, saying whether it ran. Nothing extra shows in the console.<br>*Leave it off in normal play.* | off |
| **Colour square (Command, Chat, System, Error, Event, Timestamp)** | Click a colour square to open R, G and B sliders for it. The colour changes as you drag and is saved when you let go. |  |
| **Reset** | Puts that colour back to its default. |  |
| **Clear text** | Wipes every line from this session's console, removes all tabs except All, and closes the drawer. Only your console is cleared, and the lines cannot be brought back. |  |

## Colours

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **R / G / B sliders** | Red, green and blue for the colour you clicked. Only one colour's sliders are open at a time. |

## What the window shows

- Red line: a command (`!c ...`) sent by any session.
- Green line: chat.
- White line: a message from the bot itself, such as a `[Notify]` alert. Most of these show only on the All tab (a note that a command did nothing here also shows on Commands).
- Bold yellow line on a dark red band: an error, for example a command nobody knows (`Unknown command entered: -pasue`).
- Purple line: a fleet request on the Events tab.
- Orange name at the start of a chat or command line: who said it, for lines that came in over IRC. Only real IRC lines get it - a line you type that starts with `word: ` does not.
- `-cfw <who>` at the end of a command line: that command was meant only for those characters.
- Grey time at the start of each line (when Show time stamps is on).

## Good to know

- `ogre ...` commands are typed in the InnerSpace console, not here. Typed into this box, `ogre smartloot` is just sent to everyone as chat.
- Typing `oc <text>` in the InnerSpace console does exactly the same as typing `<text>` into this box: it goes to every session.
- `!c` commands run on every session, including the one you typed on. Use `-cfw <who>` or a for-who inside the command (such as `igw:${Me.Name}`) to aim it.
- Only the last 2000 lines are kept.
- All console settings live in OgreSave\Common\OgreConsole.json and apply to every character on this PC.

## One tab selected

With **Commands** selected only command lines show. The other tabs glow when something new lands in them.

![Commands tab](../assets/console/tab-commands.png)

## The settings drawer open

![Settings drawer](../assets/console/settings.png)

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/windows/mcp.md

# Master Control Panel

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> A grid of buttons that send commands to your characters. Pick a page on the left; the static buttons stay the same on every page.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Click a button** to send its command to the characters picked in **For Who**.
> - **Right-click a button** to build its command, rename it, colour it, copy or paste it, or assign it to a key.
> - **Right-click a page** to rename or colour it; **+ Page** adds one.
> - **Drag** buttons and pages to rearrange them.
> - The **magnifier** finds a button by name or command; the **gear** changes button size and options.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Buttons are shared by every character on this PC and saved as you go.
> - **Alt** + the backtick key opens and closes this window.
> - A key assigned to a button follows it when you move the button or its page. Clearing the button removes its keys.
> - A colour is kept however you close the picker; **Reset** takes a custom colour off.
> - A button needs a name - use **Clear button** to remove one.

**Open it:** Press **Alt** and the backtick key together to open or close it, or type `ogre mcp` (close with `ogre end mcp`). `ogre mcp` does nothing if the MCP is already open. Tick **Enable OgreMCP** (OgreBot, Settings tab, On Load) to open it every time a profile loads.

## What it is for

The Master Control Panel (MCP) is a grid of buttons that send commands to your characters: follow, pause, camp, evac, cast an ability, travel, and anything else the bot's command list offers. Buttons are organised into pages (the left column). A block of static buttons stays the same on every page, and the rest of the grid changes with the page you pick. The For Who window decides which characters a button's command goes to. Every change is saved at once and shows up live in the MCP of every other character on the same PC.

## Title bar

The buttons in the title bar. The **?**, the lock and the X are on every window.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Magnifier (Find)** | Opens or closes the Find drawer, to search every button on every page by its name or its command. |
| **For Who** | Shows or hides the For Who window, which picks the characters a button's command goes to. The text turns green while For Who is showing. |
| **Gear (Settings)** | Opens or closes the Layout drawer (button size, spacing, font size and the options below). |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes the MCP, and with it the For Who, Build command and Assign keys windows.<br>*Key binds still work with the window closed.* |
| **Alt + backtick key (keyboard)** | Opens the MCP if it is closed, closes it if it is open. |

## Pages (left column)

Each page is its own set of buttons for the right-hand block. The static block does not change when you switch pages.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Click a page** | Switches the right-hand block to that page's buttons.<br>*The page you are on is shared: switching page switches it in every open MCP on this PC.* |  |
| **+ Page** | Adds a new empty page called 'Page N' at the bottom and switches to it. |  |
| **Drag a page** | Moves the page up or down the list. A line shows where it will land. You stay on the same page.<br>*Keys assigned to buttons follow the buttons, so moving pages does not change what a key presses.* | on (needs Allow moving) |
| **Right-click a page > Switch to this page** | Same as clicking the page. |  |
| **Right-click a page > Rename…** | Opens a small box to type the page name (up to 40 letters). An empty name becomes 'Page N'. |  |
| **Right-click a page > Set colour…** | Opens the colour picker for the page selector's background. Reset takes the colour off again. |  |
| **Right-click a page > Set text colour…** | Opens the colour picker for the page name's text. Auto goes back to a colour that reads well on the background. |  |
| **Right-click a page > Delete page…** | Asks you to type the page's exact name, then removes the page, all its buttons and any keys assigned to them. You stay on the page you were on.<br>*Only shown when 'Allow deleting pages' is ticked and there is more than one page.* |  |

## Static buttons

The first block of button columns (3 by default). These buttons are the same whichever page you are on - a good place for Follow, Pause, Resume and Evac.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Click a button** | Sends the button's command. It goes to the characters picked in For Who, unless the button names its own target in every step (for example 'fighter' or 'Me'), in which case it goes to that target. A button made in Raw mode runs only on the character that clicked it. The button flashes; an empty button does nothing. |  |
| **Drag a button** | Drop it on another slot to swap the two (or move it, if the slot is empty). You can drag between the static block and the page block.<br>*Letting go over empty space cancels the move. A key assigned to the button moves with it.* | on (needs Allow moving) |

## Page buttons

The block to the right of the dashed line. It shows the buttons of the page you picked. Grow the window wider for more columns, taller for more rows.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Drag a button onto a page** | Moves the button to that page: into the same spot if it is free, otherwise the first free spot. When it lands on a page other than the one you are on, a message names that page.<br>*A key assigned to the button moves with it.* |

## Right-click a button

Right-click any button slot for this menu. On an empty slot, Assign to key and Copy button are not shown.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Build command…** | Opens the Build command window to make or change what this button sends, and its label. |
| **Rename…** | Changes the text on the button (up to 40 letters). Renaming an empty slot makes a button with just a label.<br>*A button needs a name: an empty name is refused and the box says so. To remove a button, use Clear button.* |
| **Set colour…** | Opens the colour picker for the button's background. The text colour adjusts itself to stay readable unless you set one. Reset takes the colour off again. |
| **Set text colour…** | Opens the colour picker for the button's text. Auto goes back to the automatic readable colour. |
| **Assign to key…** | Opens the Assign keys window for this button, to fire it from a keyboard key, a G-key or an extra mouse button. The key belongs to the button: move the button, or move its page, and the key still presses it.<br>*Only shown on a slot that has a button. Clearing the button, or deleting its page, removes its keys.* |
| **Copy button** | Remembers the button (label, command and colours) for pasting, and puts a code for it on your Windows clipboard so you can share it. The code starts with OGREMCP1.<br>*Only shown on a slot that has a button.* |
| **Paste "<name>" [over "<name>"]** | Puts the copied button into this slot. The menu names the button, and the one it would replace.<br>*The copied button is shared by every character on this PC, so you can copy on one and paste on another. Pasting over a button keeps that button's keys, so they now press what you pasted.* |
| **Paste "<name>" from clipboard** | Shown when your Windows clipboard holds a button code (for example one someone sent you). Puts that button into this slot. A code can only make a button; it never runs anything. |
| **Clear button** | Empties the slot: the command, label, colours and any keys assigned to the button are removed. Asks first. |

## Colour picker

Used by every Set colour and Set text colour. The button changes while you drag, and the colour is kept however you close the picker (Done, Escape, or a click on the grid).

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Colour box (#rrggbb)** | Type a colour as #rrggbb, #rgb or r,g,b (numbers 0-255). A red border means it is not a colour and is ignored. |
| **R / G / B sliders and numbers** | Red, green and blue from 0 to 255. Drag a slider or type a number; the button updates as you go. |
| **Reset / Auto** | For a background it reads Reset and takes the custom colour off, so the button or page goes back to the theme's colour. For text it reads Auto and goes back to the automatic readable colour. |
| **Done** | Closes the picker. The colour is already on the button and is saved. |

## Rename

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Name box** | The new name. Enter = OK, Escape = Cancel. |
| **OK** | Saves the name. For a button, an empty name is refused with a note in red - use Clear button to remove a button. |
| **Cancel** | Closes without changing anything. |

## Clear and paste-over warning

The same small box asks before Clear button, and before a paste that would replace a button. Pasting into an empty slot never asks.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Don't ask again for [5] min** | Tick it and set the minutes (1-999) to stop this question for that long. Clears and paste-overs are snoozed separately.<br>*Only for this window: reopening the MCP asks again.* | off, 5 minutes |
| **Clear / Paste** | Goes ahead. |  |
| **Cancel** | Leaves the button as it was. |  |

## Delete page

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Type the page name** | Delete stays greyed out until this matches the page name exactly (capitals count). |
| **Delete** | Removes the page, every button on it and any keys assigned to those buttons. |
| **Cancel** | Keeps the page. |

## Find

Opened by the magnifier. Searches every button, static ones first, then page by page.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **name or command… (search box)** | Type part of a button's name or of the command it sends. Names that start with the text come first. Up/Down moves through the results, Enter jumps to the highlighted one, Escape closes. | empty |
| **Click a result** | Switches to that button's page and rings the button for a couple of seconds. It does not press it. If the button is outside the window, a message says its page, row and column. |  |
| **▶ Run** | Sends that button's command right away, the same as clicking it, and keeps the Find drawer open. |  |
| **x (close)** | Closes Find. Clicking anywhere outside it also closes it. |  |

## Settings (the gear)

The Layout drawer. Changes show at once and are saved. They change the buttons, not the window size.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Static columns** | How many columns form the static block (0-99). If the window is too narrow, fewer show. | 3 |
| **Button width** | Width of every button, 24-400 pixels. The - and + step by 2; hold to repeat. | 92 px |
| **Button height** | Height of every button and page selector, 16-200 pixels (steps of 2). | 28 px |
| **Spacing — left/right** | Space between columns, 0-40 pixels. | 6 px |
| **Spacing — above/below** | Space between rows, 0-40 pixels. | 6 px |
| **Font size** | Size of the button text, 8-40 pixels. | 12 px |
| **Show command on hover** | Resting the mouse on a button for a moment shows the command it sends. | on |
| **Outline button text** | Draws a thin outline round button text so it reads on any colour. Display only. | on |
| **Allow moving (drag to rearrange)** | Lets you drag buttons and pages around. Turn it off to stop accidental moves; clicking still works. | on |
| **Allow deleting pages** | Adds Delete page… to a page's right-click menu. | off |
| **Open For Who on load** | Shows the For Who window whenever the MCP opens. | off |
| **x (close)** | Closes the drawer. The gear does the same. |  |

## What the window shows

- Page selectors (left column): the active page has a bright outline. '+ Page' sits under the last page.
- Static block: a slightly tinted border marks static buttons. A dashed line separates them from the page block.
- Empty slots: dashed outlines with no text. Right-click one to build a button there.
- Colours: a button or page with its own colour shows it; otherwise it uses the theme colours.
- A red button showing the first 4 letters of its name and a countdown (for example 'Resc 14.2') is an ability still on cooldown. It goes back to normal when the ability is ready. This only happens for buttons that cast an ability, and only for abilities on the OgreBot Ability Tracker tab with 'Enable Ability Tracker' ticked (Settings). The longest cooldown among your characters is shown.
- A button with a glowing ring is the one Find jumped to, or the one you just pasted.
- A small message at the bottom confirms things like 'Copied "Evac" - the code is on your clipboard' or 'Moved to "Travel"'.
- A menu or box that would not fit in a short window is kept inside it and scrolls.

## Good to know

- Your buttons, pages, the page you are on and your For Who choice are one file shared by every character on this PC: Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCP.json. A change on one character shows up in every open MCP at once.
- Changing button size or spacing does not resize the window. Nudge the window edge and it snaps to fit whole buttons again.
- The page column shows only as many pages as there are rows. With more pages than rows, make the window taller (Find still reaches buttons on hidden pages).
- A button that names its own target in every step ignores For Who. If any step is left on the For Who window (blank), For Who decides.
- In a command, ${Me.Name} means the character that clicked the button.
- A button set to go over IRC is sent through OgreConsole instead while IRC is not connected; the console says so once each time IRC drops.
- A key assigned to a button follows the button: move the button, or move its page, and the key still presses it. Clearing the button or deleting its page removes the key.
- If OgreMCP.json is damaged, the MCP opens with a few sample buttons and leaves the file alone so you can repair it. Fix or restore it before changing anything in the MCP - any change saves over it.
- Buttons from the old OgreBot MCP can be brought over from the Migration window ('Migrate your MCP buttons').

The Combat page is picked: the static block (Follow Kannkor to Loot) stays, the right-hand block shows Combat's buttons.

# For Who

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Picks which characters an MCP button's command goes to, and how it is sent.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Auto / OC / IRC** - send each button its own way, or force OgreConsole or IRC.
> - **All, Me, Group, Raid** - who gets it. Nothing picked means everyone.
> - **Fighter / Mage / Priest / Scout** - click once for that class, again for "Not" that class.
> - **G1-G4** - a group of your raid.
> - **Multi** - pick several; a character must match all of them (Fighter + G1 = fighters in group 1).
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Buttons that name their own target ignore the chips (Auto / OC / IRC still applies); Raw buttons run only on you.
> - Me, Group and Raid mean the character that clicked.
> - Each session keeps its own choice: your tank can send to Group while your enchanter sends to Me.
> - The choice is not saved: a new session starts at Auto with nothing picked (everyone).
> - The X hides this window, like Done, so the choice keeps working; the For Who button on the MCP brings it back.
> - **Clear** resets the picks; the command preview setting stays.

**Open it:** Click **For Who** in the Master Control Panel's title bar (click again to hide it). Tick **Open For Who on load** in the MCP's gear to show it every time the MCP opens.

## What it is for

For Who picks which of your characters an MCP button's command goes to: everyone, just you, your group, your raid, a class, or a raid group. It also lets you force how the command travels (OgreConsole or IRC). It applies to every button that leaves its target on the For Who window - which is what a new step in Build command does unless you fill in its who. It applies the same way to a key bound to a button.

## How it is sent (Auto / OC / IRC)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Auto** | Each button goes the way it was built (OgreConsole or IRC). | on |
| **OC** | Sends every button through OgreConsole, even ones built for IRC. An IRC button's connection target is dropped. Raw buttons are not changed. |  |
| **IRC** | Sends every button through IRC (Raw buttons are not changed). If nothing is picked below, Raid lights up (the old OgreBot behaviour). While IRC is not connected, the command goes through OgreConsole instead. |  |

## Who it goes to

Click a chip to pick it; click it again to un-pick it. With nothing picked the command goes to everyone. Right-click any chip to turn it off straight away.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **All** | Every character. The same as picking nothing. Turns green when picked. |
| **Me** | Only the character whose MCP you clicked. |
| **Group** | Everyone in the clicking character's group. |
| **Raid** | Everyone in the clicking character's raid. |
| **Fighter / Mage / Priest / Scout** | Each click moves the chip on: blue 'Fighter' = only fighters, then red 'Not Fighter' = everyone except fighters, then off. |
| **G1 / G2 / G3 / G4** | Characters in that group of a raid. Characters who are not in a raid never match. |
| **Right-click a chip** | Turns that chip off in one click (no need to cycle a class chip round). |

## Multi, Clear and Done

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Multi** | Lets you pick more than one chip. A character must match ALL of them - for example Group + Not Fighter = the group's non-fighters. All cannot be combined with anything. Turning Multi off keeps only the first pick. Resting the mouse on Multi says the same.<br>*Fighter + Priest matches nobody (no character is both).* | off |
| **Clear** | Back to the start: Auto, nothing picked (everyone), Multi off. 'Show command preview' stays as it was. |  |
| **Done** | Hides the window. Your choice stays in effect. |  |

## Settings (the gear)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Show command preview** | Shows a line under the buttons with what gets added to each command, for example 'auto -cfw igw:${Me.Name}+notfighter'. Display only. | off |
| **× (close)** | Closes the settings box. The gear does the same. |  |

## What the window shows

- The lit button in the top row is how commands are sent.
- A lit chip (blue outline) is picked. All is green when picked. A red chip reading 'Not ...' means that class is excluded.
- The preview line (when turned on) shows the route, then '-cfw' and the target that is added to each command. ${Me.Name} is shown as written; it becomes the clicking character's name when sent.

## Good to know

- The chips only apply to buttons that leave their target blank. A button whose every step names a target (Me, fighter, a character name ...) goes to that target whatever chips are picked. Auto / OC / IRC still applies to it.
- Buttons made in Raw mode ignore For Who completely: they run only on the character that clicked.
- Your For Who choice is saved with the MCP buttons and shared by every character on this PC. Changing it on one character changes it on all of them.
- Me, Group and Raid mean the character that clicked (or pressed the bound key), not each character that receives the command.
- Hide the window with Done (or the MCP's For Who button). Done, or closing it with its own X, keeps your choice: it is the same when the window opens again.

### Several chips at once (Multi)

![Multi: Group + Not Fighter, with the preview line](../assets/forwho/multi.png)

Multi is ticked, Group and Not Fighter are picked, and the preview line is on: the command goes to the non-fighters in your group.

### IRC with nothing picked

![IRC lights Raid](../assets/forwho/irc.png)

### Beside the MCP

![For Who next to the MCP](../assets/forwho/with-mcp.png)

# Build command

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Makes or changes what one MCP button sends.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Label** - the text on the button (required).
> - **Send via** - OgreConsole (normal), IRC, or Raw (a command run as typed, only on you - unless it starts with oc, irc or !c, which go through OgreConsole / IRC).
> - **Pick a command** on the left, fill in its settings, then **+ Add to stack**. Stacked commands go out together, in order.
> - **Click a step** to edit it; the arrows reorder it and x removes it.
> - **Save to button** writes it to the button; **Cancel** changes nothing.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Leave a **who** box empty to use the For Who window.
> - A command you picked is not on the button until it is added; Save asks about it.

**Open it:** In the Master Control Panel, right-click any button slot and pick **Build command…**.

## What it is for

Build command makes or changes what one MCP button does. You name the button, choose how it is sent, then pick commands from the bot's command list and fill in their settings. Several commands can be stacked: they all go out together, in order, as one line. Save to button puts the result on the button you right-clicked.

## Label and how it is sent

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Label** | The text shown on the button. Required. | the button's current label |
| **OgreConsole** | The command goes through OgreConsole to your characters (the normal choice). | on |
| **IRC** | The command is sent over IRC instead of OgreConsole. While IRC is not connected it goes through OgreConsole instead.<br>*If the For Who window is set to OC or IRC (not Auto), that choice wins over this one for OgreConsole and IRC buttons.* |  |
| **Conn** | IRC only: which IRC connection(s) should act on it. Leave empty for every connection.<br>*Ignored when the command ends up going through OgreConsole.* | empty (all) |
| **Raw** | Swaps the lists for a text box. Whatever you type runs exactly as written, only on the character that clicks the button - for example `ogre perf`. For Who does not apply.<br>*Switching Send via drops a command you picked but did not add yet.* |  |

## Commands (the list)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Search…** | Narrows the list to commands whose name, short name, description or alias contains the text. The count shows how many match. | empty |
| **Click a command** | Picks it and shows its settings below, ready to add. It is not on the button until you add it. |  |

## Runs in order (the stack)

The commands the button will send, in order, all on one line.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Click a step** | Shows that step's settings below. Changes apply to the step straight away. |
| **↑ / ↓** | Moves the step up or down. |
| **✕** | Removes the step. |

## The command's settings

One row per setting of the picked command, with its type and a hint underneath. A newly picked command starts with its default values already filled in. A grey value in an empty box is the default that is used if you leave the box empty.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **who (FORWHO) box** | Which characters this step is for. Leave it empty to use the For Who window. Type a target, or use who ▾.<br>*If every step names a target, the button ignores For Who.* | empty (For Who window) |
| **who ▾** | Quick picks for the who box: Auto (the For Who window), All, Me, Group, Raid, Fighter, Mage, Priest, Scout, G1-G4. Me, Group and Raid are worked out from the character that clicks the button: that character, its group, its raid. |  |
| **pick ▾** | Shown on settings that have a fixed list of choices: pick one, or type your own. |  |
| **Text and number boxes** | Type the value. Number boxes accept only digits, a dot and a minus. |  |
| **TRUE / FALSE box** | Click to switch between TRUE and FALSE. |  |
| **＋ Add to stack** | Adds the picked command, with these settings, to the end of the stack. |  |
| **✕ Remove step** | Shown instead of Add when you are editing a step: removes that step. |  |

## Preview, Cancel and Save

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Sends** | The exact line the button will send. Display only. |
| **Cancel** | Closes the window. The button is not changed. |
| **Save to button** | Puts the label and the command on the button and closes the window. The MCP saves it at once.<br>*With no label it refuses: 'A label is required - name the button first.'* |

## Save with a command not added

If you picked and filled in a command but never pressed Add to stack, Save asks what to do with it.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Add & save** | Adds the command to the stack, then saves. |
| **Discard** | Saves without that command. |
| **Cancel** | Goes back to editing; nothing is saved. |

## Raw mode

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Raw command** | The command to run, exactly as typed, on the character that clicks the button. Useful for local things such as `ogre perf`.<br>*Text that starts with 'oc ', 'irc ' or '!c' is not run locally - it is sent through OgreConsole or IRC.* | empty |

## What the window shows

- Commands header: 'Commands' and the count (or 'shown / total' while searching).
- An 'ALL PARAMS' tag on a command means it takes everything typed after it. If another step follows it, the end marker -endargs is added for you (the step then shows 'all params +endargs').
- Runs in order: each step as it will be sent, numbered. The picked step is highlighted.
- Settings rows: the setting's name, its type (for example FORWHO, STRING, FLOAT, BOOL or ALL PARAMS) and a hint line.
- The step preview (bottom-left of the settings area) and the Sends line update as you type. Settings left at their default are left off the end of the line.

## Good to know

- Nothing is saved to the button until Save to button. Cancel or the window's X leaves the button as it was.
- A command you click in the list is only a draft until '+ Add to stack'. Save asks about it rather than losing it.
- A button pasted from a code, with only a command, opens with its command split back into steps. If it cannot be split it opens in Raw, unchanged.
- Saving an empty stack keeps the label but removes the command - the button then does nothing when clicked.

### Picking a new command

![A picked command, not yet added](../assets/mcpbuild/draft.png)

-TravelMeshGroup is picked and its destination filled in; it is not on the button until **+ Add to stack**.

### The who ▾ quick picks

![who quick picks](../assets/mcpbuild/whopick.png)

### Sending over IRC

![IRC with a Conn box](../assets/mcpbuild/irc.png)

### No label

![Save refused without a label](../assets/mcpbuild/nolabel.png)

# Assign keys

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Links a key, G-key or extra mouse button to one MCP button. Pressing it does what clicking the button does.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Key detector** - click the box, press your G-key or side mouse button, then click the box again to assign it.
> - **Click a key** in the list to assign it. Keys already in use show which button they fire.
> - **x** on a tag under Assigned to this button removes that key.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Keys work with the MCP closed, on every character on this PC.
> - A key belongs to the button: move the button or its page and the key still presses it. Clearing the button, or deleting its page, removes its keys.
> - One key can fire several buttons if you assign it more than once.

**Open it:** In the Master Control Panel, right-click a button and pick **Assign to key…**.

## What it is for

Assign keys links a key - a keyboard key, a Logitech G-key, a gamepad button or an extra mouse button - to one MCP button. Pressing the key does exactly what clicking the button does, including its For Who. Keys keep working when the MCP window is closed, and they are set up on every character on this PC.

## Key detector

The easy way to find the name of an unusual key, such as a G-key or a side mouse button.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Click here, then press your button** | Click it, then press the key within 20 seconds. The box shows the key it caught (for example '✓ G600-G12 — click to assign'). Click the box again to assign that key to this button.<br>*It only catches G-keys (G600/G510), gamepad buttons, mouse buttons 4 and up and F13-F24. For any other key, click it in the list.* |

## Key list

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **filter keys… (placeholder)** | Shows only keys whose name contains the text. Escape closes the window. | empty |
| **Click a key** | Assigns that key to this button straight away. It is saved and working at once.<br>*A key that already fires another button (shown on the right) now fires both.* |  |

## Assigned to this button

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **✕ (on a key tag)** | Removes that key from this button. It stops working at once on every character on this PC. |
| **Close** | Hides the window (and stops a key detector that is still listening). |

## What the window shows

- 'Assign a key to Evac': the button this window is working on.
- Key list: each key's InnerSpace name; '→ Pause' on the right = that key already fires the Pause button. The current button's name is highlighted and its keys are shaded.
- Detector box: dashed while waiting, 'Listening… press your extra button now' while it listens, a green tick and the key name once caught. 'key list still loading — try again in a second' means the list of keys was not ready yet.
- Assigned to this button: one tag per key, or 'none yet — click a key above'.

## Good to know

- Keys are saved in Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/OgreMCPBinds.json and set up on every character on this PC. They work even with the MCP closed.
- A key is tied to the button itself, not to where it sits. Move the button, or move its page, and the key still presses it. Clearing the button, or deleting its page, removes its keys. Pasting over a button keeps its keys, so they now press what you pasted.
- A key fires the button as it is saved right now, so editing the button changes what the key does - no need to assign it again.
- Keys from the window fire when pressed. A key that fires on release can only be made with the command `ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:AddBind[<key>,<button id>,<name>,release]`; such keys show ⭜ on their tag.
- `ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:ListBinds` lists every saved key, `ISXOgreEQ2.MCP:Buttons` lists every button with the id to use in AddBind (such as `btn:bmfk2x1a0` - not the button's name). An id like `static:0_0` or `page:2:0_1` still works; it names a slot and is switched to that slot's button the next time the MCP saves.

### Waiting for a key, and a key caught

![Listening](../assets/binds/listening.png)

![Caught G600-G12](../assets/binds/caught.png)

### Filtering the list

![Filter g600](../assets/binds/filter.png)
