# Ogre Options

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Settings for Ogre itself, shared by every character on this PC. Open it with `ogre config`.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Account** - your Ogre login. Saving it while logged out tries to log in again.
> - **Ogre** - the size of every window (UI scale); whether windows slide down, hide or stay where they are when the InnerSpace console covers them (the default - a window's right-click menu can give it its own); navmesh downloads (all zones, only the zones you go to, or none); and the **Session watch**: the uplink announces a session that freezes, recovers or disappears, and fires an event for uplink scripts (off by default).
> - **Theme** - pick a colour scheme, or change any colour. Changes show at once.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Nothing is kept until you press **Save**, which saves every tab. Closing undoes unsaved theme colours.
> - The UI scale, the InnerSpace console choice and the Session watch take effect when you press Save.
> - `ogre config` while this window is open does nothing - what you typed stays.
> - A window you scaled yourself (right-click its title bar) ignores the UI scale until you pick Scale: use default.

**Open it:** Type `ogre config` (or `ogre options` / `ogre info`) in the InnerSpace console. If it is already open, that does nothing - what you typed in it stays. It also opens by itself on the Account tab when your Ogre login is missing or wrong.

## What it is for

Ogre Options holds the settings that belong to Ogre itself rather than to one character's bot: your Ogre account login, how big every window is drawn, what happens when the InnerSpace console opens over a window, the colour theme, how navmeshes are downloaded, and whether the uplink watches for frozen sessions. Everything here is shared by every session on this PC. Nothing is kept until you press Save (the Theme tab also has its own Save theme button).

## Tabs

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Account / Ogre / Theme** | Switches the page. Save saves every tab at once, not just the one you are looking at. | Account |

## Account tab

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Username** | Your Ogre account name - the login OgreBot checks when it loads.<br>*Saving a blank box does not erase the saved name.* | empty on a first install |
| **Password** | Your Ogre account password. If you are not logged in when you press Save, Ogre tries to log in again straight away ('Saved - logging in...'). If you are already logged in, a new password is used the next time the bot loads.<br>*Saving a blank box does not erase the saved password.* | empty on a first install |
| **Show password** | Shows the password as text instead of dots so you can check it.<br>*Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.* | off |

## Ogre tab

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **UI scale — default for every window (right-click a window to override one)** | How big every Ogre window is drawn: 0.75, 0.9, 1 (100%), 1.1, 1.25 or 1.5. Applies to all windows as soon as you press Save. A window you scaled yourself (right-click its title bar, Scale + / Scale −) keeps its own size until you pick Scale: use default on it.<br>*The list opens inside the window and pushes the setting below it down, so every size is in view.* | 1 (100%) |
| **When the InnerSpace console covers a window** | What happens to an Ogre window that the InnerSpace console covers when you open it. Slide it below the console, then put it back: it moves down out of the way and returns when the console closes. Hide it until the console closes. Leave it where it is: nothing moves.<br>*Like the UI scale, it takes effect when you press Save. This is the default for every window: a window can have its own, from its title bar's right-click menu, under When Console is open (Slide below, Hide or Leave in place; Use default goes back to this one).* | Slide it below the console, then put it back |
| **Navmesh downloads** | Navmeshes are the zone maps the bot uses to walk and fly. **All zones, in the background**: every zone's mesh downloads while you play, the zone you are in first. **Only the zones I go to**: a zone's mesh downloads when you enter it or a route heads there. **Off**: nothing downloads, and nav tells you when a zone has no mesh.<br>*Takes effect as soon as you press Save. It is the same setting as `ogre patch mesh all\|ondemand\|off`.* | All zones, in the background |
| **Announce sessions that freeze, recover or disappear** | Every session tells the uplink it is alive every 5 seconds. With this on, the uplink announces a session that goes silent (30 seconds, 90 while loading), comes back, or closes for any reason, and fires OgreEvent_SessionFrozen, OgreEvent_SessionRecovered and OgreEvent_SessionGone for scripts running in the uplink.<br>*Saved for the whole PC; Save also tells the uplink at once. `ogre sessions on\|off` turns it on or off until the uplink restarts.* | off |

## Theme tab - presets

The colours of every Ogre window. Changes show at once on every open window; they are kept only when you save.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Start from: Toxic, Ogre, Ogre Bold, Forest, Swamp, Stone, Steel Blue, Amethyst, Crimson, Amber, Nightshade, Venom** | Paints every window in that ready-made colour scheme. Any colour you change below is changed on top of the scheme you started from. The lit button is the scheme you are on; none is lit once you have changed a colour. | Toxic |

## Theme tab - colours

Each row is one colour used across all windows. Click the square to open Hue / Saturation / Lightness sliders under that row, or type a colour code (like #3f7f2b) in the box on the right.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Title bar** | The bar at the top of every window. |
| **Inset (lists, logs)** | Sunken areas such as lists, logs and the console's input box. |
| **Window body** | The main background of every window. |
| **Cards / headers** | Boxes and header strips inside a window. |
| **Inputs / rows** | Text boxes, dropdowns and list rows. |
| **Selected row** | The highlight on the row you picked in a list. |
| **Dividers** | Faint lines between sections. |
| **Borders** | Outlines around boxes and inputs. |
| **Text** | Normal text. |
| **Bright text** | Stand-out text, and the text on buttons. A light colour here gives the text on buttons and tabs a thin black outline so it stays readable. |
| **Dim text** | Labels and hints. |
| **Faint text** | The least important text, such as 'nothing here' messages. |
| **Primary button** | The main button in a window, such as Save. |
| **Button** | All other buttons. |
| **Grid buttons (MCP, For Who)** | The button grids in the Master Control Panel and the For Who picker. |
| **Focus / hover ring** | The outline on the box you are typing in or hovering over. |
| **Titles / links** | Window titles, links and the selected tab. |
| **Headings** | Section headings inside windows. |
| **Good** | Good news, such as 'Saved.' |
| **Warning** | Warnings, such as 'unsaved changes'. |
| **Bad** | Errors and problems. |
| **Colour square (opens H / S / L sliders)** | Opens sliders for that colour right under its row; the colour changes as you drag. Click the square again to close them. |
| **Colour code box (e.g. #1f9a2a)** | Type a colour code (#rgb or #rrggbb). It applies as soon as it is valid; an invalid code turns the box's border red. |

## Theme tab - saving

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Save theme** | Keeps the colours you see now. The main Save button at the bottom saves them too.<br>*Other sessions on this PC pick up the new theme the next time their windows reload.* |
| **Undo changes** | Goes back to the last saved theme. |
| **saved / unsaved changes** | Tells you whether what you see has been saved. |

## Save and Close

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Save** | Saves every tab: your login, UI scale, the console setting, navmesh downloads, and the theme if you changed it. The UI scale and console setting apply right away. The text beside it shows 'Saving…', then 'Saved.', 'Saved - logging in...' or 'Save FAILED'. |
| **Close** | Closes the window without saving. Unsaved theme changes are undone. |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Same as Close. |

## What the window shows

- Every option here is for the whole PC, not one character. They live in OgreSave\Common\OgreOptions.json (UI scale), OgreSave\Common\OgreConsole.json (the console setting), OgreSave\Common\UIState.json (the theme) and OgreSave\patcher.json (navmesh downloads). The login is kept separately in OgreSavePrivate\Common\ISXOgre.json.
- The text to the right of Close is the result of your last Save.

## Good to know

- Nothing is kept until you press Save. Closing the window throws away unsaved changes, including theme colours you were trying out.
- Save saves all four tabs at once.
- A window you scaled yourself ignores the UI scale here. Right-click its title bar and pick Scale: use default to make it follow again.
- The InnerSpace console setting is about the InnerSpace console (the one you type `ogre` commands in), not OgreConsole.
- A new password is only used right away if you were not logged in. Otherwise it takes effect the next time the bot loads.

## Ogre tab

![Ogre tab](../assets/options/ogre.png)

## Theme tab

![Theme tab](../assets/options/theme.png)

# Reset UI Windows

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Puts Ogre windows back where they started. Use it when a window is off-screen and you cannot reach its title bar. Open it with `ogre windowreset`.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Reset** on a row moves that window back to its starting spot and size, at the normal UI scale, unlocked.
> - **Reset All Windows** does that for every window in the list, except help windows and the OgreHUD.
> - **Refresh** re-reads the list after you open or close windows.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Reset forgets the window's saved position. Move it where you want and use Save Position again.
> - A hidden window stays hidden; Reset only moves it.
> - Each window's own title-bar right-click menu also has Reset.

**Open it:** Type `ogre windowreset` in the InnerSpace console. It opens in the middle of the screen. If it is already open, that does nothing.

## What it is for

Lists every Ogre window that is open in this session and puts any of them back where it started. Use it when a window has ended up off-screen (for example after switching monitors or changing resolution) and you cannot reach its title bar to drag it back. Reset puts a window back at its starting position and size, returns it to the UI scale set in Ogre Options, unlocks it, and forgets any position you saved for it.

## Header

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **↻ Refresh** | Reads the list of open windows again. The list is taken when this window opens and does not update by itself. |

## The window list

One row per open window (this one is left out).

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Reset** | Moves that window back to where it first opened, at its starting size and at the UI scale set in Ogre Options, unlocks it, and makes sure its title bar is on the current screen. Any position you saved for it with Save Position is forgotten.<br>*A hidden window stays hidden - Reset only moves it.* |

## Reset everything

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Reset All Windows** | Does a Reset on every window in the list at once, hidden ones included. Help windows and the OgreHUD are listed but left where they are; use their own Reset button.<br>*No confirmation. Every saved position is forgotten.* |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes this window. Nothing else changes. |

## What the window shows

- Each row: the window's title, then its position (x, y), size (width × height, 'auto' when it sizes itself) and its scale if it is not 1.
- OFF-SCREEN (red): the window is open but its title bar is outside the screen.
- HIDDEN (grey): the window exists but is hidden, for example the OgreBot main window after a plain `ogre`.
- LOCKED: the window was locked from its title-bar right-click menu. Reset unlocks it.
- 'No other windows are open.' when there is nothing to reset.

## Good to know

- Every window also has a Reset on its own title-bar right-click menu. This window is for the ones you cannot reach.
- Reset forgets a window's saved position, so it opens at its default spot next time too. Drag it where you want it and use Save Position again.
- Only windows that are open right now are listed. A closed window is not affected.
- The list does not update by itself; press Refresh after opening or closing windows.

## After a Reset

The off-screen SmartLoot window is back at its starting spot and the OFF-SCREEN badge is gone.

![After Reset](../assets/windowreset/after-reset.png)

## Nothing else open

![Empty list](../assets/windowreset/empty.png)

# Instance Controller

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Runs zones for your group, one after another: travels in, fights through the zone, and moves on to the next.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Queue zones**: pick a zone on the left and double-click it (or Add). **Add all** queues every zone the list is showing (this folder, after the search and the variant filter), in its order. Drag rows to reorder.
> - **Sort** (beside the Zones heading): the zones are listed by their number by default (**Sort: #**); click it for **Sort: A-Z**, by zone name. It is remembered, and Add all follows it.
> - **Remove** and **Clear** sit beside the Queue heading. Remove takes out the highlighted row (click a row first; right-clicking the highlighted row does the same), Clear empties the queue. Each is greyed out until there is something for it to do.
> - **Stop after this zone** (shown while a list runs): the zone you are in finishes, then the list stops and the end-of-list actions run (call to the guild hall or home, camp). Run clears it.
> - **Run** starts the list. **Pause** holds the Instance Controller only (OgreBot keeps running). **End** stops the run. While the end-of-list actions run (guild hall, home, camp), End cancels them: nothing more starts, and the client is not closed.
> - **Options** decide what happens in and after each zone: loop the list, reset zones first, call home at the end, and more.
> - **Summon merc if solo** (on by default): once you are inside the zone with nobody else in your group, it summons your mercenary (`merc resume`). On a zone-in that happens as you land, so the mercenary gets the rebuff time too.
> - **Every option is also a command**: `ogre ic -skipshinies` turns one on, `ogre ic -skipshinies=off` turns it off, and one command can carry several. `ogre ic options` lists them all.
> - **Zone file**: IC File Option 1-3 and IC File Args are for the zone you run. The zone file names the options and reads them.
> - **Startup Options** are commands sent at the start of every zone, then undone when the run ends.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Closing this window stops a running list, the same as End.
> - If a zone fails, the group stays in that zone and the list stops.
> - Every zone file must say how it leaves the zone. Reload skips a file that does not, and the log says what to add.
> - While IC travels the group to a zone, OgreBot is paused, so buffs that drop at each zone line are not recast out in the world. A toon that gets attacked on the way is resumed to fight, then paused again. On arrival everyone is resumed and has a few seconds to rebuff before the zone starts.
> - Settings (including Max wait per zone) and the queue are saved, and shared by every character on this PC.

**Open it:** Type `ogre ic` (or `ogre ic panel`) in the console. It opens at 775x460. If the window is already open, the command does nothing.

## What it is for

The Instance Controller (IC) runs a list of instanced zones for you, one after another. You browse the zone files, queue the zones you want (each stamped with a variant such as [Heroic]), then press Run. For each row IC travels the group to the zone (resetting it first if asked), applies your Startup Options, walks the zone file's steps (paths, nameds, chests, shinies) and zones out, then moves to the next row. When the list is done it can call the group home, camp out, or loop back to the top.

## Title bar and tabs

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **▼ / ▲** | Shrinks the window to a one-line strip showing the run status, Pause and Expand. Clicking again restores the previous size. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*The strip is 440 pixels wide and only as tall as its content.* | expanded |
| **Close (X)** | Closing the window STOPS a running list, exactly like End (the reason shown is 'panel closed'), and turns IC's pause off.<br>*Closing is not just hiding the window. It does NOT cancel end-of-list actions that are already running (use End for that), so closing the window on the way out never undoes an armed camp.* |  |
| **Run / Startup Options / Settings** | Switches the page you see. Display only. | Run |

## Shrunk to a strip

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Pause / Resume** | Same as the Pause button at the bottom. Turns IC's own pause on or off. OgreBot's pause is not touched.<br>*Only visible when shrunk.* |
| **Expand** | Restores the full window. |

## Run tab - choosing zones

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Root dropdown (e.g. "test (4)")** | Picks which of the three content roots to browse: default, test or custom. Each shows how many files it has. Picking one goes to that root's top folder and clears the selected file. The choice is saved.<br>*Browse choice only. The roots have no priority order.* | default; on first ever open it auto-jumps to the first root that has files |
| **Up** | Goes up one folder in the browse list and clears the selected file.<br>*Disabled at a root's top level.* |  |
| **search** | Filters the browse list to files whose zone name or path contains the text. Not case-sensitive. It applies about 0.2 seconds after you stop typing.<br>*Not saved, so it clears when the extension reloads.* | empty |
| **any variant / [Solo] / [Heroic] / ...** | Two jobs. (1) Hides files that do not have this variant. (2) Every zone you queue is tagged with this variant, which decides which instance the zone-in travels to. 'any variant (browse only)' turns the filter off and tags nothing. The choices are every variant found in the loaded zone files. Saved.<br>*With 'any', queuing a file that has 2+ variants pops up a pick-one menu at the row.* | any variant |
| **Reload** | Re-reads every zone file from the three roots. Prints 'N zone(s) from M file(s) - X skipped, Y warning(s)'. The selected file is cleared if it no longer exists. A zone file that does not say how it leaves the zone is skipped, and the log names the file and the line to add (see Write your own zone files).<br>*A queued row whose file vanished fails with 'press Reload' when the row starts.* |  |

## Run tab - the zone list

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Sort: # / Sort: A-Z** | Flips the order of the Zones list: by the files' number (Sort: #, the default) or by zone name (Sort: A-Z). The button names the order shown. Add all queues in the same order. Saved. | Sort: # |
| **Folder row (name + file count)** | Single click opens that folder. |  |
| **Zone row (click)** | Selects the file. The add bar then shows its name, and its difficulty menu if it has one.<br>*Zone files marked as disabled are hidden.* |  |
| **Zone row (double-click)** | Adds the zone to the end of the queue, tagged with the chosen variant and the remembered difficulty. With no variant chosen: a file with 0 or 1 variants is added directly; a file with 2 or more opens a pick-one popup at the row. The pick is checked against the zone file; a pick it does not allow is refused, and the error lists the allowed values. The new row becomes the highlighted one.<br>*The popup pick is one-off. It does not change the variant filter.* |  |

## Run tab - the queue

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Queue row (click)** | Highlights the row. This is the target for Remove and for right-click remove. It does NOT choose where Run starts. |
| **Drag a row** | Press a row and drag it up or down to reorder the queue - anywhere on the row; the drag starts once the mouse moves a few pixels, so a click is never taken for a drag. It is a move, not a swap: rows in between shift one place. The moved row becomes highlighted. Saved.<br>*It works even while a list is running.* |
| **Right-click a row** | Removes the row, but only if it is already the highlighted one. A right-click on any other row does nothing (it is only noted in the log).<br>*The highlight is the confirmation step.* |
| **Remove** | Removes the highlighted queue row (right-clicking the highlighted row does the same). Saved.<br>*Greyed out until a row is highlighted - click one first. Not blocked while a list runs.* |
| **Clear** | Empties the whole queue, with no confirmation. Saved.<br>*Greyed out while the queue is empty. Not blocked while a list runs.* |

## Run tab - adding to the queue

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Difficulty ('choose…' until set)** | A difficulty that stays chosen while you browse. It is added to rows queued from files that have a difficulty menu, and checked against that file when you add. The bot does NOT use it during a run yet: when the row starts, IC only logs 'the difficulty on this row is recorded but not acted on yet'.<br>*Only shown when the selected file has a difficulty menu (a list of choices). Saved.* | empty |
| **Difficulty number box (e.g. '1-80')** | Same as the Difficulty dropdown, for files that use a number range. It takes effect when you press Enter or click away. Also recorded only, not used yet.<br>*Only shown when the selected file uses a range. The range is checked when you add, not while you type.* | empty |
| **Add** | Queues the selected file exactly like a double-click, including the variant popup.<br>*Disabled until a file is selected.* |  |
| **Add all** | Queues every zone the Zones list is showing (this folder, after the search and the variant filter), in the list's order, each tagged with the variant chosen up top and the remembered difficulty. With no variant chosen, a file with 2 or more variants is left out. One console line says how many were added and why any were left out (already queued, needs a variant, refused).<br>*Greyed out when the list shows no zone files (folders are not zones). A zone already in the queue is not added again.* |  |

## Run tab - options

When the window is too short for every option, the option grid scrolls (the lists and the footer stay on screen). The picture here is the grid as it opens; the next section's picture is the same grid scrolled down. Every tick-box is also a console switch, and `ogre ic options` lists them all.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Loop list** | After the last row finishes, the list starts again at row 1. It is read again before each next row, so unticking it during a list ends the list at its last row. When a whole pass only skipped zones (every zone on the list locked), the list waits until the first lockout ends instead of going round again at once. It is turned OFF automatically when a safety check stops the list: fewer than 10 free inventory slots, the group shrank, or a member is dead.<br>*A zone never starts again inside the instance it just finished. If a zone's exit did not take the group out, the list stops and says why; Stop and Run starts it where you stand. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -loop` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Ogre IM** | Between zones, at most once every 30 minutes, runs the Inventory Manager (`ogre im -destroy -tse`) and the list waits for it. In a guild hall it also uses the depot and sells (`-depot -sell`), then the group repairs. The first one is due 30 minutes after the list starts. One that comes due while you are flying or dead is skipped until the next 30 minutes.<br>*Only after a zone that ran (not one that was skipped), and not when Stop after this zone ends the list. If the IM is still going after 30 minutes, the list goes on without it. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -im` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Summon Mender bot to sell** | With Ogre IM, outside a guild hall: the IM also sells to a mender bot (`-sell`). A mender bot already within 10 m is used; otherwise, when a Mechanized Platinum Repository of Reconstruction is in your bags and ready, IC uses it to summon one. The bot is targeted so the sell picks it. The sell waits (up to a minute) for the automatic repair at the bot to end, because that repair closes the bot's window.<br>*No item, item not ready, or no bot 15 seconds after the summon: the IM runs without the sell, and the log says why. Does nothing in a guild hall (it has its own merchant) or with Ogre IM off. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -summonMenderToSell` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Zone in first** | When a row starts and you are not standing in its zone, the travel system takes the whole group there (the queued variant picks the instance), and the file starts on arrival. The group's bots are paused for the trip, so buffs that drop at each zone line are not recast out in the world. On arrival IC waits for the group (up to 2 minutes, then it names who is missing and goes on), resumes everyone and gives 8 seconds to rebuff before the file starts. If there is no route, IC warns and runs where you stand. Off = always runs where you stand.<br>*Zoning in always runs the file from the top; a named # or Resume point is dropped. Zone-in gives up after 20 minutes. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -zoneIn` (`=off` turns it off).* | ON |
| **Summon merc if solo** | Once inside the zone, when nobody else is in your group (your mercenary not out either), IC summons your mercenary (`merc resume`). On a zone-in it happens as the group lands, so the mercenary gets the rebuff time too; when you start already standing in the zone, it happens as the run starts.<br>*A character with no mercenary hired just gets the game's own one-line answer. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -summonMercIfSolo` (`=off` turns it off).* | ON |
| **Reset zones first** | Only during a zone-in. It first checks the lockout table (read again from the Zone Reuse window if the bot's copy is more than 15 minutes old; if it cannot be read within 30 seconds, the zone-in goes ahead without the check). Locked and not resettable: the zone is SKIPPED and the list moves on. Otherwise it runs 'oc !c -ResetZone igw:<you> <zone>' so every member resets, then travels. Off = lockouts are not checked; the group goes into the instance it is locked to.<br>*A locked zone that cannot be reset is skipped, not failed. This option never spends a Force reset charge. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -resetZones` (`=off` turns it off).* | ON |
| **Skip dead/missing checks** | The list does NOT stop when someone has left the group or a member is dead - checked when Run starts and before each next row. The free inventory slots check (at least 10) still stops it.<br>*Without it, either one stops the list, turns Loop list off and runs the end-of-list actions. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -skipGroupChecks` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Halt at end of zone** | When a zone's steps finish cleanly, IC pauses itself inside the zone, before the exit and zone-out steps. OgreBot keeps running. The Pause button becomes Resume; pressing it runs the zone-out and the list continues. If the group leaves the zone while held, the zone counts as done and IC stays paused until Resume.<br>*A zone file's own zone-out step can do the hold instead. That way also sends an OgreConsole message and speaks '<name> IC' aloud (text-to-speech). Not applied to a failed zone. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -haltAtEnd` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Call to GH after each zone** | When a zone's steps are done (after any Halt at end of zone), the group is called to the guild hall INSTEAD of zoning out: the group's bots are paused, you run GetToGH and the rest of the group is sent the same, and the bots are resumed when everyone has landed. Nothing of the zone file's exit runs; the next zone starts from the guild hall. A call that fails, or takes more than 180 seconds, ends the zone all the same (a carry-on failure, like a failed exit).<br>*When it is on, Stay until a zone is ready is not used. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -callGHAfterEachZone` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Stay until a zone is ready** | When a zone's steps are done, before the zone-out, the group waits INSIDE the zone until a zone still on the list can be run: not locked, or resettable. The zone you are in counts too: it is zoned out of, reset and run again. The lockout table is read once; when nothing is ready, it is read again when the first lockout among those zones ends. Untick it to let the group go.<br>*Not used when Call to GH after each zone is on, or when Stop after this zone is ticked (there is no next zone to wait for). Also a console switch: `ogre ic -stayInZoneUntilZoneReady` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **After a lost zone: Call to guild hall / Call to home / nothing** | When a zone is given up because all its wipe-recovery tries are used: everyone is revived first (up to 60 seconds), then this runs. 'Call to guild hall' = go to the guild hall (GetToGH), up to 180 seconds. 'Call to home' = cast Call to Home, up to 90 seconds. 'nothing' = revive only. The list then moves on to the next row.<br>*A zone file with its own after-wipe list replaces this completely. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -afterWipe=callgh` (or `callhome`, `none`).* | Call to guild hall (callgh) |
| **Skip the boss** | A named that the zone file marks as the boss is not fought. It ends as 'skipped - Do NOT Kill Boss is on'.<br>*Only affects nameds the zone file marks as the boss. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -skipBoss` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Skip shinies** | No shiny is looted at all: every shinies step of the zone file ends at once as 'skipped - the Skip shinies option is on'.<br>*Wins over whatever the zone file says about no-trade shinies. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -skipShinies` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Pause for no-trade shinies** | In a shinies step, a shiny whose loot window holds a no-trade item is NOT looted: its window is left open for you and IC pauses itself (the group keeps playing), with a console message and a '<name> shiny' text-to-speech. Take the item, then press Resume; the step goes on to the next shiny. Loot everything is turned off for the group while the step runs, so the auto-loot leaves the item too.<br>*A zone file that sets its own no-trade rule on the step overrides this option. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -pauseForNoTradeShinies` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Do not loot no-trade boss chest** | When the step for a named the zone file marks as the boss begins (before the kill), your Leader Only loot is set to take tradable items and Smart Loot only (not loot everything, no distribution, not in combat); your loot options are put back after the loot step. A Leader Only loot window that still holds a no-trade item is left open for you, with a console message and a '<name> boss chest' text-to-speech, and IC waits until it is gone.<br>*Free For All windows are not touched - each character's own loot options take them. Non-boss chests loot no-trade items as usual unless the zone file says otherwise. The zone file's own no-trade rule overrides this. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -doNotLootNoTradeBossChest` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |

## Run tab - more options (scroll down)

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Call to guild hall** | When the list ends, pauses the group's bots and runs the go-to-guild-hall command (GetToGH) for you. It also sends 'oc !ci -GetToGH igwbn:<you>' so the rest of the group does the same. Waits up to 180 seconds, then moves on.<br>*Ticking it unticks Call to home (only one can be on). Runs only when the list completes or a safety check stops it: NOT after a failed zone, NOT after End, NOT when a row could not start. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -callGH` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Call to home** | When the list ends, pauses the group's bots and casts Call to Home for you and the group through a console command. Done when a zone change is seen, or after 90 seconds.<br>*Either/or with Call to guild hall. Same end-of-list triggers. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -callHome` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Camp out** | After any call to the guild hall or home, camps the whole group: the rest of the group is sent a camp-to-desktop first, then this character camps to the login screen. Each client closes once its character has left the world. If this character's camp is still busy after 120 seconds, or the character is still in the world afterwards, the camp counts as failed.<br>*Same end-of-list triggers as Call to guild hall. The others' camp is their own, with its own retry. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -campAtEnd` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Exit even if the camp fails** | Only with Camp out on. If this character's camp failed, runs 'exit' and closes the client with the character still in the world, with a loud warning in the log. The rest of the group is also sent an exit with a 90-second countdown along with its camp, so a client whose camp failed is closed too (one whose camp worked is gone by then).<br>*Does nothing without Camp out. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -exitIfCampFails` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **IC File Option 1 / 2 / 3** | Three tick-boxes for the zone file you run: the zone file decides what each one means and reads it (`ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileOption[n]` in a script, `{{ic.options.fileOption1}}` in the file). Each box shows the name the zone file gives it (its `fileOptions`, or what its running script set with `ISXOgreEQ2.IC:SetFileOptionLabel`), else 'IC File Option 1', 2 or 3. Saved.<br>*The names follow the zone that is running, else the file selected in the Zones list. A zone file that does not use them ignores them. Also console switches: `ogre ic -fileOption1` (2, 3; `=off` turns one off).* | off |
| **IC File Args** | Text for the zone file to read (`ISXOgreEQ2.IC.FileArgs` in a script, `{{ic.options.fileArgs}}` in the file). It is sent and saved when you press Enter or leave the box, not on every key.<br>*Also a console switch: `ogre ic -fileArgs=<text>`.* | empty |

## Run tab - bottom row

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **named #** | Type which named you are on (1, 2, 3...) and press Enter, or just press Run. Only works for the queue row whose zone you are standing in: that row's next run starts at that named's lead-in (its walk and pre-fight steps). The row shows 'start at step N (named X)'. Used once. 1 or blank = from the top. If you are not in a queued zone, it is ignored with a warning.<br>*The box empties once it is used. A file with no such named is refused.* | blank |
| **Stop after this zone** | Shown only while a list runs. The zone you are in finishes as always (its steps, then Halt at end of zone or Call to GH after each zone), then the list stops as if that were its last row - no Ogre IM, no loop wait, no next zone, no Stay until a zone is ready - and the end-of-list actions run. Untick it to carry on.<br>*Run clears it, and so does the list stopping. Not saved. A failed zone still stops the list without the end-of-list actions. Also a console switch: `ogre ic -stopAfterZone` (`=off` turns it off).* | off |
| **Pause / Resume** | Turns IC's own pause on or off. While paused, IC does nothing: no zone steps advance, the zone-in stops, and the list waits. Actions already started keep going. OgreBot's pause is NOT touched. Also releases a Halt at end of zone hold.<br>*The window keeps updating while IC is paused (for example when OgreBot is paused or resumed). Run also clears the pause.* | running |
| **Resume** | Only shown when you stand in a queued zone whose last run was stopped mid-zone. That row restarts at the step where it stopped, then Run fires.<br>*The stop point is not saved to disk.* | hidden |
| **Run** | Starts the list. It starts at the queue row for the zone you are standing in, otherwise row 1, never the highlighted row. It clears IC's pause, checks the row's choices against the zone file again, and runs the safety checks (at least 10 free slots, nobody dead). Each row then runs in turn: zone-in, apply startup options, zone steps, exit.<br>*Greyed out while running, while the end-of-list actions of the last list are still going (press End to cancel them first), with an empty queue, or if OgreBot is not loaded with a profile. Refuses right after a zone-in while the bot is still learning what is around it. A failed zone stops the list and IC stays in the zone.* |  |
| **End** | Stops the run where it stands and clears IC's pause. The current step is cancelled, exit steps do NOT run, and the list stops. The stop step is remembered for Resume, and the startup options are reverted. During a zone-in, IC's travel route is stopped and the group stays put. End-of-list actions are not triggered. For a zone run by a LavishScript (.iss) file, IC stops following it but the script itself keeps running. While the end-of-list actions are running, End cancels them: nothing that has not started yet runs (no camp, no exit), and an unfinished camp is stopped so the client is not closed. A trip to the guild hall or a Call to Home already under way finishes on its own, and the group stays paused - resume OgreBot when you are ready. The console says what was left behind.<br>*Greyed out only when nothing is running and no end-of-list action is running. If the game had already begun the /camp countdown, the camp can still take the character to the login screen; the client stays open.* |  |

## Startup Options tab

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Add defaults** | Appends the 17 shipped default rows to your list. Existing rows are kept, so pressing twice gives duplicates.<br>*The very first time (before any IC settings are saved) the list starts with the defaults.* |  |
| **Reset to defaults** | Replaces your whole list with the shipped defaults. The 'Reload profile when the run ends' checkbox is left as is.<br>*No confirmation.* |  |
| **Clear** | Empties the startup list. It stays empty; the defaults are not added back.<br>*No confirmation.* |  |
| **Startup row (click)** | Highlights the row. Display only; you need it before a right-click remove. |  |
| **Checkbox** | Enables or disables the row without deleting it. A disabled row is struck through and never runs. | enabled |
| **S / D / G** | Turns on or off whether the row runs when solo, duo or grouped. Players are counted and mercenaries are not: 1 = solo, 2 = duo, 3+ = group. The mode you are in right now is ringed. You cannot turn off the last lit letter (a warning is shown). | S, D and G all on for a new row |
| **Drag a row** | Press a row (not its tick box or S/D/G chips) and drag it up or down to reorder; the drag starts once the mouse moves a few pixels. It is a move, not a swap. Order matters because rows run top to bottom. |  |
| **Right-click a row** | Deletes the row, but only if it is the highlighted one.<br>*Here the window itself does the check; for the queue the bot does it.* |  |
| **a console command, e.g. oc !ci -ChangeOgreBotUIOption igw:${Me.Name} checkbox_settings_loot TRUE** | The command for a new row. It is run exactly as written, as a console command, at the start of every zone.<br>*${Me.Name} is expanded when the row runs.* | empty |
| **label (optional)** | An optional display name for the new row. If blank, the command itself is shown. | empty |
| **Add** | Adds the typed command as a new row: enabled, runs in solo, duo and group. Refused if the command is blank.<br>*Clears both boxes after adding.* |  |
| **Reload profile when the run ends (start fresh)** | This is how startup options are undone. When a zone run ends for any reason (completed, failed, stopped, skipped) and startup rows were applied, IC reloads your OgreBot profile. If you were not solo, it also sends 'oc !ci -LoadProfile igwbn:<you> Use_UI' so every member reloads its own profile. This also throws away any change you made by hand mid-run.<br>*Skipped if the list is empty or the run ended before the rows went out.* | ON |

## Settings tab

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Max wait per zone (seconds) + Set** | A safety limit. A zone still running this many seconds after it started is stopped where it stands. 0 = no limit. Applies to normal zone files and to zones run by a LavishScript (.iss) file.<br>*Saved with the other IC settings (panel.json), so it survives a reload. Time IC spends paused or halted, and time spent staying in a finished zone, does not count toward it.* | 3600 (60 minutes) |
| **Refresh** | Marks the bot's copy of the lockout table as out of date. It does NOT read it now: the table is re-read from the Zone Reuse window the next time a zone-in needs it.<br>*The status shows 'stale' until then.* |  |

## What the window shows

- Root dropdown: the root name plus its file count, e.g. "test (4)".
- Breadcrumb: <root> or <root> / <folder>.
- Zones list header: "Zones (shown of total loaded)".
- Zones list folder rows: ▸ name, then the number of files under it.
- Zones list file rows: the zone name (or path) plus chips - one per variant (e.g. [Solo], [Heroic]) or "no variants"; a difficulty chip (a range "1-80" or choices "normal/expert"); ".iss" when the file hands the run to a LavishScript file. Hover shows the zone name and root/path.
- Zones list empty messages tell apart: "no zone files loaded", "this root is empty - try test (4)", "nothing in this folder matches", "nothing matches the filter".
- Queue header: "Queue (n)".
- Queue rows: label (zone name + variant), and grey sub-text - "diff X" when a difficulty is set; "start at step N (named 3)" when a start point is set; otherwise "stopped at step N (stepId)" when there is a Resume point. While a list runs, a ▶ marks the row it is on.
- Add-bar text: "Double-click a zone to queue it", or "<zone> as [Heroic]", or "<zone> — double-click to choose a variant".
- Status line (the first that applies is shown): 1. orange "HELD inside the zone" - zone - press Resume to zone out; 2. orange "Instance Controller is PAUSED"; 3. while running: bold state (zoning in / launching / running), the zone or zone-in destination and current travel hop, "list r/t (loop)", the phase (enter / steps / wipe / exit) with "(wipe recovery w of max[, given up])", "/ stepId", and a note; 4. orange "END OF LIST - <call to guild hall | call to home | camp | exit> in progress"; 5. "completed <zone> - note", orange "completed with failures <zone> - N step(s) did not do their job" (for example a named never spawned), or red "failed <zone> - note"; 6. red "OgreBot is not loaded - IC drives its verbs, so it needs a profile open"; 7. otherwise "N zone(s) loaded". A skipped zone shows as "completed" with the skip reason.
- Shrunk strip: a shorter version of the same status, e.g. "IC idle - N zone(s)".
- Startup Options rows: checkbox, label, grey monospace command, and S/D/G chips (lit = runs in that mode, ringed = your current mode).
- Startup Options status: "E of T enabled · K would run now (solo|duo|group)".
- Settings - Lock table: green "fresh - N row(s)" (read in the last 15 minutes and not marked out of date), or orange "stale", plus "a refresh is armed" while a re-read is waiting.
- Settings - Content roots: default = Scripts/Ogre/EQ2/IC/default, test = Scripts/Ogre/EQ2/IC/test, custom = Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/IC/custom.
- Settings - Pause: Instance Controller and OgreBot, each "running" or orange "PAUSED".

## Good to know

- Closing the IC window ends the running list, exactly like pressing End. It does not just hide the window.
- Run starts at the queue row for the zone you are standing in, otherwise at row 1. The highlighted row does not decide where Run starts.
- Pausing IC does not pause OgreBot, and pausing OgreBot does not stop IC. A paused OgreBot with IC running is the normal way to move through a zone.
- The Difficulty setting is saved on the row but a run does not use it yet.
- When the window is short, the options scroll: scroll them down for At end of list and Zone file.
- A failed zone stops the list and leaves the group in that zone so it can be looked at. No end-of-list action (guild hall, home, camp) runs.
- A zone lost to a wipe is different: everyone is revived, the After a lost zone choice runs, and the list moves on.
- End-of-list actions run only when the list completes or a safety check stops it (fewer than 10 free bag slots, someone left the group, or someone is dead). Never after End.
- End cancels the end-of-list actions while they run. Anything not yet started never runs and an unfinished camp is stopped (the client is not closed); a trip to the guild hall or a Call to Home already under way finishes on its own. Closing the window does not cancel them.
- Camp out camps the whole group, not just the IC character.
- Zoning in always runs the zone file from the top. A named # or Resume point only applies when you are already standing in that zone.
- Reload profile when the run ends (on by default) reloads the profile of every group member at the end of each zone. It also throws away any change you made by hand during the run.
- The search text is not saved.
- All IC settings (including Max wait per zone), the queue and the startup list live in one file, Scripts/OgreSave/EQ2/IC/panel.json, shared by every character on the PC. Each session loads it once and overwrites it on every change.
- Refresh (Zone lockouts) does not read the lockout table straight away. It is re-read the next time a zone-in needs it.
- Add defaults appends the shipped rows again, so pressing it twice gives duplicates. Reset to defaults and both Clear buttons ask no confirmation.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/windows/zonereset.md

# Zone Reset

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Shows your zone lockout timers and resets them, for this character or for your group or fleet.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Refresh** - read the zone list and timers from the game again.
> - **Click a zone** on the left to queue it; click it on the right to remove it. The **Add** buttons queue many at once.
> - **Show** - tick Solo, Heroic, Raid or Other to choose which zones the list shows. **Sort** - by Status (resettable first), Type (solo, heroic, raid) or Name. These only change the view: the **Add** buttons still look at every zone.
> - **Reset queue for me** - reset every queued zone on this character.
> - **Reset queue via ... for ...** - send the reset to the characters in the Master Control Panel's For Who window.
> - **Force reset** - ctrl-click a queued zone, then press it twice: the first press only arms it, a second press within 5 seconds does the reset.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - Green can be reset, orange is locked (time left in brackets), yellow has no data.
> - **Force reset spends a limited reset charge** and cannot be undone. It only confirms if the game's message names that zone.

**Open it:** Type `ogre zone` (also `ogre reset` or `ogre zonereset`). If the window is already open, this does nothing.

## What it is for

Zone Reset shows your zone lockout timers and resets them for you. It reads the game's Zone Reuse window and lists every zone, coloured by whether it can be reset now, is still locked, or has no data. You pick the zones you want in a reset queue, then reset them on this character, or send the reset to your group or fleet. A separate Force reset button spends one of your limited reset charges on one zone. It needs two clicks, and has a safety check.

## Header and colours

The status text on the right says what the last action did (for example 'scraped 7 zone(s) + 3 with no timer'). 'working…' appears next to the title while it is busy. The colour key explains the zone list: green can be reset, orange is locked with the time left shown in brackets, pale yellow has no data.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Refresh** | Reads the zone list and timers again. It briefly opens the game's Zone Reuse window, reads it, and closes it.<br>*Opening this window with no list yet does a Refresh for you. Nothing happens when you are not in the world.* |

## Full zone list

Every zone the game has a lockout record for: resettable first, then locked, then no data. Zones with 'Raid' in the name carry a small 'raid' tag. Hover a row to see the game's own tooltip for it.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Click a zone** | Adds that zone to the reset queue on the right. A zone already in the queue is not added twice. |
| **Add resettable** | Adds every green (resettable) zone to the queue. |
| **Add non-raid** | Adds every resettable zone that does not have 'Raid' in its name. |
| **Add non-locked** | Adds every zone that is not locked: the resettable ones and the ones with no data. |

## Reset queue

The zones you picked. The queue is kept while the bot is loaded, even if you close this window, but is not saved to disk.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Click a queued zone** | Removes it from the queue. |  |
| **Ctrl-click (or Alt-click) a queued zone** | Selects that zone as the Force reset target (it is highlighted). Ctrl-click it again to unselect. Display only until you press Force reset. |  |
| **Clear list** | Empties the reset queue. |  |
| **Force reset selected / Force reset: <zone> / Click again to SPEND a charge on: <zone>** | Spends one of your limited zone reset charges to reset the selected zone right now, even if it is locked. It takes two clicks: the first click only arms the button (its text changes to 'Click again to SPEND a charge on: <zone>'), and a second click within 5 seconds does the reset. The bot then opens the Zone Reuse window, finds the zone, clicks Force Reset, and only clicks the confirm button if the game's confirm message names exactly that zone. If it does not, nothing is clicked, no charge is spent, and the confirm window is left open for you.<br>*Cannot be undone. If you do not click again within 5 seconds, the button goes back to normal and nothing is spent.* | greyed out until a zone is selected (and while the window is busy) |
| **Reset queue for me** | Resets the lockout timer of every queued zone on this character only, one zone every half second.<br>*Greyed out while the window is busy. With an empty queue it just says the queue is empty.* |  |
| **Reset queue via <oc/irc> for <who>** | Sends a reset for every queued zone to the characters picked in the Master Control Panel's For Who window, over the bot console (or IRC if that is what the For Who window says). Each character that receives it resets its own timer for those zones. The button text shows where it will go.<br>*If the For Who window has never been set, this goes to every character (all).* | oc for all (when the For Who window has never been set) |

## Footer

A reminder of how the lists work, and that Force reset spends a limited charge.

## What the window shows

- Green zone: its lockout can be reset now (the game's tooltip says so).
- Orange zone with [time]: locked; the time in brackets is how long is left.
- Pale yellow zone: no timer data (the game knows the zone but shows no timer for it).
- 'raid' tag: the zone name contains 'Raid'. The Add non-raid button skips these.
- Status text (top right): what the last action did, for example 'reset 3 queued zone(s)', 'the reset queue is empty', 'not in world', or 'ABORTED: ...' when the Force reset safety check refused.
- 'working…': a refresh or reset is running. The reset buttons are greyed out until it finishes.

## Good to know

- Force reset spends a real, limited reset charge and cannot be undone. The first click only arms it; the reset happens on a second click within 5 seconds. The ordinary 'Reset queue' buttons do not spend charges.
- The fleet button uses the For Who window from the Master Control Panel, not your group. If that window was never set, it resets for every character.
- Refresh and Force reset briefly open the game's Zone Reuse window. That can cause a short stutter. A queue reset opens it too, but only on a character whose game has not loaded its zone list yet.
- The queue is forgotten when the bot is unloaded.

### Choosing a Force reset target

Ctrl-click a zone in the queue:

![Force reset target](../assets/zonereset/force.png)

### While it works

![Busy](../assets/zonereset/busy.png)

### Before the first read

![Empty](../assets/zonereset/empty.png)

# OSA

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> The On Screen Assistant: the NPCs around you with health, your threat, distance and who they are attacking. Named first, then nearest first - up to 35 rows, and every named in range comes before any other NPC.
>
> **What you can do here**
>
> - **Click a row** to target that NPC. The green row is the one you are fighting.
> - **Gear** - choose the columns (HP, Threat, Distance, Target), then **Apply**.
> - Set how far it looks, "targets only" and Clip Y Axis in OgreBot, HUDs tab, OSA section.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - It opens and closes with **Use On Screen Assistant (OSA)** on OgreBot's Settings tab; `ogre osa` also opens it (and does nothing if it is already open).
> - THR is your threat in percent; at 100 it shows your lead over the next player.
> - Clip Y Axis hides NPCs 8 or more above or below you - the floors over and under you.

**Open it:** Tick **Use On Screen Assistant (OSA)** on OgreBot's Settings tab - it opens at once, opens every time that profile loads, and closes when you untick it. You can also type `ogre osa`.

## What it is for

A compact list of the NPCs around you: name, health, your threat, distance, and who each one is attacking. Named mobs are listed first, then the rest nearest first. Click a row to target that NPC. How far it looks, whether it hides NPCs that are not fighting and whether it hides NPCs on other floors are set in OgreBot, on the HUDs tab (OSA section).

## Title bar

The title shows how many NPCs are listed, for example OSA — 9 NPCs.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **⚙ (gear)** | Opens and closes the column picker at the top of the window. |
| **Title bar close (X)** | Closes the window. The OgreBot box stays ticked; type `ogre osa` to bring it back.<br>*To turn OSA off for good, untick the box in OgreBot.* |

## The list

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Click a row** | Targets that NPC. |

## Column picker

Opened with the gear. Name is always shown.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **HP%** | Shows the HP column: the NPC's health in percent. | on |
| **Threat** | Shows the THR column: your threat on that NPC in percent. When you are at the top of its hate list (100), it shows how far ahead of the next player you are instead. | on |
| **Distance** | Shows the DIST column: how far away the NPC is, in metres. | on |
| **Target** | Shows the TARGET column: the name of whoever that NPC is targeting. Empty means it is not targeting anyone. | on |
| **Apply** | Uses the ticked columns, closes the picker, and remembers the choice for next time.<br>*Ticking a box does nothing until you press Apply.* |  |

## What the window shows

- Rows: NPCs and named NPCs only - no players, pets, corpses or objects. Named first, then everyone else, each group nearest first. At most 35 rows - every named in range is listed before any other NPC, so a far-away named is never the one cut.
- Green row with bold green name: the NPC you are fighting - your target, or your target's target if you have a friend targeted.
- HP: health in percent. THR: your threat in percent, or your lead over the next player once you are at 100. DIST: distance in metres. TARGET: who that NPC is targeting.
- 'no NPCs in range' when nothing is inside the scan radius.
- It refreshes 5 times a second.

## Good to know

- Scan Radius, Display NPCs with Targets Only and Clip Y Axis (OgreBot, HUDs tab) only apply while the Use On Screen Assistant box is ticked. If you open OSA with `ogre osa` and the box is not ticked, it looks 50 metres out and lists every NPC on every floor.
- Scan Radius is capped at 200 metres.
- Clip Y Axis (only show mobs on the same floor as you), in the same OgreBot section, hides every NPC whose height differs from yours by 8 or more.
- `ogre osa` when OSA is already open does nothing and prints nothing.

## Empty

![No NPCs in range](../assets/osa/empty.png)

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Kannkor/ISXOgre/main/docs/EQ2/bot/windows/npccast.md

# NPC Cast Monitoring

> **:bulb: In game - the ? button on this window says**
>
> Two tabs. **Monitor** writes down every spell a mob casts, with its name and spell number. **Watch list** watches the mobs listed for your current zone, and when one starts a listed spell, the bot can interrupt it or run your commands.
>
> **Monitor**
>
> - **Start** / **Stop** - turns the log on and off. It keeps running while you fight, zone or die, until you press Stop.
> - **my target + its target** - logs your target and your target's target. These are the only spells that come with a **name**, because the name is read off your cast bars. Target the mob, or target the tank the mob is attacking.
> - **+ named NPCs nearby** / **+ every NPC nearby** - also logs other casters within 100 metres. Their spells show a spell number but no name, unless you have seen that spell on your cast bar before.
> - **Copy** - puts the whole list on your clipboard, ready to paste.
> - **Clear** - empties the list for this zone.
> - Each zone has its own list, saved to the file named under it. Send that file, or paste the copied list, to whoever asked for it.
>
> **Watch list**
>
> - **Add the spell my target is casting** - press it while your target's cast bar is up.
> - **Add by hand** - type a mob name and a spell number.
> - **interrupt** - the bot interrupts that spell with an interrupt you have ready.
> - **label** / **commands** - opens a small editor under the spell. Type, then **Save** or **Cancel**.
> - **remove** / **remove mob** - stop watching a spell or a whole mob here.
>
> **Good to know**
>
> - The Watch list only works when **NPC Cast Monitoring** is ticked on OgreBot's Settings tab. While it is off, a red bar tells you when a button cannot do anything. Interrupts and commands also need OgreBot open and not paused. The Monitor needs none of that.
> - **Scan radius** takes 5 to 500. Leave it empty to use the default.
> - Your changes go in your own list, so updates never remove them. **Reset my edits** deletes them all for this zone, with no undo.

**Open it:** Type `ogre npccast` (also `ogre npccastmonitoring`, `ogre npccast panel` or `ogre npccast config`). If the window is already open, this does nothing. `ogre npccast status` prints the watch status in the console instead.

## What it is for

This window has two tabs. **Monitor** writes down every spell a mob casts, with the spell's name and its ability id, so you can copy the list or send the file to whoever asked for it. It only records; it never makes the bot do anything. **Watch list** watches the mobs listed for the zone you are in, found by their exact name. When a watched mob starts casting one of the listed spells, the bot can interrupt it, run your own commands, or both. Each zone has a shipped list that comes with the bot, and your own list on top of it. Everything you change on the Watch list goes into your own list, so a bot update never removes it. The window opens on the Monitor tab.

## Header and tabs

The top line shows the zone and a count. On the Monitor tab the count is how many spells are in the log. On the Watch list tab it is how many mobs and spells are listed and how many mobs are being watched right now.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Monitor** | Shows the Monitor tab: the log of what mobs cast. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*The window always opens on this tab.* | shown |
| **Watch list** | Shows the Watch list tab: the mobs and spells watched in this zone, and what the bot does about them. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does. |  |

## Monitor: what to log, Start and Stop

Pick whose spells to log, then press Start. One of the three buttons is always lit. Your target and your target's target are logged in every choice.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **my target + its target** | Logs the spells of your target and of your target's target. Players are left out. These are the only spells that come with a name, because the name is read off your cast bars. Target the mob, or target the tank the mob is attacking.<br>*Your choice is not saved. After you restart the game it is back to this one.* | on |
| **+ named NPCs nearby** | Also logs every named NPC within 100 meters of you. Their spells show the ability id but no name, unless that spell was once named from your cast bars.<br>*Changing this while the Monitor runs takes effect at once.* | off |
| **+ every NPC nearby** | Also logs every NPC within 100 meters of you, named or not. Their spells show the ability id but no name, unless that spell was once named from your cast bars. | off |
| **Start / Stop** | Start begins logging and the button turns into a red Stop. It checks four times a second and keeps going while you fight, zone or die, until you press Stop. Stop saves the log and stops; the list stays on screen.<br>*Closing the window does not stop it. It also runs while OgreBot is closed or paused, and with NPC Cast Monitoring unticked.* |  |

## Monitor: the log

One row per mob and spell, in the order they were first seen. A grey bar above the log says what your last button press did. With either of the 'nearby' choices, a second grey bar explains why some spells have no name.

## Monitor: Copy, Clear and the file

Under the log: whether the Monitor is running ('monitoring') or 'stopped', the two buttons, and the file the log is saved to.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Copy** | Puts the whole log on your clipboard as text, ready to paste: a line with the zone name, a line naming the columns, then one line per row (mob \| spell \| ability id \| cast time \| seen). The grey bar says how many lines were copied.<br>*Greyed out while the log is empty.* |
| **Clear** | Empties the log for this zone, and its saved file too. Spell names already learned are kept.<br>*No confirmation and no undo. Greyed out while the log is empty.* |

## Watch list tab

The Watch list always shows the zone you are in right now. Everything below is on this tab.

## Watch list: header

On this tab the zone name is the name of the zone's list file. The counts on the right say how many mobs and spells are listed and how many mobs are being watched right now.

## Watch list: adding spells

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Add the spell my target is casting** | Target a mob while its cast bar is up and press this. The mob's name and the spell it is casting are added to your list for this zone. The result shows in a green (worked) or red (did not work) bar under the buttons.<br>*The spell is added with no label and no action, so nothing happens yet. Tick interrupt or add commands afterwards.* |  |
| **mob name (box)** | The name of the mob to add, exactly as the game shows it. Capital letters do not matter.<br>*This box is not cleared after adding (the number and label boxes are), so you can add several spells for the same mob.* | empty |
| **ability id (box)** | The spell's number (its ability id). Anything that is not a digit is removed. Cleared after adding. | empty |
| **label (optional) (box)** | A name you give the spell so you know what it is. Only shown in this window. Cleared after adding. | empty |
| **Add by hand** | Adds the typed mob and spell number to your list for this zone. Nothing happens if the mob name or the number is empty.<br>*If that mob already has that spell in your list, nothing changes (the label is not updated).* |  |

## Watch list: zone settings and files

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Scan radius (box)** | How far away (in meters) mobs are watched in this zone. The grey number is the value in use when the box is empty. | empty (50) |
| **Set** | Saves the scan radius into your list for this zone. It must be from 5 to 500. An empty box or 0 removes your value, so the shipped value (or 50) is used again.<br>*A number outside 5-500 is refused: a red bar says so and nothing is saved. Check the footer's 'scanning to' number for the value in use.* |  |
| **scan players instead of NPCs** | When ticked, this zone watches players instead of NPCs. Saved into your list for this zone at once.<br>*Only useful for testing in a guild hall with other players casting.* | off |
| **Reload** | Reads the lists for the zone you are in again from disk. Use it after you edit a list file by hand. |  |
| **Import Classic custom** | Copies the converted custom lists from OgreBot Classic into your own list folder. A zone you already have your own list for is skipped, never overwritten. The console says how many files were copied and skipped.<br>*This works even when NPC Cast Monitoring is turned off.* |  |
| **Reset my edits** | Deletes your own list for this zone, so only the shipped list is left. Everything you added, removed or changed in this zone is gone, including the scan radius and the players setting.<br>*There is no confirmation and no undo.* |  |

## Watch list: messages

Bars under the buttons tell you what happened. Green or red is the result of your last capture or edit: when something you pressed could not be done (monitoring is off, no zone is loaded, a scan radius out of range, a list file that cannot be read or written), a red bar says why. Other red bars are problems with a list file. Grey bars are notes.

## Watch list: the list

One block per mob. Under each mob is one row per spell. A yellow 'yours' tag means the mob or spell comes from your own list. 'radius N' is a distance set just for that mob. 'watch only' means the mob has no spells listed. A long list of commands is cut short on its row; hold the mouse over it to read all of it.

| Control | What it does | Default |
|---|---|---|
| **Mob name / arrow** | Click to fold a mob's spells away or show them again. Display only - changes what you see, not what the bot does.<br>*Folds are forgotten when the window is reopened.* | open |
| **remove mob** | Stops watching this mob in this zone. A mob from your own list is deleted from it. A mob from the shipped list is switched off in your list, so it stays off after updates.<br>*No confirmation. To get a shipped mob back, use Reset my edits (which undoes all your edits in this zone).* |  |
| **interrupt** | When ticked and this mob starts casting this spell, the bot targets that mob and casts an interrupt spell that is ready right now. Saved at once.<br>*Nothing is cast if you have no interrupt ready, or while OgreBot is closed or paused.* | as the list says |
| **label** | Opens a small editor right under this spell's row, with a box holding its current name. Type a new name and press Save. Cancel closes the editor without saving.<br>*Saving an empty box removes the name you gave it. A spell from the shipped list then shows its shipped name again.* |  |
| **commands** | Opens a small editor right under this spell's row, with the commands the bot runs each time this mob starts this spell, one per line. The row shows how many commands are set and what they are.<br>*Commands only run while OgreBot is open and not paused.* |  |

## Watch list: editing a label or commands

Pressing label or commands opens this editor under the spell's row.

| Control | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Editor box** | The name or the command lines you are editing. What you type is kept while the list refreshes. Only one editor is open at a time; opening another one drops what you had not saved.<br>*Pressing Enter does not save. Use the Save button.* |
| **Save** | Saves the editor's text into your own list for this zone and closes the editor. For commands, empty lines are skipped, and saving an empty box removes your commands; a spell from the shipped list then uses its shipped commands again. |
| **Cancel** | Closes the editor. Nothing is saved. |
| **remove** | Removes this spell from the mob. A spell from your own list is deleted. A shipped spell is switched off in your list.<br>*Removing the last spell of a mob you added removes that mob too. A mob from the shipped list stays watched.* |

## Watch list: footer

Shows how far the bot scans and for what (NPCs or players), and where the shipped list and your own list for this zone are stored on disk.

## What the window shows

- Monitor header: the zone the log belongs to - the same name the Watch list tab shows - and 'N spell(s) logged', the number of rows in the log.
- Monitor log columns: Mob, Spell (its name, or a grey '(no name yet)'), Ability ID, Cast time (seconds, from the latest cast) and Seen (how many times that mob cast it). One cast counts once, even though the Monitor sees it several times while the cast bar is up. Casting the same spell again counts again.
- Monitor grey bars: the result of your last Start, Stop, Copy or Clear. With either 'nearby' choice, a second bar says that casts from mobs that are not your target (or your target's target) only get an ability id.
- Monitor footer: 'monitoring' in green while it runs, 'stopped' when it does not, and 'saved to' the log file for this zone.
- Zone name (both tabs): the file name used for the zone, for example Castle_Vacrul_Caverns_of_the_Forsaken_Heroic_II. '(no zone)' when nothing is loaded.
- 'N mob(s) · N ability entr(ies) · watching N': how many mobs and spells are listed, and how many mobs the scan is watching right now.
- Green bar: your last capture worked (or that spell was already in your list). Red bar: your last capture or edit did not work, with the reason (no target, not casting, monitoring off, radius out of range, and so on).
- Red 'OFF' bar: NPC Cast Monitoring is turned off on OgreBot's Settings tab. The list is empty and nothing is watched.
- Grey 'OgreBot is closed' bar: mobs are still watched, but nothing is interrupted and no commands run until OgreBot is open.
- Grey 'Per-cast logging is off' bar: shows until you tick NPCCastDebug on OgreBot's Debug tab.
- Red file bars: the shipped list or your list for this zone cannot be read, your file uses the old 'nomerge' spelling, or some spell numbers in it are not valid and were skipped.
- Grey 'REPLACES' bar: your file is set to replace the shipped list instead of adding to it.
- Mob tags: 'yours' = from your list, 'radius N' = a distance set just for that mob, 'watch only' = no spells listed.
- Spell rows: the spell number, its label ('(no label)' if none), the interrupt box, how many commands it runs, and a 'yours' tag when it comes from your list.
- Watch list footer: 'scanning to N for NPCs/players' is the widest distance in use (the zone radius or the biggest per-mob radius). 'shipped:' and 'yours:' are the two list files for this zone.

## Good to know

- The Monitor and the Watch list are separate. The Monitor only writes down what mobs cast; it never interrupts or runs anything, and it needs neither the NPC Cast Monitoring checkbox nor OgreBot open.
- Spell names in the Monitor only come from your cast bars (your target and your target's target), and only when the cast lasts longer than about a quarter of a second. Once a spell's name is known, it shows for that spell everywhere, in every zone and next time too.
- Each zone keeps its own Monitor log. Zone while it runs and the old zone's log is saved and the new zone's saved log comes back. Send the file named under the log, or paste what Copy gives you.
- The Monitor keeps running after you close the window. Press Stop (or type `ogre npccast monitor off`) to end it. The console can also start it: `ogre npccast monitor`, `ogre npccast monitor named` or `ogre npccast monitor all`.
- The Watch list is switched by the 'NPC Cast Monitoring' checkbox on OgreBot's 'Settings' tab. While it is off, the list is empty and capturing, reloading, adding, removing and editing are refused with a red bar saying so. Only Import still works.
- Entering a zone that has a list (shipped or yours) ticks that checkbox for you, once per zone. If you untick it, it stays off until you next enter a zone that has a list, or your profile is loaded again.
- A watched mob starting a spell that is not listed (or a 'watch only' mob) does not interrupt or run anything. It only lets encounter scripts know the mob is casting.
- Interrupts and commands only happen while OgreBot is open and not paused.
- Reset my edits deletes all your Watch list edits for this zone at once, with no confirmation.
- The Watch list only covers the zone you are standing in. To edit another zone's list, go there or edit its file.
- With NPC Cast Monitoring off, an empty Watch list says so and asks you to turn it on - adding needs it on.

### The Monitor with named NPCs nearby

With **+ named NPCs nearby** picked, a second grey bar explains the missing names. The named NPC at the bottom was never on your cast bars, so its spells have no name yet:

![Monitor with named NPCs nearby](../assets/npccast/mon-named.png)

### The Monitor before you start

Nothing logged yet, so Copy and Clear are greyed out:

![Monitor before Start](../assets/npccast/mon-empty.png)

### Watch list: a mob folded away

The first mob is folded shut. The last mob has no spells listed, so it is 'watch only':

![A folded mob](../assets/npccast/folded.png)

### Watch list: no list yet, and switched off

A zone with nothing listed, after a capture that failed (the target was not casting), with OgreBot closed and debug logging off:

![Empty zone](../assets/npccast/empty.png)

With the NPC Cast Monitoring checkbox turned off in OgreBot:

![Monitoring off](../assets/npccast/off.png)
